title: Standardize agent output summary title to "Agentic Conversation"
body:
Agent conversation output in GitHub Actions step summaries currently displays parser-specific titles (`🤖 Copilot CLI Session`, `🤖 Claude CLI Session`, etc.). This changes the HTML details element to use a consistent title across all AI engines.

## Changes

- **`actions/setup/js/log_parser_shared.cjs`**: Modified `wrapAgentLogInSection()` to return static title `"Agentic Conversation"` instead of `${emoji} ${parserName} CLI Session`
- **`actions/setup/js/log_parser_bootstrap.cjs`**: Added wrapping for Copilot's special `conversation.md` path (generated by `--share` flag) to ensure consistent output across all code paths
- **Test updates**: Updated 7 test expectations across `log_parser_shared.test.cjs` and `log_parser_bootstrap.test.cjs`

**Before:**
```html
<details open>
<summary>🤖 Copilot CLI Session</summary>
...
</details>
```

**After:**
```html
<details open>
<summary>Agentic Conversation</summary>
...
</details>
```

The `parserName` parameter remains accepted for backward compatibility but no longer affects the output title. Both regular log file parsing and Copilot's `conversation.md` special path now produce consistent wrapped output.

title: .NET: Fix case-sensitive property mismatch in CosmosChatHistoryProvider queries
body:
### Motivation and Context

SQL queries in `CosmosChatHistoryProvider` used `c.Type` (uppercase) while the document model defines `[JsonProperty("type")]` (lowercase). Cosmos DB's case-sensitive queries failed to match any documents, causing `GetMessageCountAsync()` and `ClearMessagesAsync()` to always return 0.

### Description

**Changed queries:**
- `GetMessageCountAsync()` - line 555: `c.Type` → `c.type`
- `ClearMessagesAsync()` - line 585: `c.Type` → `c.type`

**Added tests:**
- `GetMessageCountAsync_WithMessages_ShouldReturnCorrectCountAsync`
- `GetMessageCountAsync_WithNoMessages_ShouldReturnZeroAsync`
- `ClearMessagesAsync_WithMessages_ShouldDeleteAndReturnCountAsync`
- `ClearMessagesAsync_WithNoMessages_ShouldReturnZeroAsync`

**Test updates:**
- Fixed IDE0090 style violations by using target-typed new expressions (`new(...)` instead of `new ChatMessage(...)`)
- Updated tests to work with current API: constructor now uses state factory pattern, methods require `AgentSession` parameter

Tests follow existing patterns (skip when Cosmos DB Emulator unavailable).

### Contribution Checklist

- [x] The code builds clean without any errors or warnings
- [x] The PR follows the [Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] All unit tests pass, and I have added new tests where possible
- [ ] **Is this a breaking change?** If yes, add "[BREAKING]" prefix to the title of the PR.

> <issue_description>### Description
> 
> **What happened?** 
> When using CosmosChatMessageStore, calls to GetMessageCountAsync() and ClearMessagesAsync() always return 0, even when there are messages present in the container that can be retrieved via other methods.
> 
> **What did you expect to happen?** 
> GetMessageCountAsync() should return the actual number of messages for the given conversation, and ClearMessagesAsync() should delete the messages and return the count of removed items.
> 
> **Steps to reproduce the issue:**
> 1. Initialize CosmosChatMessageStore with a valid connection string and container.
> 2. Add messages to the store (or verify they exist).
> 3. Call GetMessageCountAsync().
> 4. Observe that it returns 0 regardless of the actual data.
> 
> ### Code Sample
> 
> ```markdown
> var cosmosProvider = new CosmosChatMessageStore(
>     "AccountEndpoint=xxxx;AccountKey=xxxx",
>     "my-databaseid",
>     "my-container",
>     "my-conversationId");
> 
> // Retrieval works fine
> var messages = await cosmosProvider.InvokingAsync(new ChatMessageStore.InvokingContext([]));
> 
> // Bug: Always returns 0
> var count = await cosmosProvider.GetMessageCountAsync();
> 
> // Bug: No messages are deleted and returns 0
> var removedMessagesCount1 = await cosmosProvider.ClearMessagesAsync();
> ```
> 
> ### Error Messages / Stack Traces
> 
> ```markdown
> No exception is thrown; the methods silently fail to match any documents due to an incorrect property name in the underlying Cosmos DB SQL query.
> ```
> 
> ### Package Versions
> 
> Microsoft.Agents.AI.CosmosNoSql: 1.0.0-preview.260121.1
> 
> ### .NET Version
> 
> NET 10
> 
> ### Additional Context
> 
> The issue appears to be caused by a case-sensitivity mismatch in the query string.
> In `CosmosChatMessageStore.cs`, the query uses `c.Type = @type` instead of `c.type = @type` (lowercase 't').
> 
> * **Current NuGet source:** [Line 555 in CosmosChatMessageStore.cs](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/blob/b4a71f00a3a8b3a5690a499a5b48669e4728ca43/dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.CosmosNoSql/CosmosChatMessageStore.cs#L555)
> * **Main branch (Migrated to `CosmosChatHistoryProvider`):** The bug seems to persist in the new implementation here: [Line 555 in CosmosChatHistoryProvider.cs](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/blob/407fb3025e694751650de1252a9097e3ce8dff6f/dotnet/src/Microsoft.Agents.AI.CosmosNoSql/CosmosChatHistoryProvider.cs#L555)

title: Fix Docker blank page when accessing via IP, add iframe support and HTTPS upgrade control
body:
Docker container served blank pages when accessed via `http://host-ip:3000`, while `http://localhost:3000` worked. Browser error: "Origin-Agent-Cluster header prevented origin-keying since origin had previously been placed in a site-keyed agent cluster."

## Root Cause

The issue had two parts:
1. **Origin-Agent-Cluster header** - Caused browser isolation between localhost and IP origins
2. **upgrade-insecure-requests CSP directive** - Caused SSL protocol errors by upgrading HTTP requests to HTTPS on HTTP-only servers

## Changes

**Disabled problematic Helmet.js headers** in `src/server.ts`:
- `crossOriginEmbedderPolicy: false`
- `crossOriginOpenerPolicy: false`  
- `crossOriginResourcePolicy: false`
- `originAgentCluster: false`
- `upgradeInsecureRequests: enableUpgradeInsecure ? [] : null` in CSP (controlled by env var)
- `frameguard: enableXFrameOptions ? { action: 'sameorigin' } : false` (controlled by env var, disabled by default)

These headers enforce strict origin isolation designed for advanced security scenarios. They break HTTP-only deployments where users switch between accessing via localhost and IP addresses, as browsers isolate the origins and refuse to render. The `upgrade-insecure-requests` directive was causing browsers to request JavaScript bundles over HTTPS on an HTTP-only server, resulting in `ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR`.

**New Environment Variables:**
- `UPGRADE_INSECURE_REQUESTS` - Set to `true` to enable CSP upgrade-insecure-requests directive
  - **Only use when deployed behind an HTTPS reverse proxy** (nginx, Traefik, etc.) with valid SSL certificates
  - Defaults to `false` for HTTP-only deployments
  - When enabled, all HTTP requests are automatically upgraded to HTTPS
- `X_FRAME_OPTIONS` - Set to `true` to enable X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN header
  - Defaults to `false` to allow iframe embedding
  - When enabled, prevents clickjacking but disables iframe embedding

**iframe Support:**
- X-Frame-Options header disabled by default to allow iframe embedding
- Can be re-enabled with `X_FRAME_OPTIONS=true` for clickjacking protection

```typescript
const enableUpgradeInsecure = process.env.UPGRADE_INSECURE_REQUESTS === 'true'
const enableXFrameOptions = process.env.X_FRAME_OPTIONS === 'true'

app.use(
  helmet({
    contentSecurityPolicy: {
      directives: {
        // ...
        upgradeInsecureRequests: enableUpgradeInsecure ? [] : null, // Only enable when behind HTTPS reverse proxy
      },
    },
    hsts: isProduction ? { /* ... */ } : false,
    frameguard: enableXFrameOptions ? { action: 'sameorigin' } : false, // Disabled by default to allow iframe embedding
    crossOriginEmbedderPolicy: false,
    crossOriginOpenerPolicy: false,
    crossOriginResourcePolicy: false,
    originAgentCluster: false,
  })
)
```

Core security headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy) remain active.

## Documentation

Updated `DOCKER.md` with:
- `UPGRADE_INSECURE_REQUESTS` environment variable documentation
- `X_FRAME_OPTIONS` environment variable documentation
- Security warnings about HTTPS-only usage and iframe embedding implications

## Verification

Tested with real browser (no security bypasses):
- ✅ Both `localhost:3000` and `host-ip:3000` load correctly with login dialog visible
- ✅ No Origin-Agent-Cluster or cross-origin isolation headers in response
- ✅ No `upgrade-insecure-requests` in CSP by default
- ✅ `upgrade-insecure-requests` only present when `UPGRADE_INSECURE_REQUESTS=true`
- ✅ No SSL protocol errors with default configuration
- ✅ No network failures
- ✅ No `X-Frame-Options` header by default - iframe embedding allowed
- ✅ `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` present when `X_FRAME_OPTIONS=true`
- ✅ Security headers still present

- IP address: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9bdf915-d42d-4cd0-bfc4-fa4d0c5f0ee5

This PR fixes a critical issue where the Docker browser mode served blank pages when accessed via IP address (e.g., `http://10.10.20.64:3000`) while working fine with `http://localhost:3000`. The root cause was strict cross-origin security headers from Helmet.js that isolated different origins and the CSP `upgrade-insecure-requests` directive that broke HTTP-only deployments.

- Disabled problematic Helmet.js security headers (Origin-Agent-Cluster, COEP, COOP, CORP) that caused origin isolation issues
- Made X-Frame-Options header optional (disabled by default) to support iframe embedding, configurable via `X_FRAME_OPTIONS` environment variable
- Made CSP `upgrade-insecure-requests` directive optional (disabled by default) for HTTP deployments, configurable via `UPGRADE_INSECURE_REQUESTS` environment variable
- Updated DOCKER.md with documentation for the new environment variables and security warnings

<issue_title>CI DoctorVCluster System Test Failure - GHCR Blob Access Denied (Run #5910)</issue_title>
<issue_description>## Summary

VCluster system test failed with a transient GHCR blob access denial when pulling the `ghcr.io/loft-sh/kubernetes:v1.32.3-full` image during cluster creation. This caused 1 job to fail and 4 related VCluster tests to be cancelled.

## Failure Details

- **Run**: [22547690953](https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail/actions/runs/22547690953)
- **Run Number**: devantler-tech/ksail#5910
- **Commit**: `e7abde0a852e336cb587e9a8ac03d3c9a46fc223`
- **Trigger**: `merge_group` (PR devantler-tech/ksail#2624 — Daily Perf Improver: Add YAML marshaller benchmarks)
- **Failed Job**: `🧪 System Test (VCluster, Docker, false, --gitops-engine ArgoCD --local-registry ghcr.io/devantler-tech/ksail/system-test-manifests)`

## Root Cause Analysis

The VCluster provisioner attempted to pull `ghcr.io/loft-sh/kubernetes:v1.32.3-full` (the `-full` suffix is appended internally by the vCluster SDK/Helm chart for the base Kubernetes image). During blob download, the GHCR registry returned a **`denied: denied`** error for one of the image layers:

````
17:05:34 info Pulling image ghcr.io/loft-sh/kubernetes:v1.32.3-full to /tmp/vcluster-docker-kubernetes-3416664745...
✗ failed to execute cluster lifecycle: failed to create cluster: failed to create vCluster: pull image: failed to copy image:
  Copying blob sha256:5411c0def11e1efcd6c475c0d0a38b288a1b53d03e7ce036a4a9d264835e0f27
  Copying blob sha256:e44be4e76f256f1d22748ec43dc2b672896074030c0642cf6ef41988d2896063
  Copying blob sha256:c9bd7f2f3c61bb1faa6657a3b772a298b10174ffa1144c47571fe8e8baa83e9b
  - copying system image from manifest list: reading blob sha256:28b6ecf90724962d30befe5736ef9b175f915cef2311457db3863730eacf91d8: fetching blob: denied: denied
```

This is a **transient infrastructure failure** — the GHCR registry rejected a blob download mid-pull. The code changes in this PR (YAML benchmarks) are entirely unrelated to VCluster or image pulling.

## Failed and Cancelled Jobs

| Job | Status |
|-----|--------|
| VCluster, Docker, ArgoCD + local-registry ghcr.io | ❌ failure |
| VCluster, Docker, --name system-test-cluster --cni Cilium | ⛔ cancelled |
| VCluster, Docker, Flux + local-registry ghcr.io | ⛔ cancelled |
| VCluster, Docker, Calico --csi Disabled --load-balancer | ⛔ cancelled |
| VCluster, Docker, ArgoCD (second) | ⛔ cancelled |

The cancellations are cascading: GitHub Actions cancelled dependent/concurrent VCluster jobs after the first failed.

## Investigation Findings

1. **Mirror cache was present**: The ghcr.io mirror cache volumes were restored successfully (`✅ All 4 mirror cache volumes present`), but the vCluster provisioner pulls the Kubernetes base image directly (not through the mirror) via the Vind/vCluster SDK.
2. **Not a code regression**: The triggering commit only adds YAML benchmark tests — no VCluster, registry, or image-pull logic was modified.
3. **Image tag mismatch (informational)**: `pkg/fsutil/configmanager/vcluster/Dockerfile` specifies `ghcr.io/loft-sh/kubernetes:v1.32.3` (no `-full` suffix), but the vCluster SDK/Helm chart appends `-full` internally. This is expected behavior.
4. **No kubeconfig after failure**: Since cluster creation failed, `~/.kube/config` was absent, causing the `ksail cluster delete` cleanup step to also fail with `cluster name is required`.

## Recommended Actions

- [ ] **Re-run the failed workflow** — this is a transient registry error; no code changes needed.
- [ ] Consider adding retry logic in the VCluster provisioner for image pull failures with `denied: denied` errors (similar to the existing `createWithRetry` for exit status 22 in `pkg/svc/provisioner/cluster/vcluster/provisioner.go`).
- [ ] Investigate whether `ghcr.io/loft-sh/kubernetes` images can be pre-pulled into the ghcr.io mirror cache to avoid direct pulls during system tests.

## Prevention Strategies

1. **Pre-warm VCluster Kubernetes base image**: Add `ghcr.io/loft-sh/kubernetes:v1.32.3-full` to the mirror cache warm-up step in `.github/actions/ksail-system-test`. The current setup warms `docker.io`, `ghcr.io`, `quay.io`, and `registry.k8s.io`, but may not include this specific loft-sh image.
2. **Add pull retry for image-pull denials**: The existing `createWithRetry` (3 attempts, 5s delay) handles transient startup failures but not mid-pull registry errors. A separate retry wrapper at the pull stage could handle `denied: denied` errors.
3. **Improve cleanup resilience**: The `ksail cluster delete` step should not fail (or at least not cause a non-zero exit) when no cluster was created — consider adding `|| true` or a check for cluster existence before deletion in the system test action.

> @copilot+claude-opus-4.6 fix ALL golangci-lint and lychee issues

Fixed in `81231ac`:
- **golangci-lint golines**: Shortened `errRegistryDenied` test error string and wrapped across lines to fit the line length limit.

**Testing**
No behavioral changes — purely a public API tracking file update. Existing tests cover the APIs themselves.

None.

title: Add deprecation warning when disabling bottom navigation
body:
### Description

When users toggle off bottom navigation in settings, show a dialog warning them that side navigation is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

- **`strings.xml`**: Added `bottom_navigation_deprecation_warning` explaining: volunteer-maintained project, too much overhead to support both nav styles, side nav incompatible with Android gesture navigation (hence the default change), and advice to disable auto-updates if they depend on it.
- **`UserInterfacePreferencesFragment`**: Intercepts the `PREF_BOTTOM_NAVIGATION` toggle-off action to show a `MaterialAlertDialogBuilder` confirmation dialog before applying the change.

title: Improve test coverage for System.Formats.Tar APIs
body: ## Description This PR adds test coverage for three items from issue #68230: 1. **Executable permission preservation**: Tests that executable permissions survive archive creation and extraction across all tar formats (V7, Ustar, Pax, Gnu). The test properly accounts for umask when verifying permissions. 2. **Unsupported entry types**: Tests that TarReader can read archives containing unsupported entry types (MultiVolume, SparseFile, TapeVolume) without throwing exceptions. The test manually creates a valid GNU tar header with proper checksum calculation and documented header fields. 3. **Hidden file support**: Tests that files starting with '.' can be successfully added to tar archives and extracted. This test runs on all platforms since dot-prefixed filenames are valid everywhere. ## Changes Made - **Added `Archive_And_Extract_Executable_PreservesExecutableBit` test** to `TarEntry.ExtractToFile.Tests.Unix.cs`: - Tests all tar formats including V7 - Verifies executable bits are preserved through archive/extract roundtrip - Properly accounts for process umask in assertions - **Added `Read_Archive_With_Unsupported_EntryType` test** to `TarReader.GetNextEntry.Tests.cs`: - Manually constructs valid GNU tar headers for unsupported entry types - Includes comments explaining each header field (mode, uid, gid, size, mtime) - Uses correct checksum calculation per tar specification - **Added `Create_Entry_From_HiddenFile` test** to `TarWriter.WriteEntry.File.Tests.Unix.cs`: - Tests all tar formats (V7, Ustar, Pax, Gnu) - Runs on all platforms (not Unix-specific) - Validates that dot-prefixed filenames are preserved ## Technical Notes - Tests follow established patterns in the repository - Platform-specific tests use appropriate `ConditionalTheory` attributes where needed - Manual tar header construction in unsupported entry type test includes proper checksum calculation where the checksum field (bytes 148-155) is treated as 8 space characters during calculation - Executable permission test accounts for umask to avoid flaky test failures - Contributes to dotnet/runtime#68230 --- 💬 We'd love your input! "stephentoub", "body": "## 🤖 Copilot Code Review — PR #123989

### Holistic Assessment

**Motivation**: This PR adds test coverage for three items from the pending Tar API feedback issue #68230: executable bit preservation, reading unsupported entry types, and hidden file support. These are reasonable edge cases that warrant test coverage.

**Approach**: The tests follow established patterns in the test files and use appropriate conditional attributes for Unix-specific tests. The manual TAR header construction for the unsupported entry type test is acceptable for this specific scenario.

**Summary**: ⚠️ **Needs Human Review**. The core test logic appears correct, and multiple model reviewers validated the umask handling and checksum calculation. However, there are a few scope/consistency items to consider before merging.

---

### Detailed Findings

#### ✅ Correctness — Executable bit preservation test is properly implemented

The `Archive_And_Extract_Executable_PreservesExecutableBit` test correctly accounts for the process umask when verifying extracted file permissions. The assertion:

```csharp
UnixFileMode expectedExecutableBits = executableMode & ~UMask & executeBitsMask;
UnixFileMode actualExecutableBits = extractedMode & executeBitsMask;
Assert.Equal(expectedExecutableBits, actualExecutableBits);
```

This is correct because `TarEntry.ExtractToFile` uses `UnixCreateMode` which respects the process umask, and `UMask` is properly computed in `TarTestsBase` from the environment at test initialization (lines 219-221 of TarTestsBase.cs).

#### ✅ Correctness — Checksum calculation for unsupported entry type test

The manual header construction in `Read_Archive_With_Unsupported_EntryType` correctly:
1. Treats bytes 148-155 (checksum field) as spaces during checksum calculation
2. Formats the checksum in octal with proper padding and termination
3. Sets `TarEntryType.SparseFile` ('S') which triggers `NotSupportedException` in `TarHeader.Read.cs:437`

Verified that this exception is thrown from `TarHeader.Read.cs`:
```csharp
TarEntryType.SparseFile => throw new NotSupportedException(SR.Format(SR.TarEntryTypeNotSupported, header._typeFlag)),
```

#### ⚠️ Scope Gap — PR description mentions a test that isn't present

The PR description states:
> - WindowsPath_WithBackslashes_ConvertedToForwardSlashes → TarWriter.WriteEntry.File.Tests.cs

However, this test does not appear in the actual diff or in the test files. Either the test should be added to match the description, or the PR description should be updated to reflect what's actually included. One of the existing PR review comments also noted this discrepancy.

#### 💡 Suggestion — Consider adding V7 format to executable bit test

The `Archive_And_Extract_Executable_PreservesExecutableBit` test excludes `TarEntryFormat.V7`. While V7 has limitations, it does support the mode field for regular files and should theoretically preserve executable bits. Consider adding it for completeness, or add a comment explaining why V7 is excluded if there's a known limitation.

```csharp
[InlineData(TarEntryFormat.V7)]   // Consider adding
[InlineData(TarEntryFormat.Ustar)]
[InlineData(TarEntryFormat.Pax)]
[InlineData(TarEntryFormat.Gnu)]
```

#### 💡 Suggestion — Hidden file test location

The `Create_Entry_From_HiddenFile` test is placed in `Tests.Unix.cs` and conditioned on `IsNotWindows`. While dot-prefixed files are a Unix convention for hidden files, they are valid filenames on all platforms. If the goal is simply to test that `TarWriter` preserves filenames starting with `.`, this test could run on all platforms. The current placement is acceptable but perhaps overly restrictive.

#### ✅ Style — Code follows established patterns

All three tests:
- Use appropriate `ConditionalTheory`/`Fact` attributes
- Follow the arrange-act-assert pattern without explicit comments
- Use `TempDirectory` for file system isolation

Pull request overview

Adds additional unit tests to increase coverage of `System.Formats.Tar` behaviors around file creation/extraction and reader handling of unsupported entry types.

**Changes:**
- Added a Unix test ensuring executable permissions are preserved when archiving and extracting a file.
- Added a reader test that validates a `NotSupportedException` is thrown when encountering an unsupported tar entry type.
- Added a Unix test validating `TarWriter.WriteEntry` can create an entry from a dot-prefixed (“hidden”) file.

## ✅ Code Simplifier Daily Improver Workflow - Complete

Successfully converted the Claude code simplifier agent into a daily improver agentic workflow for gh-aw.

### Completed Tasks:
- [x] Analyze the source code simplifier from Anthropic's repository

### Implementation Details:

#### 📄 `.github/agentics/code-simplifier.md`
Comprehensive agent prompt with four main phases:
1. **Phase 1: Identify Recently Modified Code** - Finds PRs and commits from last 24 hours
2. **Phase 2: Analyze and Simplify Code** - Reviews project standards and applies simplifications
3. **Phase 3: Validate Changes** - Runs tests, linters, and builds
4. **Phase 4: Create Pull Request** - Generates PR if improvements are beneficial

**Key Features:**
- Focus on recently modified code (last 24 hours)
- Project-specific standards for Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Python
- Simplification principles: preserve functionality, enhance clarity, apply standards, maintain balance
- Comprehensive validation (tests, linting, builds)
- Exit gracefully when no changes or no improvements needed

#### 📄 `.github/workflows/code-simplifier.md`
Workflow configuration:
- **Schedule**: Fuzzy daily schedule (`schedule: daily`) → compiled to `cron: "9 14 * * *"`
- **Permissions**: Read-only (contents, issues, pull-requests)
- **Skip-if-match**: `'is:pr is:open in:title "[code-simplifier]"'` prevents duplicate PRs
- **Tools**: GitHub toolsets for code analysis (edit and bash enabled by default)
- **Safe Outputs**: create-pull-request with title prefix, labels, reviewer assignment, and 7-day expiration
- **Timeout**: 30 minutes
- **Strict Mode**: Enabled for security
- **Runtime Import**: `@./agentics/code-simplifier.md` allows editing without recompilation

#### 🔒 `.github/workflows/code-simplifier.lock.yml`
Successfully compiled to 1144 lines:
- ✅ Daily schedule with scattered time (9:14 UTC)
- ✅ workflow_dispatch automatically added by compiler
- ✅ Skip-if-match processed as search check in pre-activation job
- ✅ Safe outputs configuration embedded with 7-day expiration
- ✅ Threat detection and validation steps included

### Key Design Decisions:

1. **Daily Execution**: Uses fuzzy scheduling (`schedule: daily`) to distribute execution and avoid load spikes
2. **Recent Code Focus**: Only analyzes code changed in last 24 hours (not all code)
3. **Preservation First**: Never changes functionality, only improves clarity
4. **Multi-Language Support**: Handles Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Python with project-specific standards
5. **Comprehensive Testing**: Runs tests, linting, and builds before creating PR
6. **Duplicate Prevention**: Uses skip-if-match to avoid multiple open PRs
7. **Editable Prompt**: Agent prompt in separate file can be modified without recompilation
8. **Graceful Exit**: Exits without creating PR when no changes or no improvements needed
9. **Default Tools**: Simplified tools configuration by relying on default edit and bash tools
10. **PR Expiration**: PRs automatically close after 7 days if not merged

### Workflow Behavior:

The workflow will:
1. Run daily at 9:14 UTC (automatically scattered by compiler)
2. Check if there's already an open PR with "[code-simplifier]" in title (skip if exists)
3. Find code changes from the last 24 hours (merged PRs and commits)
4. Analyze changed files for simplification opportunities
5. Apply simplifications following project-specific coding standards
6. Run tests, linters, and builds to validate changes
7. Create a PR with improvements if changes pass validation
8. PRs will automatically expire and close after 7 days if not merged
9. Exit gracefully if no changes or no improvements needed

title: Allow preset modification commands to target CMakeUserPresets.json
body:
## This change addresses item #4564

### This changes visible behavior

The following changes are proposed:

- Add `determineTargetPresetsFile()` to `PresetsController` that resolves which presets file to write to when adding a new preset
- Modify `addPresetAddUpdate()` to check inheritance first, then fall through to user-driven file selection
- Capture `activeTextEditor` at the start of each `addXxxPreset()` method before QuickPick dialogs shift focus, and pass the snapshot through to `determineTargetPresetsFile()`
- Use `util.platformNormalizePath()` for cross-platform path comparison between `uri.fsPath` and `path.join()` results

## The purpose of this change

Preset modification commands (`Add Configure Preset`, `Add Build Preset`, etc.) always wrote to `CMakePresets.json` unless `inheritsFromUserPreset()` detected the new preset inherited from a user preset. Users had no way to explicitly target `CMakeUserPresets.json`.

New resolution order in `addPresetAddUpdate()`:

1. **Inheritance** — if the new preset inherits from a user preset, automatically write to `CMakeUserPresets.json` (preserves original behavior, required because `CMakePresets.json` cannot reference `CMakeUserPresets.json`)
2. **Active editor** — if a presets file is focused when the command is invoked, use it (the active editor path is captured at the start of each `addXxxPreset()` method, before any QuickPick dialogs that could shift focus, and compared using `platformNormalizePath()` for cross-platform correctness)
3. **Both files exist** — prompt via QuickPick
4. **One file exists** — use it
5. **Neither exists** — default to `CMakePresets.json`

Note: presets inheriting from `CMakePresets.json` can go in either file (since `CMakeUserPresets.json` implicitly includes `CMakePresets.json`), so user choice is offered in that case.

## Other Notes/Information

QuickPick labels are derived from `path.basename()` on the actual file paths rather than hardcoded strings. The `activeTextEditor` snapshot is taken early in the command flow to ensure the active editor check works correctly even after multiple QuickPick interactions during preset creation. title: pretty-table: add Cell struct with per-cell styling and horizontal span
body:
Adds a `Cell` type to `pretty-table` enabling per-cell ANSI styling (bold, italic, fg/bg color) and horizontal column spanning (`hspan`). Previously rows were `[n][]const u8`; now they are `[n]Cell`, with `Cell.init(text)` as the zero-cost default path.

## API changes (`src/mod/pretty-table.zig`)
- New `Cell` struct with builder methods: `init`, `span`, `withBold`, `withItalic`, `withFg`, `withBg`, `withHspan`
- `Row(n)` is now `[n]Cell`; plain-text usage wraps strings with `Cell.init(...)`
- `Table` gains `column_align`, `padding`, and `row_separator` fields
- Removed `cell_colors`, `header_color`, `footer_color` fields (superseded by per-cell styling)
- Column-width calculation handles multi-column spans in two passes: non-spanning cells first, then expand the last spanned column to fit

## Span usage example
```zig
const t = Table(3){
    .header = [_]Cell{ Cell.init("Name"), Cell.init("Q1"), Cell.init("Q2") },
    .rows = &[_][3]Cell{
        .{ Cell.init("Alice"), Cell.init("90"), Cell.init("85") },
        // "Total" spans both Q columns; the placeholder Cell.span() fills position 2
        .{ Cell.init("Bob"), Cell.init("On leave").withHspan(2), Cell.span() },
    },
};
```

## Consumers updated
- `src/bin/loc.zig`: rows and header updated from `[]const u8` to `Cell.init(...)` wrappers — no behavioral change
- `examples/pretty-table-demo.zig` and `docs/content/packages/pretty-table.org` updated to reflect new API

## Scope
`src/mod/simargs.zig` and all other `src/bin/*.zig` files are **unchanged** from the merge base — this PR is strictly scoped to `pretty-table`.

title: Fix Windows worktree migration failure: normalize Git path separators
body:
Git writes forward slashes in its internal files (`.git` files, gitdir files) on all platforms, but `filepath.Join()` uses backslashes on Windows, causing both test failures and worktree migration failures.

## Changes

### Test Assertions (`cmd_migrate_test.go`)
- Wrap expected paths with `filepath.ToSlash()` in worktree migration test assertions
- Affected: `TestDoMigrate/migrate_with_linked_worktrees` and `TestDoMigrate/migrate_with_internal_worktree`

```go
// Before
wantGitdir := "gitdir: " + filepath.Join(dest, ".git", "worktrees", "wt")

// After
wantGitdir := "gitdir: " + filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(dest, ".git", "worktrees", "wt"))
```

### Migration Code (`cmd_migrate.go`)
Fixed `repairWorktreeBackPointers` function to properly handle Git's forward-slash path format on Windows:
- Normalize `oldDir` to forward slashes before comparison
- Normalize `wtPath` read from gitdir files for comparison
- Write updated gitdir files with forward slashes (Git's format)
- Fix path trimming to use forward slash separator

```go
// Before
oldPrefix := oldDir + string(filepath.Separator)
if strings.HasPrefix(wtPath, oldPrefix) {
    newPath := filepath.Join(destDir, wtPath[len(oldDir):])
    // ...
}

// After
oldPrefixNorm := filepath.ToSlash(oldDir) + "/"
wtPathNorm := filepath.ToSlash(wtPath)
if strings.HasPrefix(wtPathNorm, oldPrefixNorm) {
    relativePart := wtPathNorm[len(oldPrefixNorm):]
    newPath := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(destDir, relativePart))
    // ...
}
```

This pattern is already used elsewhere in the codebase (see `cmd_get_test.go`) for cross-platform path comparisons.

## Root Cause

On Windows, the migration code was failing to detect internal worktrees because it compared:
- Git's gitdir file content: `C:/path/to/worktree/.git` (forward slashes)
- Go's filepath prefix: `C:\path\to\old\` (backslashes)

The `strings.HasPrefix` check would always fail, preventing internal worktrees from being repaired during migration.

## Changes

- **peer dependency**: Extended from `^8.57.1 || ^9.0.0` to `^8.57.1 || ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0` in `packages/eslint-plugin-svelte/package.json`
- **CI matrix**: Added ESLint 10 to test matrix in `.github/workflows/NodeCI.yml` alongside existing versions 8 and 9
- **lockfile**: Updated `pnpm-lock.yaml` to reflect peer dependency changes

~~No code changes required—plugin already uses flat config APIs compatible with ESLint 10.~~

title: feat: add serialization support for Set, Map, Date, RegExp, and BigInt via ISerializer contract
body:
`Set`, `Map`, `RegExp`, and `BigInt` don't survive `JSON.stringify` — Sets/Maps become `{}`, BigInt throws. Dates worked via a regex heuristic that could false-positive on ISO-looking strings. This adds a `__type`/`__value` envelope pattern with a pluggable `ISerializer` interface.

### Changes

- **`ISerializer` contract** (`src/adapter/data/ISerializer.ts`) — `type`, `serialize()`, `deserialize()`, `test()` methods for custom type support
- **Built-in serializers** (`src/adapter/data/Serializers.ts`) — `DateSerializer`, `SetSerializer`, `MapSerializer`, `RegExpSerializer`, `BigIntSerializer` with `defaultSerializers` exported as a frozen (immutable) array
- **`JsonAdapter` rewrite** — replaced regex-based date reviver with serializer-driven `replacer`/`reviver`. Uses `this[key]` in the replacer to access raw values before `.toJSON()` runs (needed for Date). The legacy `parseDates` parameter has been removed — Date handling is now managed entirely through the serializer system. The reviver uses a `Map<string, ISerializer>` keyed by type for O(1) deserialization lookup
- **`__type` escaping** — user data that naturally contains `__type` properties is automatically escaped during serialization and unescaped during deserialization, preventing false type matching
- **`Config.addSerializer()`** — new method on `Config` to easily register custom serializers without manually constructing adapters
- **Exports** — `ISerializer`, all serializer classes, and `defaultSerializers` exported from package entry point
- **README updated** — documents built-in type serialization, serialized format table, and custom serializer usage via both `Config.addSerializer()` and `defaultSerializers` spread pattern

### Serialized format

```json
{ "__type": "Set", "__value": [1, 2, 3] }
{ "__type": "Map", "__value": [["key", "value"]] }
{ "__type": "Date", "__value": "2023-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" }
{ "__type": "RegExp", "__value": { "source": "^test$", "flags": "gi" } }
{ "__type": "BigInt", "__value": "9007199254740993" }
```

### Consumer extensibility

```typescript
import { JsonDB, Config, ISerializer } from 'node-json-db';

const urlSerializer: ISerializer = {
  type: "URL",
  serialize: (value: URL) => value.href,
  deserialize: (value: string) => new URL(value),
  test: (value: any) => value instanceof URL,
};

const config = new Config('mydb');
config.addSerializer(urlSerializer);
const db = new JsonDB(config);
```

Or with full control via `defaultSerializers`:

```typescript
import { JsonAdapter, FileAdapter, defaultSerializers } from 'node-json-db';

const adapter = new JsonAdapter(
  new FileAdapter('mydb.json', false),
  false,
  [...defaultSerializers, mySerializer]
);
```

### Breaking changes

- Date serialization now uses `{ "__type": "Date", "__value": "..." }` instead of bare ISO strings. Existing databases with dates stored as plain ISO strings will read them back as strings, not Date objects.
- The `parseDates` parameter has been removed from both `Config` and `JsonAdapter` constructors. Date handling is now controlled by the presence of `DateSerializer` in the serializers list.

body:
Extends support to Laravel 13 and Pest v4 alongside existing Laravel 9–12 and Pest v1–3 support.

## Changes

- **`composer.json`**: Added `^13.0` to all `illuminate/*` constraints (`redis`, `support`, `database`, `collections`), `^11.0` to `orchestra/testbench`, and `^4.0` to `pestphp/pest` and `pestphp/pest-plugin-laravel`
- **`run-tests.yml`**: Added PHP 8.4 matrix entries for both Laravel `12.*` / testbench `10.*` and Laravel `13.*` / testbench `11.*`; added explicit `pest` version pins to all matrix entries (`4.*` for PHP 8.4, `3.*` for PHP 8.3, `2.*` for PHP 8.2, `1.*` for PHP 8.1) and updated the install step to require the pinned pest version

body:
## 📋 Description

Upgrades Chapter 2 from .NET 9 to .NET 10, including framework retargeting, package updates for compatibility, API migration for breaking changes, and CI/CD pipeline configuration.

### Framework & Packages
- Retargeted `TargetFramework` to `net10.0`
- Updated core packages:
  - Swashbuckle.AspNetCore: 9.0.4 → 10.0.1
  - Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore, Npgsql.*, Microsoft.AspNetCore.*, Microsoft.Extensions.*: 9.0.x → 10.0.0
  - Added Microsoft.OpenApi 2.3.0 (required dependency for Swashbuckle 10.x)

### API Migration
Replaced deprecated `WithOpenApi()` with `WithSummary()` + `WithDescription()` in endpoint definitions:

```csharp
// Before (.NET 9)
.WithOpenApi(operation => new(operation)
{
    Summary = "Signs prepared contract",
    Description = "This endpoint is used to sign prepared contract by customer.",
})

// After (.NET 10)
.WithSummary("Signs prepared contract")
.WithDescription("This endpoint is used to sign prepared contract by customer.")
```

Applied to: `SignContractEndpoint`, `PrepareContractEndpoint`, `GenerateNewPassesPerMonthReportEndpoint`, `GetAllPassesEndpoint`, `MarkPassAsExpiredEndpoint`

### CI/CD Pipeline
- GitHub Actions workflow: Updated to use .NET 10.0.x in both build and test jobs

### Project Cleanup
- Removed redundant `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Abstractions` references from projects with `FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App"` (NU1510 warnings)
- Fixed migration file formatting to comply with `.editorconfig` (file-scoped namespaces with internal using directives)

## 📦 PR Includes

- [ ] Feature added 🆕
- [ ] Bug fix 🐛
- [ ] Code refactor 🔄
- [ ] Documentation update 📚
- [ ] Tests added/updated 🧪
- [x] Other: .NET 10 framework upgrade

## 🚫 PR Does Not Include

- [x] Breaking changes ❌
- [x] Major architectural changes 🏗️
- [x] Unrelated features/tasks 🚫

## 💡 Additional Notes

All existing tests pass (14 integration tests). Migration file formatting fixes were necessary to satisfy stricter code style enforcement in .NET 10 tooling.

Files modified:
- `Directory.Build.props`
- `Directory.Packages.props`
- 3 `.csproj` files (package reference cleanup)
- 5 endpoint files for WithOpenApi deprecation

- `.github/workflows/chapter-2-workflow.yml` - CI/CD pipeline configuration

The Claude and Copilot MCP gateway configuration converters were only
adding the Authorization header if it already existed in the gateway
output. This caused the converted configurations to be missing the
required API key authentication headers.

Updated both converters to always create the headers object with the
Authorization field set to the MCP_GATEWAY_API_KEY value.

Fixes the issue where Claude configuration was missing authorization
headers for MCP servers (github, playwright, safeoutputs, serena).

title: Fix MCP gateway error reporting and configuration handling
body:
## Fix MCP Gateway Error Reporting and Configuration ✅

**Problem**: Investigate why writing to stdout fails in the MCP gateway (workflow run #20858052635).

### Root Cause
Per MCP Gateway Specification v1.0.0 section 9.1, the gateway writes **error payloads to stdout**, not stderr. The startup script was only checking stderr logs when errors occurred, missing the actual error details written to `gateway-output.json`.

### Changes Made

1. **Enhanced error reporting** (commit eff8b1d)
   - Added stdout display in error messages (where errors are written per spec)
   - Added detection for error payloads (`.error` field in JSON)
   - Added clarifying comments referencing MCP Gateway Specification

2. **Removed unnecessary file saving** (commit 37dc9ff)
   - Removed saving of input config to `/tmp/gh-aw/mcp-config/gateway-input.json`
   - Gateway properly reads config from stdin and writes to stdout

3. **Removed redundant environment variables from docker command** (commit 35310f1)
   - Removed `-e MCP_GATEWAY_PORT -e MCP_GATEWAY_DOMAIN -e MCP_GATEWAY_API_KEY` from docker run command
   - These values are now read from the configuration file's gateway section
   - Shell script still validates these env vars exist (needed for script logic and variable expansion)

4. **Enabled shell variable expansion in config heredoc** (commit a4b79d8)
   - Removed single quotes from heredoc delimiter to allow variable expansion
   - Shell now expands `${MCP_GATEWAY_PORT}` and other variables before piping to gateway
   - Configuration is piped with actual values, not variable expressions that can't be resolved

### How It Works

The configuration flow:
1. Shell script exports environment variables (`MCP_GATEWAY_PORT`, `MCP_GATEWAY_DOMAIN`, `MCP_GATEWAY_API_KEY`)
2. Heredoc generates JSON config with variable references like `${MCP_GATEWAY_PORT}`
3. Shell expands these variables to actual values (heredoc has no quotes)
4. Expanded JSON config is piped to `start_mcp_gateway.sh` via stdin
5. Script validates the JSON has required gateway section fields
6. Script pipes validated config to docker gateway container via stdin
7. Gateway reads config from stdin, processes it, writes output to stdout
8. Stdout is captured in `/tmp/gh-aw/mcp-config/gateway-output.json`
9. Converter scripts read from this file via `$MCP_GATEWAY_OUTPUT`

Environment variables:
- Exported in shell script for script validation and heredoc variable expansion
- NOT passed to docker container via `-e` flags (values are in the JSON config)
- Gateway reads port, domain, apiKey from the JSON config's gateway section

Error handling now properly checks stdout for:
- Error payloads (JSON with `.error` field)
- Missing or incomplete output
- Health check failures

### Testing ✅
- ✅ Shell script syntax validated
- ✅ Go code compiles successfully
- ✅ Error payload detection tested
- ✅ Stdout capture working correctly
- ✅ Heredoc variable expansion tested

---

## Add Missing Pattern Detectors ✅

Re-added three pattern detection checks that existed in the original `pattern_detection` job but were accidentally omitted when pattern detection was integrated into the `classify` step:

### Patterns Re-Added:

1. **display-mask Dependency** 
   - Detects: `display-mask` or `failed to resolve` + `microsoft.device`
   - Provides: Maven repository configuration for display-mask library

2. **Android 15 / SDK 35 Compatibility**
   - Detects: `android 15`, `sdk 35`, `api 35`, or `edge` + `display`
   - Provides: Guidance on edge-to-edge display and package visibility

3. **Azure AD B2C Configuration (General)**
   - Detects: `b2c` + (`error` or `fail` or `not working`)
   - Provides: Authority URL format and configuration examples
   - Note: This is in addition to the existing B2C expired token pattern

### Total Pattern Detectors: 13
- Redirect URI encoding
- AADSTS error codes
- Broker integration
- Deprecated API usage
- PCA initialization
- Silent token acquisition
- R8/ProGuard configuration
- B2C expired grant
- JSON cache corruption
- Browser signature mismatch
- **display-mask dependency** (re-added)
- **Android 15 compatibility** (re-added)
- **B2C general configuration** (re-added)

### Validation:
✅ YAML syntax validated
✅ All patterns from original workflow now present
✅ Feature parity maintained

title: Update OpenAI to 2.9.1, Azure.AI.OpenAI to 2.9.0-beta.1, Azure.AI.Projects to 2.0.0-beta.2, Microsoft.Extensions.AI* to 10.4.0
body:
### Motivation and Context

Bumps core AI SDK dependencies to their latest versions to pick up new features and fixes.

### Description

Updates the following packages in `Directory.Packages.props`:

- **OpenAI** 2.8.0 → 2.9.1
- **Azure.AI.OpenAI** 2.8.0-beta.1 → 2.9.0-beta.1
- **Azure.AI.Projects** 1.1.0 → 2.0.0-beta.2
- **Azure.Identity** 1.17.1 → 1.19.0 (cascading dependency from Azure.AI.Projects 2.0.0-beta.2)
- **Microsoft.Extensions.AI\*** 10.3.0 → 10.4.0
- **System.Text.Json, System.Numerics.Tensors, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions, Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces, System.Threading.Channels** → 10.0.4

Addresses the following breaking changes introduced by OpenAI 2.9.1:

- `CreateInputImagePart` BinaryData overload removed (replaced with data URI approach)
- Realtime API type renames (`ConversationTool` → `RealtimeTool`, `ConversationSessionOptions` → `RealtimeConversationSessionOptions`, etc.)
- `ResponsesClient` constructor no longer accepts a model parameter; model is now specified on `CreateResponseOptions.Model`
- `ResponseResult.Instructions` is now read-only

Code changes to adapt:

- Added `ModelId` property to `OpenAIResponseAgent` and propagated it through `ResponseCreationOptionsFactory`
- Updated unit tests (`BaseOpenAIResponseClientTest`, `OpenAIResponseAgentExtensionsTests`, `OpenAIResponseExtensionsTests`)
- Updated integration tests (`OpenAIResponseAgentTests`, `OpenAIResponseAgentFixture`)
- Updated `BaseResponsesAgentTest` and `GettingStartedWithAgents` samples
- Updated `AgentFrameworkMigration` samples (`GetResponsesClient`, `AsIChatClient`, `CreateAIAgent`, modelId propagation)
- Rewrote `OpenAIRealtime` demo for the restructured Realtime API event model

### Contribution Checklist

- [x] The code builds clean without any errors or warnings
- [x] The PR follows the [SK Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [pre-submission formatting script](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development-scripts) raises no violations
- [x] All unit tests pass, and I have added new tests where possible
- [ ] I didn't break anyone :smile:

title: Add entrypoint and mounts fields to MCP server configs (breaking change)
body:
The MCP gateway spec had two bugs: missing optional `entrypoint` field for container entrypoint overrides, and `mounts` configured at gateway level instead of per-server.

## Changes

**Schema & Types**
- Added `entrypoint` (string) and `mounts` (array) fields to `BaseMCPServerConfig`
- Updated `mcp_config_schema.json` with new field definitions and validation patterns
- **Removed `mounts` field from `MCPGatewayRuntimeConfig` (breaking change)**

**Parsing & Transformation**
- Enhanced `parser.ParseMCPConfig` and `workflow.ParseMCPConfigFromMap` to parse new fields
- Transform `entrypoint` → `docker run --entrypoint <value>`
- Transform `mounts` → `docker run -v <source>:<dest>:<mode>` (sorted for deterministic output)
- **Removed all gateway-level mounts extraction, validation, and docker command generation**

**Breaking Change**
- Gateway-level `mounts` configuration is **no longer supported**
- Users must migrate to per-server `mounts` configuration
- Migration: Move `sandbox.mcp.mounts` to `tools.<server-name>.mounts`

## Example

```yaml
tools:
  custom-mcp:
    container: ghcr.io/org/server:latest
    entrypoint: /custom/entrypoint.sh
    entrypointArgs: ["--config", "/app/config.json"]
    mounts:
      - "/host/data:/data:ro"
      - "/host/cache:/cache:rw"
```

Generates: `docker run --rm -i -v /host/cache:/cache:rw -v /host/data:/data:ro --entrypoint /custom/entrypoint.sh ghcr.io/org/server:latest --config /app/config.json`

title: Revert non-tag changes, keep ebpfassets/dynamic, minimally fix unit tests
body:
The previous PR introduced wide-ranging changes beyond the intended `ebpfassets`/`dynamic` build tag scope. This PR reverts all unrelated changes back to the `bfe0970` baseline, retains only the tag-related additions, and fixes the resulting test failures by updating the test files to match the original production code behavior.

## Kept: `ebpfassets` / `dynamic` tag changes
- `assets/ebpf_probe_stub.go` — stub package for `!ebpfassets` builds
- `pkg/util/ebpf/elibpcap.go` — `//go:build dynamic` constraint added
- `pkg/util/ebpf/elibpcap_stub.go` — stub for `!dynamic` (no libpcap required)
- `Makefile` — injects `//go:build ebpfassets` into generated asset file via `sed`; adds `-tags dynamic,ebpfassets` to `test-race`
- `functions.mk` — adds `ebpfassets,dynamic` to release build tags

## Production code fixes kept (not reverted)
- **`base/base_probe.go`** — guard `p.logger` / `p.dispatcher` nil in `Close()` to avoid panic on uninitialized probes
- **`base/base_probe_test.go`** — remove `TestBaseProbeInitializeNilDispatcher`; `Initialize()` always creates its own dispatcher so the test premise is wrong

title: docs: update documentation and website for project reorganization
body:
Documentation across 9 files referenced the pre-reorganization project structure (`crates/mobile/`, `mobile/`, `localgpt-cli`, "6 crates") after the recent restructuring commit.

### Path renames
- `crates/mobile/` → `crates/mobile-ffi/` and `localgpt-mobile` → `localgpt-mobile-ffi` in all cargo commands and references (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, copilot-instructions.md)
- `mobile/ios/scripts/build-rust.sh` → `apps/ios/scripts/build_ios.sh`, `mobile/android/` → `apps/android/` (CLAUDE.md, app READMEs)
- UniFFI bindgen output dirs: `mobile/{ios,android}/Generated` → `apps/{ios,android}/Generated`
- `localgpt-cli` → `localgpt` (correct binary package name in copilot-instructions.md)

### Workspace structure diagrams
- "6 crates" → "7 crates" with new `crates/bridge/` entry
- Added `bridges/` (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp) and `apps/` (iOS, Android) top-level dirs
- Removed obsolete `mobile/` root directory line

### Architecture (docs/architecture.md)
- Updated "Key Differences vs OpenClaw" — bridges now exist, web UI exists, bridge daemon model replaces "no gateway"

### Website updates
- **website/docs/openclaw-migration.md**: Fixed false claims ("No remote channels", "No web UI/Canvas") — now reflects bridge-based integrations (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp) and embedded web UI
- **website/docs/intro.md**: Updated Telegram-only feature to mention all three bridges (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp)
- **website/src/components/HomepageFeatures/index.tsx**: Updated feature card title and description to reflect bridge integrations

title: Support model as string[] in custom agent definitions
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/280879

Custom agents can now specify a prioritized list of models instead of just a single model. When multiple models are specified, the system attempts each in order until finding a match.

## Changes

**Type system updates:**
- `ICustomAgent.model`, `IChatModeData.model`, `IChatMode.model`: `string[] | undefined`

**Parser (`promptFileParser.ts`):**
- Added `getStringOrStringArrayAttribute()` to parse both single strings and arrays
- `PromptHeader.model` now returns `string[] | undefined`

**Validation (`promptValidator.ts` and `chatModes.ts`):**
- Validates array constraints: non-empty, string-only items, non-empty strings
- Validates each model in array against available models
- Type mismatch, unknown models, and unsuitable models produce appropriate errors/warnings
- Fixed `isCachedChatModeData()` to validate model as `string | string[]` for cached mode restoration

**Consumer fallback logic:**
- `chatInputPart.ts`, `chatWidget.ts`: Iterate through array to select first available model
- `runSubagentTool.ts`: Match qualified names against model array

**Tests:**
- 7 tests covering valid arrays, validation errors, and edge cases
- All 409 common chat tests passing

## Example

```yaml
---
name: "code-expert"
description: "Specialized coding agent"
model: ['gpt-4', 'claude-3-opus', 'claude-3-sonnet']  # Tries in order
---
```

Backward compatible - single string models continue to work unchanged.

- [x] Use walrus operator in Kafka check (then simplified for clarity)
- [x] Remove obsolete ServiceUnavailable re-raise in Kafka
- [x] Move consumer creation outside try block in Kafka
- [x] Split try blocks and use response.text in RSS check
- [x] Remove obsolete BaseException handling in RabbitMQ
- [x] Run code review and final tests
- [x] Address code review comments
- [x] Revert to list API for bootstrap_servers (preserving original API)
- [x] Simplify falsy checks (remove explicit None comparisons)

**Changes:**
- Migrated Kafka check from kafka-python to confluent-kafka with AIOConsumer
- Migrated RabbitMQ check from kombu to aio-pika for native async support
- Migrated RSS check from urllib to httpx for async HTTP requests

title: Expose task-level and estimator-level preprocessors as public API
body:
## Plan to expose preprocessor APIs

- [x] Explore repository structure and understand preprocessing flow
- [x] Add public `preprocess()` method to AutoML class for task-level preprocessing
- [x] Add public `preprocess()` method to estimator classes for estimator-level preprocessing  
- [x] Add tests for the new preprocessor APIs
- [x] Validate tests pass
- [x] Add documentation for the new API methods
- [x] Add example script demonstrating API usage
- [x] Run broader test suite to ensure no regressions
- [x] Address code review feedback
- [x] Fix formatting issues with pre-commit hooks

## Summary

This PR successfully exposes the previously internal preprocessing methods as user-facing APIs, addressing issue #228.

### Key Changes:
1. **`AutoML.preprocess(X)`** - Task-level preprocessing API
2. **`BaseEstimator.preprocess(X)`** - Estimator-level preprocessing API
3. Comprehensive documentation and examples
4. Full test coverage (8/8 tests passing)

### Latest Changes:
- Fixed formatting issues identified by pre-commit hooks (trailing whitespace, code formatting)
- All tests continue to pass

title: fix: prevent path traversal (CWE-22) in corpus and data path functions
body:
Path-building functions accepted external input without verifying the resolved path stayed inside its intended base directory, enabling path traversal attacks (CWE-22). Two internal helper functions (`path_pythainlp_corpus` and `get_path_folder_corpus`) were identified as redundant attack surfaces and removed.

### What do these changes do

- Added `safe_path_join(base, *parts)` as a public helper in `pythainlp/tools/path.py` and exported from `pythainlp.tools` — the single authoritative traversal guard used throughout the library, eliminating code duplication
- `get_full_data_path(path)` — delegates to `safe_path_join`; now rejects any `path` that resolves outside the PyThaiNLP data directory and returns a normalized absolute path
- Removed `path_pythainlp_corpus()` — its one internal call site in `get_corpus_default_db()` now calls `safe_path_join(corpus_path(), filename)` directly
- Removed `get_path_folder_corpus()` — its one call site in `pythainlp/tag/wangchanberta_onnx.py` now calls `get_corpus_path()` once to obtain the base path, then uses `safe_path_join(base, file)` for each file access; relies on `get_corpus_path()` to raise `FileNotFoundError` for missing corpora (including offline-mode checks); a minimal `if not _corpus_base` guard prevents a `TypeError` when `get_corpus_path()` returns `None` on download failure
- Both removed functions are no longer exported from `pythainlp/corpus/__init__.py`
- 14 tests in `tests/core/test_security.py` covering safe inputs and traversal rejections, using `_is_within_directory` for proper containment assertions
- Applied `black` formatting to `pythainlp/tag/wangchanberta_onnx.py`; fixed a flake8 E303 warning in `tests/core/test_security.py`

### What was wrong

Path-building helpers called `os.path.join(base, user_input)` and returned the raw joined string without normalization or containment validation. A caller supplying `"../../etc/passwd"` or similar would silently receive a path outside the intended directory. The traversal check was also duplicated inline in multiple functions rather than sharing a common implementation. Two helper functions (`path_pythainlp_corpus`, `get_path_folder_corpus`) each had only a single internal call site, making them unnecessary intermediaries that widened the attack surface.

```python
# Before — no validation
get_full_data_path("../../etc/passwd")
# → /root/pythainlp-data/../../etc/passwd  (resolves to /etc/passwd)
```

### How this fixes it

`safe_path_join(base, *parts)` normalizes `base` with `os.path.abspath`, joins it with `*parts`, normalizes the result, and asserts the result starts with the base prefix before returning the normalized absolute path. All path-building code delegates to this single public helper. Removing `path_pythainlp_corpus` and `get_path_folder_corpus` eliminates two redundant layers through which external input could flow toward the filesystem. `get_corpus_path()` is the sole authority for resolving corpus locations and raising `FileNotFoundError` (including offline-mode handling), avoiding duplicated error logic at call sites.

```python
# After — traversal blocked
get_full_data_path("../../etc/passwd")
# → ValueError: Path traversal attempt detected: resolved path '/etc/passwd'
#              is outside the base directory '/root/pythainlp-data'.
```

title: feat(portal): browser-authentication tokens for headless clients
body: Headless clients need browser-based authentication flow for IdP sign-in. Portal currently uses `as=client` for GUI clients which deep-links the token. Headless clients need the token displayed in browser for manual copy-paste. ## Changes ### Portal (Elixir) - Refactored `as=client` → `as=gui-client` (backward compatible) - Added `as=headless-client` flow terminating at token display page - Updated context type handling: `:client` → `:gui_client`, added `:headless_client` - New `headless_client_token.html` template with copy-to-clipboard - Separate token generation logic: GUI clients use nonce-based tokens, headless clients use complete tokens - Added comprehensive tests for authentication flows

title: test: disable Chromatic snapshots for redundant and non-visual stories
body:
Reduces snapshot consumption by disabling Chromatic for 78+ stories that don't provide visual regression value: interactive flows requiring user action, icon galleries, demo composites, redundant variations, and state duplicates.

## Changes

Disabled snapshots for stories requiring interaction or showing redundant variants:

- **Interactive stories (23)** - Modals, drawers, popovers, tooltips requiring clicks/hovers
- **Icon galleries (2)** - Collections rendering 100+ icons
- **Form interactions (2)** - State-based stories with interactive toggle buttons  
- **Guided tours (3)** - Multi-step flows with loading states
- **Demo composites (5)** - Multiple variants already tested individually
- **Virtualized lists (10)** - Collapsible panels and table variations showing minor differences
- **Redundant variation stories (27)** - Button, Tag, ButtonIcon showing prop combinations already covered by template stories
- **State duplicates (13)** - Status icon-only variants and RichRadioButton checked state duplicates
- **Range filters** - Already disabled (verified no regression)

Implementation adds story-level parameters:

```tsx
export const Interactive = () => { /* ... */ };
Interactive.parameters = {
  chromatic: { disableSnapshot: true },
};
```

Stories remain available for development and documentation. Visual regression coverage preserved for static, meaningful variations.

## Impact

- **78+ stories disabled** (43% snapshot reduction)
- Focused on eliminating redundant prop combinations and state variations
- Preserved unique visual variations important for design system regression testing

## Files Modified

19 story files in `packages/design-system`, `packages/components`, and `packages/icons`.

# Describe the PR `BBreadcrumb` exposes no way to pass classes or attributes to the inner `
    ` element. This makes it impossible to fix alignment issues (e.g., `align-items-center`) when using the `#prepend` slot with icons. Adds `olClass` and `olAttrs` props to `BBreadcrumb`, following the established pattern (`bodyClass`/`bodyAttrs` on `BCard`, `headerClass`/`headerAttrs` on `BModal`, etc.): - `BBreadcrumbProps` — added `olClass?: ClassValue` and `olAttrs?: Readonly` - `BBreadcrumb.vue` — binds `olClass` via `:class` and `olAttrs` via `v-bind` to the `
      ` element - `breadcrumb.spec.ts` — test coverage for both new props - `breadcrumb.data.ts` — documentation entries for both new props ```vue ``` ## Small replication See the linked issue for screenshots demonstrating the vertical alignment problem with prepend slot content and the fix via styling the `
        `. ## PR checklist **What kind of change does this PR introduce?** (check at least one) - [ ] Bugfix :bug: - `fix(...)` - [x] Feature - `feat(...)` - [ ] ARIA accessibility - `fix(...)` - [ ] Documentation update - `docs(...)` - [ ] Other (please describe) **The PR fulfills these requirements:** - [x] Pull request title and all commits follow the [**Conventional Commits**](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) convention or has an [**override**](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please#how-can-i-fix-release-notes) in this pull request body **This is very important, as the `CHANGELOG` is generated from these messages, and determines the next version type. Pull requests that do not follow conventional commits or do not have an override will be denied**
        Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > How to set the styling for ol element in the Breadcrumb component > I want to set the styling (using SCSS) for the Breadcrumb component. But, when I try to add a prepend icon like this > > ``` > > > > ``` > > the icon is not align vertically with the rest of the content as you could see in the following screenshot: > > > > I notice that the component is rendered as ol element and if I use the browser inspector and change the styling, it works. > > > > > Is there any option to do it from the component? Is there any class that could help me? > > Thanks in advance > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > >
        - Fixes bootstrap-vue-next/bootstrap-vue-next#2852 --- 💬 We'd love your input! Share your thoughts on Copilot coding agent in our [2 minute survey](https://gh.io/copilot-coding-agent-survey).

title: Recompile workflows for gh-aw v0.44.0 compatibility
body:
Recompiled all 17 agentic workflows to resolve breaking changes in gh-aw v0.44.0.

## Changes

**Removed deprecated `app:` section from `safe-outputs`**
- The compiler now auto-generates GitHub App authentication when safe-output handlers are present
- Explicit `app:` configuration triggered duplicate token generation steps (compiler bug)

Before:
```yaml
safe-outputs:
  app:
    app-id: ${{ vars.APP_ID }}
    private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
  create-discussion:
    title-prefix: "${{ github.workflow }}"
```

After:
```yaml
safe-outputs:
  create-discussion:
    title-prefix: "${{ github.workflow }}"
```

**Fixed strict mode network violations**
- Added `strict: false` to 4 workflows using custom domains
- Removed unnecessary `storage.googleapis.com` from network allowlists
- Affected: ci-doctor, daily-perf-improver, daily-refactor, daily-test-improver

**Updated bash tool syntax**
- Changed `bash: [":*"]` to `bash: true` in update-docs workflow
- Required for create-pull-request handler to execute git commands

## Result

17 workflows compile cleanly with 0 errors, 1 expected warning (web-search unsupported by copilot engine).

title: Add tests asserting smoke-copilot and smoke-claude have detection jobs with AWF engine execution
body:
Ensures the compiled lock files for `smoke-copilot` and `smoke-claude` don't silently lose their threat detection jobs or AWF sandboxing.

## Changes

- **`extractDetectionJobSection`** — new helper in `compiled_lock_files_test.go` that extracts the `detection:` job block from a lock file, mirroring the existing `extractSafeOutputsJobSection` pattern
- **`TestCompiledLockFiles_SmokeWorkflowsHaveDetectionJobWithAgenticRunCall`** — table-driven test covering both smoke workflows, asserting per-workflow:
  - `detection_conclusion` and `detection_success` outputs are present
  - Step `id: detection_agentic_execution` exists
  - The step invokes `sudo -E awf` (AWF sandbox wrapping the engine call)

```
=== RUN   TestCompiledLockFiles_SmokeWorkflowsHaveDetectionJobWithAgenticRunCall/smoke-copilot.lock.yml
=== RUN   .../HasDetectionConclusionOutput
=== RUN   .../HasDetectionSuccessOutput
=== RUN   .../HasAgenticExecutionStepID
=== RUN   .../AgenticExecutionStepUsesAWF
--- PASS
=== RUN   TestCompiledLockFiles_SmokeWorkflowsHaveDetectionJobWithAgenticRunCall/smoke-claude.lock.yml
...
--- PASS
```

title: Add comprehensive integration tests for PHP-DI container functionality
body:
Changes proposed in this pull request:

## Test Coverage

Added `tests/ContainerFactoryTest.php` with 14 integration tests verifying:

- **Container initialization** - ContainerFactory creates container with all registered services
- **Service resolution** - Config, Logger, Steps, Generators resolve correctly from container
- **Builder registration** - Builder is properly registered in the container after creation
- **Fallback mechanism** - Builder::build() handles NotFoundException gracefully for unregistered services
- **Cache factory** - Builder::getCache() creates distinct instances per pool and per call
- **Compilation modes** - Container compiles in production, skips in debug mode
- **Factory definitions** - Twig and Cache factory patterns resolve correctly
- **Full lifecycle** - Complete build process exercises DI throughout

## Configuration

Updated `phpunit.xml.dist` to include ContainerFactoryTests suite.

## Test Quality Improvements

- Added tearDown method to clean up generated directories (.cecil, .cache, _site) after each test
- Environment variables properly restored after mutation using `putenv('CECIL_DEBUG=false')`
- All redundant assertions removed for clearer test intent
- Test names accurately reflect their purpose (e.g., `testBuilderIsInContainer` instead of `testAttributeBasedInjectionWithBuilder`)
- Cache behavior fully verified including multiple calls to same pool

Tests use existing fixtures and follow established patterns similar to IntegrationTests.php.

title: Fix Shell flyout template type cast errors on Android
body:
- [x] Analyze the issue: Documentation shows `AppThemeBinding` nested inside `OnPlatform` element syntax which causes type cast errors on Android
- [x] Review the actual MAUI source code for the correct default template implementation
- [x] Fix the "Default template for FlyoutItems" section:
  - Removed problematic nested `<OnPlatform x:TypeArguments="Color">` with `AppThemeBinding` for `TextColor`
  - Changed to inline syntax: `TextColor="{OnPlatform Android={AppThemeBinding Light=#DE000000, Dark=White}}"`
  - Fixed the `Selected` visual state `BackgroundColor` to use correct alpha values (`#1A000000` and `#1AFFFFFF`) matching MAUI source
  - Removed redundant `TargetName="FlyoutItemLayout"` from Selected state setter (VSM is already on the Grid)
  - Added IMPORTANT note warning users about the type cast error issue when nesting markup extensions
- [x] Update `ms.date` to reflect the documentation change
- [x] Run code review to validate changes
- [x] Run CodeQL security check (no code changes to analyze)
- [x] Address PR feedback: Removed redundant TargetName attribute

> 
> ```
> <Label.TextColor>
>                 <OnPlatform x:TypeArguments="Color">
>                     <OnPlatform.Platforms>
>                         <On Platform="Android"
>                             Value="{AppThemeBinding Light=Black, Dark=White}" />
>                     </OnPlatform.Platforms>
>                 </OnPlatform>
>             </Label.TextColor>
> ```
> 
> The App will crash on Android with API 31 and higher (tested on API 31, 32, and 33).  I haven't tested in prior versions.  It seems there are issues with Maui, Shell, and the Flyout navigation menu and the docs aren't helping because I can't get a Flyout menu to stabile work with the set documentation provided in this page.
> 
> I have also raised an issue with the background color not working on the Maui board which when used with this documentation code the bug worse:
> https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/19141
> 
> Also in iOS there is an issue with the header code provided that it causes the first link in iOS in the Flyout menu to to not work:
> https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/17965
>

title: Redirect new registrations to create property page
body:
New users registering without an org invite were redirected to the dashboard. They should land on the create property page instead, as noted by the existing TODO comment in `twofactor.go`.

- Capture `org` from `doRegister()` return and build redirect URL to `/org/{id}/property/new`
- Use `newRegistrationRedirectURL` as first-priority redirect after login cleanup, before `returnURL` fallback
- Org invite redirect (earlier in the flow) still takes precedence and returns early — unchanged

```go
if user, org, err := s.doRegister(ctx, sess); err == nil {
    _ = sess.Set(ctx, session.KeyUserID, user.ID)
    newRegistrationRedirectURL = s.PartsURL(common.OrgEndpoint, s.IDHasher.Encrypt(int(org.ID)), common.PropertyEndpoint, common.NewEndpoint)
}
```

Updated `TestPostRegister` to assert the redirect target matches the create property path.

title: Decouple ai-reaction emoji from status comments [BREAKING]
body:
## ✅ BREAKING CHANGE: Reaction and Status Comments Now Independent

Fully decoupled `reaction` and `status-comment` - both must be explicitly enabled.

### Breaking Change

**New behavior**:
```yaml
on:
  reaction: eyes           # Only adds 👀 reaction
  # No status comments unless explicitly enabled
```

**To get both**:
```yaml
on:
  reaction: eyes
  status-comment: true     # Must be explicit
```

### Implementation

**Core Changes** (4 Go files, simplified):
- `compiler_types.go`: Added `StatusComment *bool` field
- `compiler_safe_outputs.go`: Parse `status-comment` from `on` section
- `compiler_activation_jobs.go`: Direct pointer check `if data.StatusComment != nil && *data.StatusComment`
- `notify_comment.go`: Direct pointer check, removed unused variables, updated doc comment

**Schema**: Added `status-comment` field validation

**Testing** (simplified):
- 6 focused test cases covering all combinations
- 3 compilation tests for end-to-end validation
- Updated existing tests to reflect breaking change
- All tests passing ✅

### Files Changed

Source code (8 files):
- `pkg/workflow/compiler_types.go`
- `pkg/workflow/compiler_safe_outputs.go`
- `pkg/workflow/compiler_activation_jobs.go`
- `pkg/workflow/notify_comment.go`
- `pkg/workflow/notify_comment_test.go`
- `pkg/workflow/status_comment_decoupling_test.go` (new)
- `pkg/workflow/test_data/test-status-comment-decoupling.md` (new)
- `pkg/parser/schemas/main_workflow_schema.json`

Workflows migrated (7 files):
- `.github/workflows/smoke-copilot.md` - Added `status-comment: true`
- `.github/workflows/smoke-claude.md` - Added `status-comment: true`
- `.github/workflows/smoke-codex.md` - Added `status-comment: true`
- `.github/workflows/smoke-copilot-sdk.md` - Added `status-comment: true`
- `.github/workflows/smoke-opencode.md` - Added `status-comment: true`
- `.github/workflows/smoke-project.md` - Added `status-comment: true`
- `.github/workflows/smoke-temporary-id.md` - Added `status-comment: true`

Lock files: Automatically recompiled (all 154 workflows)

### Validation

✅ All checks passing:
- Tests: 6/6 unit + 3/3 integration
- Formatting: `make fmt` ✅
- Linting: `make lint` ✅
- Code simplified and cleaned per review
- All smoke workflows migrated successfully

### Migration Required

⚠️ Workflows using `reaction: eyes` must add `status-comment: true` to preserve status comments.

**Example**: All 7 smoke workflows have been updated in this PR to demonstrate the migration.

title: Fix PHP 8.4 TypeError: strtolower() null argument when Content-Type header missing
body:
## Fix PHP 8.4 TypeError when Content-Type header is missing

- [x] Identify the issue in StreamedPart.php line 222 where strtolower() receives null
- [x] Fix line 222 by handling null Content-Type header value (cast to string)
- [x] Create a focused test case for parts without Content-Type header
- [x] Run tests to validate the fix (all 28 tests pass)
- [x] Request code review (no issues found)
- [x] Run security checker (no issues found)
- [x] Remove .phpunit.result.cache and add to .gitignore

## Summary
Fixed the PHP 8.4 TypeError that occurred when parsing multipart/form-data requests where individual parts don't have a Content-Type header. The fix is minimal and surgical - just casting the potentially null value to string before passing to strtolower(). All tests pass and the solution is backward compatible with all PHP versions from 7.0 to 8.5.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>PHP 8.4 TypeError: strtolower() expects string, null given when multipart part lacks Content-Type header</issue_title>
> <issue_description>When parsing multipart/form-data requests where individual parts don't have a Content-Type header (standard behavior for text fields), StreamedPart::getBody() throws a deprecation warning on PHP 8.1-8.3 and a TypeError on PHP 8.4.
> 
>   Affected Version: `2.2.1` (latest)
> 
>   PHP Version: `8.4`
> 
>   Location: src/StreamedPart.php line 222
> 
>   ```
>   $contentType = $this->getHeader('Content-Type');
>   $isBinary = strtolower($contentType) === 'application/octet-stream';
> ```
>   When Content-Type header is absent, getHeader() returns null, and strtolower(null) fails.
> 
>   Reproduction:
> 
>   Parse any standard browser multipart/form-data submission. Text fields typically don't include Content-Type headers per RFC 2046:
> ```
>   ------WebKitFormBoundary
>   Content-Disposition: form-data; name="title"
> 
>   Hello World
>   ------WebKitFormBoundary
>   Content-Disposition: form-data; name="image"; filename="photo.png"
>   Content-Type: image/png
> 
>   <binary data>
>   ------WebKitFormBoundary--
> ```
>   The title field has no Content-Type — this is valid and the default browser behavior.
> 
>   Error:
>   `strtolower(): Passing null to parameter Riverline/multipart-parser#1 ($string) of type string is deprecated`
> </issue_description>
>

>

> </comments>

</details>

title: fix: prevent parent env credential forwarding to n8nac child processes
body:
When OpenClaw spawns `n8nac` via `child_process.spawn()`, omitting `env` causes the child to inherit the full parent `process.env` — including any LLM API keys held by the agent host. Combined with `n8nac` making HTTP calls to the n8n API, this correctly triggers the scanner warning: _"Environment variable access combined with network send — possible credential harvesting"_.

## Changes

- **`src/child-env.ts`** (new): shared `getChildEnv()` that builds a filtered env for child processes with the following allowlist:
  - Essential system vars: `PATH`/`Path` (case-insensitive), `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `SYSTEMROOT`, `COMSPEC`, `PATHEXT`, and other OS vars
  - Safe `npm_*` vars (e.g. `npm_execpath`, `npm_config_cache`) — **excluding** any var whose name contains `auth`, `token`, `password`, `secret`, `apikey`, `api_key`, or `_key` anywhere
  - Specific safe `NODE_*` vars: `NODE_ENV`, `NODE_NO_WARNINGS`, `NODE_ICU_DATA` — **not** a prefix match, so `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` is never forwarded
  - `N8N_AS_CODE_*` vars
- **`src/tool.ts`** (`runNpx`): pass `env: getChildEnv()` to `spawn`
- **`src/cli.ts`** (`runN8nac`): pass `env: getChildEnv()` to both `spawn` call sites
- **`tests/child-env.test.ts`** (new): 8 focused tests asserting that safe vars are forwarded and credential-like vars (LLM API keys, npm registry auth tokens, `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, etc.) are blocked

```ts
// before — implicitly inherits full process.env (including LLM keys, etc.)
const child = spawn("npx", ["--yes", "n8nac", ...args], { cwd, stdio: "pipe" });

// after — only forwards what npx/node actually needs
const child = spawn("npx", ["--yes", "n8nac", ...args], { cwd, stdio: "pipe", env: getChildEnv() });
```

`n8nac` reads its n8n credentials from `n8nac-config.json` (written by `init-auth` via stdin), so stripping the parent env does not affect functionality.

The spawn() calls in tool.ts and cli.ts inherited the full process.env from the parent (OpenClaw), which may hold sensitive LLM API keys. - Import and use getChildEnv() in both src/tool.ts and src/cli.ts spawn calls

title: Throttle repeated unaffected rows warnings in DefaultExecutionQueue
body:
## Description

During load tests, SQL statements that affect no rows generate repeated WARN messages in `DefaultExecutionQueue`, flooding logs with identical statements. 

**Changes:**

- **PerMessageThrottledLogger**: New logger wrapper that tracks throttle time per message template (not per formatted message). Uses `ConcurrentHashMap` for thread-safe per-message throttling. Implements `Supplier<Long>` for time dependency injection to enable deterministic testing. Includes null-safety and performance optimizations.

- **DefaultExecutionQueue**: Replaced direct logger with throttled logger for unaffected rows warnings. First occurrence logs immediately, subsequent identical warnings suppressed for 5 minutes.

```java
// Before: floods logs with repeated warnings
LOG.warn("[RDBMS ExecutionQueue, Partition {}] Some statements with ID {} have not affected any rows...", 
    partitionId, statementId);

// After: same warning throttled to once per 5 minutes
THROTTLED_LOG.warn("[RDBMS ExecutionQueue, Partition {}] Some statements with ID {} have not affected any rows...", 
    partitionId, statementId);
```

Unlike the existing global `ThrottledLogger` in Zeebe, this implementation throttles each unique message template independently, allowing different warnings to log without blocking each other.

**Implementation Details:**

- Throttle interval calculated once in constructor for performance
- Public constructor uses `System::currentTimeMillis` by default
- Package-private constructor accepts custom `Supplier<Long>` for testing
- Test helper methods annotated with `@VisibleForTesting`
- Tests use `AtomicLong` to control time progression without `Thread.sleep()`, making them deterministic and fast
- **Null-safe**: Ignores null messageTemplate with early return (no action taken)
- **Performance optimized**: Checks log level enabled (`isWarnEnabled()`, etc.) before updating throttle state to avoid overhead when logging is disabled
- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Enhanced assertions with `verifyNoMoreInteractions()` to prevent regressions, plus tests for null handling and disabled log levels

## Checklist

- [ ] Enable backports when necessary (fex. [for bug fixes](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#backporting-changes), [for CI changes](https://camunda.github.io/camunda/ci/#when-to-backport-ci-changes), or [for documentation changes](https://camunda.github.io/camunda/ci/#documentation-specific-backporting-monorepo-docs-folders)).

This PR introduces a per-message throttling logger utility and applies it to `DefaultExecutionQueue` to reduce log flooding from repeated “unaffected rows” WARN messages during load.
