title: Adopt unified UIKit Auto Layout approach for iOS controls
body:
iOS platform mixes layout strategies: manual `Frame` setting, `UIViewAutoresizing` masks, and `LayoutSubviews()` overrides. This replaces all of them with Auto Layout constraints as the single layout mechanism.

### New: `ConstraintHelper` utility

Internal helper (`src/Spice/Platforms/iOS/ConstraintHelper.cs`) for common constraint operations:

- `PinEdges(child, parent, insets)` — pin all 4 edges, sets `TranslatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false`
- `UpdateInsets(constraints, inset)` — update constants in-place (no constraint churn)
- `RemoveConstraints(constraints)` — deactivate a constraint set
- `ApplyAlignment(child, parent, hAlign, vAlign, margin, widthReq, heightReq)` — maps Spice layout properties to constraints

### `View.UpdateAlign()` → `ApplyConstraints()`

Replaces the manual `CGRect` frame computation (margin arithmetic, alignment switch, `SizeToFit()`) with `ConstraintHelper.ApplyAlignment()`. `UpdateAlign()` kept as alias for existing callers.

### Container migrations

- **`Application`** — `UIViewAutoresizing.All` → `UIViewAutoresizing.None` + `PinEdges` for Main view. Constraints cleaned up on Main swap.
- **`Border`** — Removed `SpiceBorderView` subclass and `LayoutSubviews`/`UpdateContentLayout` frame logic. Content pinned with constraints; `OnPaddingChanged` calls `UpdateInsets` directly.
- **`ContentView`** — Removed `SpiceContentView` subclass and `_paddingWrapper`. Same constraint pattern as Border.
- **`RefreshView`** — Removed `SpiceRefreshView` subclass and `_paddingWrapper`. Same constraint pattern.
- **`SwipeView`** — Content wrapper uses constraints instead of `AutoresizingMask = FlexibleWidth | FlexibleHeight`.

### What's unchanged

`Grid`, `ScrollView`, `StackLayout` retain their `LayoutSubviews` overrides — Grid does complex cell layout, ScrollView manages `ContentSize`, and StackLayout delegates to `UIStackView`. Leaf controls (`Label`, `Button`, `Image`, etc.) unchanged; they already set `AutoresizingMask = None` and are now positioned by the parent's constraint-based `ApplyConstraints()`.

<issue_description>Adopt unified UIKit Auto Layout approach for iOS controls (replace manual frames/autoresizing masks)

## Summary
The iOS platform implementation in Spice currently mixes layout strategies:

- Most controls initialize native views with `AutoresizingMask = UIViewAutoresizing.None` (e.g. `View`, `Border`, `BoxView`, `Label`, `StackLayout`, etc.)
- Some views set frames manually in `LayoutSubviews()` (e.g. `Border.UpdateContentLayout()` called from `SpiceBorderView.LayoutSubviews`)  
  Source: https://github.com/jonathanpeppers/spice/blob/main/src/Spice/Platforms/iOS/Border.cs
- `Application` uses autoresizing masks (`UIViewAutoresizing.All` / `FlexibleWidth|FlexibleHeight`) for root/Main behavior.

This leads to inconsistent behavior and requires each container/control to re-implement resize handling. We should migrate to a **standard UIKit Auto Layout** approach for iOS, using constraints as the single source of truth for sizing/positioning. This will be more predictable, more idiomatic UIKit, and should unify behavior across all controls.

## Goals
- Use **Auto Layout constraints** rather than:
  - manual `Frame` setting for layout
  - `UIViewAutoresizing` masks for resizing behavior
- Ensure consistent layout behavior across all iOS controls and containers.
- Make property changes (Padding, Margin, alignment, WidthRequest/HeightRequest, etc.) update constraint constants rather than re-laying out via frames.
- Reduce custom `LayoutSubviews` implementations where constraints suffice.

## Proposed design (Option B generalized)
### Core rules
1. For all iOS native views created by Spice:
   - `AutoresizingMask = UIViewAutoresizing.None`
   - `TranslatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false` when the view is placed into a parent-managed layout
2. Parents/containers are responsible for installing constraints for children when they are added.
3. Layout-related Spice properties map to constraints:
   - `Padding` (container) → constants on child pin constraints
   - `Margin` (child) → constraints from child to parent edges (or wrapper view approach)
   - `HorizontalOptions` / `VerticalOptions` → constraint strategy:
     - Fill: pin leading/trailing and/or top/bottom
     - Center: centerX/centerY (+ optional <= constraints)
     - Start/End: leading/trailing or top/bottom pins
   - `WidthRequest` / `HeightRequest` → width/height constraints with appropriate priorities

### Border specific changes
Current behavior:
- Adds content as a subview, then sets `contentView.Frame = ...` based on `Padding` and `Bounds`.
- Recomputes in `LayoutSubviews()`.

New behavior:
- When `Content` is set, add it and apply constraints:
  - Leading = Border.Leading + Padding
  - Trailing = Border.Trailing - Padding
  - Top = Border.Top + Padding
  - Bottom = Border.Bottom - Padding
- Store those four constraints and update their constants when `Padding` changes.
- Remove `UpdateContentLayout()` frame logic; `LayoutSubviews()` override should no longer be needed for content sizing.

Acceptance criteria for Border:
- Changing `Padding` updates content position/size without needing manual frame.
- Rotation/resizing updates correctly via Auto Layout.
- Replacing `Content` removes old constraints cleanly.

## Application specific changes
- Replace `UIViewAutoresizing.All` / `FlexibleWidth|FlexibleHeight` logic with constraints:
  - Root `NativeView` pinned to `UIWindow` (or to the controller’s view)
  - `Main` pinned to root `NativeView` on all edges (0 constants)
- Ensure `MainChanging/MainChanged` removes constraints when swapping the main view.

## Migration plan (incremental)
1. Introduce a small internal helper API for constraints, e.g. `ConstraintSet` utilities:
   - `PinEdges(child, parent, insets)`
   - `Center(child, parent)`
   - `SetSize(child, width?, height?, priority)`
   - `UpdateInsets(existingConstraints, insets)`
2. Migrate simple container(s) first (`Border`, `Application`) to validate the pattern.
3. Migrate remaining container controls (`RefreshView`, layouts, etc.).
4. Ensure leaf controls (Label, Image, BoxView, etc.) do not perform frame logic and can be constrained by parents.
5. Add sample / test page verifying:
   - rotations
   - dynamic content size changes
   - nested borders/padding
   - margin + fill/center behaviors

## Out of scope / open questions
- How to map Spice’s layout model exactly onto constraints (especially `Margin` + non-fill alignments) without introducing wrapper views everywhere.
- UIStackView: decide whether `StackLayout` continues using `UIStackView` arrangedSubviews (Auto Layout-friendly) but ensure constraints integrate cleanly with Spice options.
- Performance considerations: constraint churn on frequent property updates (consider updating constants vs recreating constraints).

title: fix: use domain exception pattern in ProductDetailRoute, remove PHPStan ignore
body:
`ProductDetailRoute` was throwing `new ProductNotFoundException(...)` directly, violating the domain exception pattern and requiring a PHPStan baseline suppression.

### Changes

- **`ProductException`**: Added `notFound(string $productId): ProductNotFoundException` static factory method that returns `new ProductNotFoundException($productId)`, preserving full backward compatibility for callers catching the legacy exception
- **`ProductDetailRoute`**: Replaced `throw new ProductNotFoundException($productId)` with `throw ProductException::notFound($productId)`; swapped import accordingly
- **`phpstan-baseline.neon`**: Removed the suppressed "domain exception pattern" entry for `ProductDetailRoute.php`
- **`ProductDetailRouteTest`**: Exception expectation remains `ProductNotFoundException::class` (since `notFound()` returns that type)

title: [copilot-setup-steps.yaml] Skip azure/login on user forks
body:
The `azure/login` step in `copilot-setup-steps.yaml` fails on user forks since the Workload Identity Federation credentials are only configured for the main repos.

- Add `if` condition to skip the `azure/login` step when running on forks:

```yaml
if: github.repository_owner == 'Azure'
```

title: Validate dispatch_workflow safe output functionality and add usage documentation
body:
Investigation of workflow run 21543485044 suggesting dispatch_workflow safe output is unsupported. Found all components fully implemented and functional.

## Validation Results

**Tool Generation** - `generateDispatchWorkflowTool()` creates MCP tools with `_workflow_name` metadata from `dispatch-workflow` frontmatter config

**MCP Registration** - `registerPredefinedTools()` registers tools when `config.dispatch_workflow` exists, attaches handlers that inject workflow_name

**Handler Processing** - `dispatch_workflow.cjs` validates against allowed list, enforces max limits, dispatches via `github.rest.actions.createWorkflowDispatch`

**Safe Output Flow**:
```json
{
  "type": "dispatch_workflow",
  "workflow_name": "worker-workflow",
  "inputs": {
    "campaign_id": "bootstrap-123",
    "payload": "{\"target\": \"repositories\"}"
  }
}
```
→ Handler resolves `workflow_files` mapping → Dispatches `worker-workflow.yml` or `.lock.yml`

## Test Coverage

- Go: 9 tests covering validation, file discovery, extension resolution
- JavaScript: 10+ tests covering handler factory, limits, input conversion, rate limiting
- Validation script confirms end-to-end flow in test-dispatcher.lock.yml

## Configuration Flow

```yaml
safe-outputs:
  dispatch-workflow:
    workflows: [worker-workflow]
    max: 1
```
→ Generates `worker_workflow` MCP tool → Populates `workflow_files` map → Passes to handler via `GH_AW_SAFE_OUTPUTS_HANDLER_CONFIG`

## Documentation Added

Added clear usage instructions to `test-runtime.md` workflow demonstrating how to use dispatch_workflow safe output:
- Instructions section explaining the dispatch-workflow capability
- Example JSON format for dispatching workflows with inputs
- List of available workflows that can be dispatched

No code changes required. System operational as designed. If run 21543485044 failed, likely configuration issue (workflow not in allowed list, missing `actions: write` permission, or target workflow lacks `workflow_dispatch` trigger).

title: Add OpenTelemetry metrics to connection pools with standardized naming and separate gRPC and pool metrics controls
body:
## Analysis and Implementation: Expose Pool Metrics to OpenTelemetry

✅ **All tasks completed successfully**

### Recent Changes (addressing PR review feedback)
- [x] **Standardized metrics naming across pool types** - All pools now use consistent metric suffixes (.active, .idle, .total, .pending, .max, .min) while keeping provider-specific prefixes
- [x] **Removed utilization metric** - Simplified to calculated metric: `(active/max)*100`
- [x] **Defined 6 core metrics standard** - All pool implementations should provide the same 6 core metrics with consistent naming
- [x] **Updated SPI guidance** - Clear requirements for core metrics with standardized suffixes, plus flexibility for additional provider-specific metrics
- [x] **Removed backward compatibility code** - Cleaned up legacy config key support from PoolMetricsFactory and documentation
- [x] **Added comprehensive SPI telemetry guidance**:
  - Added Step 7 to IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md explaining how to implement telemetry for custom providers
  - Added Section 12.7 to Chapter 12 (Pool Provider SPI) covering telemetry integration in detail
  - Documented standard metric naming conventions
  - Provided reference implementations for both XA and non-XA pools
  - Added configuration integration guidance
  - Included testing examples
- [x] **Updated cross-references** - Added links to telemetry documentation in SPI guides
- [x] **Updated all documentation** - METRICS.md, ebook chapters, and SPI guides reflect standardized naming

### All Previous Implementation
- [x] Fixed HikariCP metrics implementation
- [x] Fixed gRPC metrics control
- [x] Enhanced logging for debugging
- [x] Virtual threads for housekeeping (Java 21+)
- [x] OpenTelemetryHolder for global instance
- [x] Separate metrics control flags
- [x] Renamed master switch to ojp.telemetry.enabled
- [x] System properties reading in PoolMetricsFactory

### Implementation Complete
- [x] 12 metrics for XA pools: 6 core + 6 additional (gauges + counters)
- [x] 6 core metrics for HikariCP pools (gauges)
- [x] Consistent suffix naming across all pool types
- [x] PoolMetrics interface abstraction
- [x] NoOp and OpenTelemetry implementations
- [x] PoolMetricsFactory (simplified, no legacy keys)
- [x] OpenTelemetryHolder for global instance
- [x] MetricsAwareHousekeepingListener
- [x] Integration with OjpServerTelemetry
- [x] HikariCP MetricsTrackerFactory integration

### Documentation Complete
- [x] **METRICS.md**: Comprehensive reference with standardized naming, calculation note for utilization
- [x] **Chapter 13 (Telemetry)**: Section 13.5 on connection pool metrics with standardized naming
- [x] **Chapter 6 (Server Configuration)**: Enhanced OpenTelemetry section (removed outdated tracing note, use fully qualified flags)
- [x] **Chapter 12 (Pool Provider SPI)**: Section 12.7 "Implementing Telemetry for Custom Providers" with standardized naming requirements
- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md**: Step 7 on OpenTelemetry integration with naming examples
- [x] **All tests pass** (361 tests total, Java 21 environment required for ojp-xa-pool-commons)

### Configuration (Simplified - No Legacy Keys)

**Recommended JVM arguments:**
```bash
-Dojp.telemetry.enabled=true                       # Master switch
-Dojp.telemetry.grpc.metrics.enabled=true         # gRPC metrics (default: true)
-Dojp.telemetry.pool.metrics.enabled=true         # Pool metrics (default: true)
-Dojp.prometheus.port=9159
-Dojp.prometheus.allowedIps=127.0.0.1,10.0.0.0/8
```

**Configuration keys (no backward compatibility):**
- `ojp.telemetry.pool.metrics.enabled` - Enable/disable pool metrics
- `ojp.xa.poolName` - Set custom pool name for XA pools

### Metrics Available

**XA Pool Core Metrics (ojp.xa.pool.connections.*):**
- active, idle, total, pending, max, min

**XA Pool Additional Metrics (ojp.xa.pool.connections.*):**
- created, destroyed, exhausted, validation.failed, leaks.detected, acquisition.time, acquisition.count

**HikariCP Pool Metrics (ojp.hikari.pool.connections.*):**
- active, idle, total, pending, max, min

**Note:** Pool utilization can be calculated as: `(active / max) * 100`

All metrics tagged with `pool.name` attribute.

### Standardized Naming Convention

All connection pool implementations follow a consistent naming pattern:
- **Format**: `ojp.<provider>.pool.connections.<metric>`
- **Core metrics** (required for all implementations): active, idle, total, pending, max, min
- **Additional metrics**: Providers can add implementation-specific metrics beyond the core set

This standardization enables:
- Consistent monitoring dashboards across all pool types
- Universal alerting rules that work with any pool implementation
- Easy comparison of pool behavior across different providers
- Clear expectations for custom SPI implementations

### Technical Notes

This module targets Java 21 and runs exclusively in ojp-server. All legacy backward compatibility code has been removed for cleaner maintainability. Custom SPI implementations now have comprehensive guidance on integrating with OJP's telemetry system, with clear requirements for the 6 core metrics using standardized suffixes, while allowing flexibility for provider-specific additional metrics.

> @copilot+claude-sonnet-4.5 do we still need a ojp.opentelemetry.enabled? just answer, don't change code.

Yes, `ojp.opentelemetry.enabled` is still needed for these reasons:

1. **Master switch**: It controls whether to initialize the OpenTelemetry SDK and Prometheus server at all. When false, the system uses no-op telemetry with zero overhead.

2. **Infrastructure setup**: It determines whether to create the PrometheusHttpServer, MeterProvider, and TracerProvider - regardless of which specific metrics are enabled.

3. **Resource management**: When disabled, no telemetry infrastructure is started (no Prometheus port opened, no exporters initialized), saving resources.

The two granular flags (`ojp.telemetry.grpc.metrics.enabled` and `ojp.telemetry.pool.metrics.enabled`) only control which metrics are collected *within* an already-initialized OpenTelemetry system. You could potentially simplify by inferring that if OpenTelemetry is enabled but both metric flags are false, don't initialize the infrastructure - but keeping the master switch provides clearer **Issue 2: Pool metrics not appearing - Likely causes:**

1. **Configuration key**: Ensure you're using `-Dojp.telemetry.enabled=true` (NOT `ojp.opentelemetry.enabled`)

2. **Pool operations**: XA pool metrics only appear when database operations occur. If you haven't executed queries that create XA connections, there won't be any pool metrics. Try running queries that use the XA datasource.

3. **Check logs**: Look for these messages in server logs:
   - `"OpenTelemetry instance registered for pool metrics"`  
   - `"Creating OpenTelemetry metrics for XA pool: <poolname>"`
   
   If you don't see these, the OpenTelemetry instance isn't being registered or pools aren't being created.

4. **Metrics naming**: XA pool metrics use prefix `ojp_xa_pool_connections_*`, HikariCP uses `ojp_hikari_pool_connections_*`. Search for those specifically.

> @copilot I see that hikari CP and XA metrics are different, I imagine that the reason might be that we use the Apache commons pool 2 and that provides different metrics, is that the reason? would it b...

You're correct about the reason for the differences. The XA pool implementation uses Apache Commons Pool 2, which provides different metrics than HikariCP's native pooling implementation.

**Key Differences:**

**XA Pools (13 metrics):**
- More granular event counters (exhausted, validation.failed, leaks.detected, acquisition time/count)
- Utilization gauge (calculated metric)
- Created/destroyed gauges (lifetime totals)
- These extra metrics come from Commons Pool 2's comprehensive statistics API

**HikariCP (6 metrics):**
- Simpler metric set focused on pool state
- Includes total connections (active + idle) which XA doesn't have
- No event counters - HikariCP's MetricsTrackerFactory only provides state snapshots
- Cleaner, more focused metric set

**Could we align them?**

**YES** - We could standardize on HikariCP's simpler metric set. Here's what we'd lose and gain:

**LOSE from XA pools:**
- `utilization` (easily calculated: `active/max * 100`)
- `created` and `destroyed` (lifetime totals, useful for debugging pool churn)
- Event counters: `exhausted`, `validation.failed`, `leaks.detected` (valuable for alerting)
- `acquisition.time` and `acquisition.count` (performance tracking)

**GAIN:**
- Consistency across all pool types
- Simpler metric set, easier to understand
- `total` connections metric (active + idle)

**LOSE that's important:**
- **Event counters are valuable** - pool exhaustion, validation failures, and leak detection are critical for production monitoring and alerting
- **Acquisition time tracking** helps identify performance bottlenecks

**My recommendation:** Keep both as-is. The differences reflect the underlying pool implementations' capabilities. Operators monitoring XA pools benefit from the additional event counters and performance metrics that Commons Pool 2 provides. The utilization metric, while derivable, is convenient for quick dashboards.

title: Add --no-watch flag to disable config file auto-restart
body:
Dev Proxy watches `devproxyrc.json` and auto-restarts on changes. This is a race condition hazard for AI agents that modify config programmatically — the proxy restarts unexpectedly mid-workflow.

Adds `--no-watch` flag that suppresses `FileSystemWatcher` setup in `ConfigFileWatcher`, preventing config-change-triggered restarts.

- **`IProxyConfiguration` / `ProxyConfiguration`** — `NoWatch` property (default `false`)
- **`DevProxyCommand`** — `--no-watch` option, wired through `ConfigureFromOptions`
- **`ConfigFileWatcher.StartAsync`** — early return when `NoWatch` is set, skipping watcher creation

```
devproxy --no-watch
```

Since the watcher is never created, `IsRestarting` stays `false` and the restart loop in `Program.cs` exits naturally — no changes needed there.

> <issue_description>Parent: dotnet/dev-proxy#1534

> ## Problem
> 
> Dev Proxy watches `devproxyrc.json` for changes and auto-restarts when the config file is modified. This is convenient for human developers but is a hazard for AI agents that modify configuration files programmatically.
> 
> An agent that:
> 1. Starts Dev Proxy
> 2. Modifies `devproxyrc.json` to change plugin settings
> 3. Continues testing
> 
> ...will trigger an unexpected proxy restart in step 2. The agent doesn't know the restart is happening, the proxy is temporarily unavailable, and in-flight requests may be lost.
> 
> There's no flag to disable this behavior.
> 
> ## Rationale
> 
> Agents need predictable behavior. An agent-driven workflow might involve modifying config between test runs or dynamically adjusting proxy settings. The auto-restart feature, while helpful for humans iterating in a terminal, creates a race condition for automated callers.
> 
> ## Proposed solution
> 
> 1. **Add a `--no-watch` flag** (or `--watch false`) to the root command that disables config file watching:
>    ```
>    --no-watch  Disable automatic restart on configuration file changes
>    ```
> 
> 2. **When `--no-watch` is set**, config changes require a manual restart (which is what agents expect — explicit control).
> 
> 3. **Document this behavior** in root `--help` — agents need to know about auto-restart even if they don't use `--no-watch`, so they can plan around it.
> 
> ## Affected code
> 
> - `DevProxy/Commands/DevProxyCommand.cs` — add `--no-watch` option
> - `DevProxy/Proxy/ConfigFileWatcher.cs` (or equivalent) — respect the flag
> - `DevProxy/Program.cs` — pass flag through restart loop

title: fix: restore Node.js 22 support and prevent future version bumps
body:
Version 7.1.1 introduced a breaking change by requiring Node.js `>=24.12.0`, breaking compatibility with Node.js 22 LTS (EOL 2027-04-30).

## Changes

- Updated `package.json` engines field from `"node": ">=24.12.0"` to `"node": ">=22.0.0"`
- Configured Renovate to restrict Node.js updates to 22.x by adding `packageRules` with `allowedVersions: "22.x"`
- Aligns with existing `.nvmrc` file which specifies Node.js 22.21.1

This restores Node.js 22 support while maintaining compatibility with Node.js 24+, and prevents Renovate from automatically suggesting updates to Node.js 24 or higher in the future.

title: [release/10.0] Fix GO batch separator not recognized in comments and escaped identifiers
body:
Fixes #37494

**Description**

EF Core splits SQL Server migration scripts into batches on lines starting with GO. To avoid splitting inside string literals, SqlServerMigrationsSqlGenerator tracks whether it is inside a quoted string.

The implementation does not handle standard SQL block comments (/* ... */). If a block comment contains a single quote, the quoted state is incorrectly toggled even though the quote is inside a comment. Since there is no matching closing quote, quoted toggle remains true across subsequent lines. As a result, a later GO line is not recognized as a batch separator and is sent to SQL Server as literal text, causing:

`Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.SqlException: Incorrect syntax near 'go'.`

**Customer impact**

Customers using SQL migrations with stored procedures or other SQL scripts that include block comments containing single quotes will experience migration failures with "Incorrect syntax near 'go'" errors. This can occur when documentation comments in SQL scripts use contractions or possessives (e.g., "It's", "user's").

Workarounds:
- Remove single quotes from block comments
- Use two single quotes in block comments to escape them

**How found**

Customer reported on 10.0.1

**Regression**

Yes, from EF Core 9.0. Introduced in #34917.

**Testing**

Added 31 tests covering:
- Block comments with single quotes (single-line and multi-line)
- Line comments with block comment markers
- Empty block comments
- Block comments with line comments inside
- Escaped identifiers with square brackets `[GO]` and double quotes `"GO"`
- Escaped closing brackets in identifiers `[g]]o]`
- Escaped double quotes in identifiers `"go""lum"`
- **Multi-line escaped identifiers spanning newlines with `go` text inside** (e.g., `INSERT INTO "\ngo\n" VALUES (1)`)
- All character combinations (quotes, slashes, asterisks, dashes, brackets) preceding GO
- Line comments (`--`) inside quotes and escaped identifiers
- **Unclosed delimiters within block comments** (e.g., `/* [bracket */` - valid SQL since comments don't require matched delimiters)
- **Unclosed delimiters within line comments** (e.g., `-- [column` - valid SQL since line comments end at EOL)
- Single quotes inside block comments
- All delimiter types inside line comments
- Escaped quotes in strings (`'test''s value'`)
- Multiple delimiters in strings

**Risk**

Medium, because the fix entails changes to a parser, so all the possible consequences aren't as clear. However, the changes only affect custom SQL operations in migrations.

title: feat: decode and track scoreboard Teams packets in modern protocol path
body:
`PacketTypesIn.Teams` was mapped in every palette but Protocol18 had no decode logic — the packet was silently dropped, leaving team state invisible at runtime.

## Changes

### Protocol (`Protocol18.cs`)
- Adds `case PacketTypesIn.Teams:` with full decode for all methods (0=create, 1=remove, 2=update, 3=add players, 4=remove players)
- **Pre-1.21.9 (< protocol 773):** `nameTagVisibility` and `collisionRule` read as UTF-40 strings
- **1.21.9+ (≥ 773):** both fields read as VarInt enum IDs (STREAM_CODEC) and mapped to canonical strings (`"always"`, `"never"`, `"hideForOtherTeams"`, `"hideForOwnTeam"` / `"pushOtherTeams"`, `"pushOwnTeam"`)
- Component fields (`displayName`, `prefix`, `suffix`) use `ReadNextChat()`, which already handles pre/post-1.20.4 JSON vs NBT wire format internally

### Domain model (`Mapping/PlayerTeam.cs`)
New class holding all team fields and a `HashSet<string> Members`.

### Runtime state (`McClient.cs`)
- `teams` dictionary (lock-guarded) updated on every `OnTeam()` call
- `GetTeams()` returns a shallow snapshot; `GetPlayerTeam(string playerName)` reverse-scans for a player's team

### Bot API (`Scripting/ChatBot.cs`, `Protocol/IMinecraftComHandler.cs`)
`virtual OnTeam(teamName, method, displayName, friendlyFlags, nameTagVisibility, collisionRule, color, prefix, suffix, players)` callback following the same pattern as `OnScoreboardObjective` / `OnUpdateScore`.

### Command (`Commands/Teams.cs`)
`/teams` lists all tracked teams with their parameters and member counts, auto-discovered via reflection like all other commands.

### Translations
Five new `cmd.teams.*` keys added to `Translations.resx` and `Translations.Designer.cs`.

## Usage

```csharp
// In a ChatBot subclass
public override void OnTeam(string teamName, byte method, string displayName,
    byte friendlyFlags, string nameTagVisibility, string collisionRule,
    int color, string prefix, string suffix, List<string> players)
{
    if (method == 0) // team created
        LogToConsole($"New team: {teamName}, members: {string.Join(", ", players)}");
}

// Query at any time
var myTeam = Handler.GetPlayerTeam("SomePlayer"); // null if not on a team
var allTeams = Handler.GetTeams();                 // snapshot dictionary
```

title: Propagate create-discussion errors to conclusion job failure tracking
body:
## Summary: Propagate create-discussion Errors to Conclusion Job

### Problem
When a create-discussion safe output fails, the error is not propagated to the agent failure tracking in the conclusion job, so failures are not reported in tracking issues/comments.

Reference: https://github.com/github/gh-aw/actions/runs/21615216168/job/62293027909#step:6:1

### Solution
Implemented error tracking for create_discussion following the same pattern as assign_to_agent. All code review feedback addressed.

### Implementation Complete ✅

- [x] Track failed create_discussion messages in safe_output_handler_manager.cjs
- [x] Export create_discussion_errors and create_discussion_error_count as outputs
- [x] Add outputs to safe_outputs job in compiler_safe_outputs_job.go
- [x] Pass errors as environment variables to conclusion job in notify_comment.go  
- [x] Update handle_agent_failure.cjs to include create_discussion errors in issue/comment
- [x] Update agent failure templates to include create_discussion_errors_context
- [x] Add comprehensive tests
- [x] Fix code review feedback (remove unused variables)
- [x] Refactor duplicate code into helper function
- [x] Merge main branch and recompile workflows
- [x] All tests pass

### Changes Made

#### JavaScript Changes
1. **safe_output_handler_manager.cjs**: Collect and export create_discussion errors
2. **handle_agent_failure.cjs**: Display create_discussion errors with helper function (merged with main branch checkout PR changes)
3. **Agent failure templates**: Include create_discussion_errors_context

#### Go Changes
1. **compiler_safe_outputs_job.go**: Add error outputs to safe_outputs job
2. **notify_comment.go**: Pass errors to conclusion job as environment variables

#### Tests
- Comprehensive test coverage in handle_agent_failure.test.cjs
- All existing tests continue to pass

This ensures create_discussion failures are properly tracked and reported in failure tracking issues/comments.

title: ci: update workflow runners and submodule checkout
body:
## Summary
Fix CI workflow failures caused by missing `iris.c` submodule checkout, and apply follow-up workflow updates requested in review.

## What changed
- Updated `.github/workflows/ci.yml` checkout step to fetch submodules recursively.
- Updated `.github/workflows/gated-checkin.yml` checkout step to fetch submodules recursively.
- Updated both workflow build jobs to run on `macos-26`.
- Added explicit least-privilege workflow permissions (`contents: read`) to satisfy Actions security checks.

## Root cause
The build failed at `Mochi Diffusion/Iris-BridgingHeader.h` because it imports `../iris.c/iris.h`, but `actions/checkout@v6.0.2` was running with `submodules: false` by default, so `iris.c/iris.h` did not exist in the workflow workspace.

## Validation
- Investigated failed run logs (`run_id: 23517333432`) and confirmed missing header error.
- Confirmed workflow diffs are minimal and targeted.
- Validated workflow YAML parses successfully after updates.
- Ran automated code review: no issues.
- Ran CodeQL security scan and resolved flagged workflow permission issues.
- Re-ran CodeQL security scan: no alerts.

## Security Summary
CodeQL initially flagged missing explicit `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions in the edited workflows. Added `permissions: { contents: read }` to affected jobs and verified no remaining alerts.

title: Dispose backing streams and skip entries on extraction failure in TarExtractor and ZipExtractor
body:
TarExtractor and ZipExtractor caught exceptions during entry extraction but continued processing, creating FileEntries with empty/corrupted streams and leaking backing stream resources.

## Changes

**TarExtractor.cs** (both sync/async):
- Dispose backing stream on extraction failure
- Skip to next entry instead of creating FileEntry

**ZipExtractor.cs** (both sync/async):
- Dispose backing stream on extraction failure  
- Skip to next entry instead of creating FileEntry
- Remove empty MemoryStream fallback in async method
- Remove `using` declaration in sync method (stream ownership transfers to FileEntry)
- Use `passthroughStream: true` parameter to avoid unnecessary stream copying and reduce allocations

```csharp
// Before: continued processing on failure
catch (Exception e)
{
    Logger.Debug(...);
}
var newFileEntry = new FileEntry(name, fs, ...); // fs may be empty/corrupted

// After: clean up and skip
catch (Exception e)
{
    Logger.Debug(...);
    fs?.Dispose();
    continue;
}
```

Aligns with RarExtractor's pattern of skipping failed entries rather than returning entries with indeterminate content. The use of `passthroughStream: true` in ZipExtractor matches the pattern already used in TarExtractor, avoiding redundant stream copies since the backing stream is already populated.

title: Remove unused pillow dependency from all requirements files
body:
### Changes

Removed unused pillow dependency from all requirements.txt files in `examples/llm_compression/`:

- `onnx/tiny_llama/requirements.txt`
- `onnx/tiny_llama_scale_estimation/requirements.txt`
- `openvino/tiny_llama/requirements.txt`
- `openvino/tiny_llama_find_hyperparams/requirements.txt`
- `openvino/tiny_llama_synthetic_data/requirements.txt`
- `openvino/smollm2_360m_codebook/requirements.txt`
- `openvino/smollm2_360m_fp8/requirements.txt`
- `openvino/smollm2_360m_adaptive_codebook/requirements.txt`
- `torch/downstream_qat_with_nls/requirements.txt`
- `torch/distillation_qat_with_lora/requirements.txt`

Analysis confirmed that none of the main.py files or other Python files in these directories import or use the pillow/PIL package.

### Reason for changes

The pillow package was listed as a dependency but was not actually used by any of the example code. Removing unused dependencies reduces the attack surface, simplifies dependency management, and avoids unnecessary package installations.

### Related tickets

N/A

### Tests

No functional changes to code. Code review completed with no issues. The examples will continue to function correctly without pillow as it was never used.

<issue_description>## Goal and Rationale

**Goal:** Implement automated benchmark regression testing infrastructure to detect performance regressions in CI.

**Why This Matters:**
- Performance regressions can silently degrade user experience without being noticed
- Manual benchmark comparisons are error-prone and often skipped during reviews
- Automated testing ensures every PR is evaluated for performance impact
- Statistical comparison provides confidence in distinguishing real changes from measurement noise
- Addresses **Phase 1 Priority devantler-tech/ksail#2** from the roadmap: Performance testing infrastructure
- Closes issue devantler-tech/ksail#2220 which had been marked as completed but lacked actual implementation

## Approach

### Implementation Strategy

**1. CI Workflow Creation** - Added `.github/workflows/benchmark-regression.yaml`:
- Triggers automatically on all PRs that modify Go code (`**/*.go`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`)
- Runs benchmarks on both PR branch and `main` branch for comparison
- Uses `benchstat` for rigorous statistical analysis (t-test) to detect significant changes
- Posts results as PR comments with automatic updates on new pushes
- Includes comprehensive interpretation guide in every comment

**2. Comprehensive Documentation** - Created `docs/BENCHMARK-REGRESSION.md`:
- Explains the automated testing system and how it works
- Provides detailed guidance on interpreting benchmark results
- Covers statistical significance (p-values, confidence intervals)
- Documents local benchmark workflows for pre-submission testing
- Includes troubleshooting section for common issues
- Describes best practices for writing effective benchmarks
- Outlines future enhancement opportunities

**3. Integration with Contributing Guide** - Updated `CONTRIBUTING.md`:
- Added reference to automated regression testing in the Benchmarks section
- Links to detailed documentation for developers
- Maintains consistency with existing documentation style

### Technical Details

**Workflow Features:**
- Multiple benchmark iterations (`count=5`) for statistical validity
- Extended benchmark time (`benchtime=3s`) for measurement accuracy
- Smart comment management (updates existing comment instead of creating duplicates)
- Detailed result interpretation guide embedded in every PR comment
- Proper error handling for benchmark failures

**Benchmark Process:**
1. Checkout PR branch → run benchmarks → save results
2. Checkout main branch → run benchmarks → establish baseline
3. Compare with `benchstat` → generate statistical comparison
4. Post/update PR comment with formatted markdown report

**Current Benchmark Coverage:**
- `pkg/apis/cluster/v1alpha1/marshal_bench_test.go`: YAML marshaling performance
- `pkg/cli/cmd/cipher/cipher_bench_test.go`: Encryption/decryption operations
- `pkg/k8s/readiness/polling_bench_test.go`: Kubernetes resource polling efficiency

## Impact

### What Changed

✅ **Automated Performance Monitoring:**
- Every PR with Go code changes receives automatic benchmark comparison
- Statistical analysis distinguishes real performance changes from measurement noise
- Results posted directly to PRs for immediate visibility to reviewers and authors
- Reduces cognitive load on reviewers by automating performance evaluation

✅ **Developer Guidance:**
- Clear documentation on reading and interpreting benchmark results
- Understanding of statistical significance (p-values, confidence levels)
- Local workflow for testing performance before pushing
- Troubleshooting section for addressing common benchmark issues
- Best practices for writing effective benchmarks

✅ **Foundation for Future Work:**
- Baseline storage capability outlined for historical comparison
- Threshold-based failure path identified for enforcing performance requirements
- Performance trend tracking opportunity documented
- Selective benchmarking approach described for optimization

### Files Modified

- `.github/workflows/benchmark-regression.yaml` (NEW) - Automated CI workflow
- `docs/BENCHMARK-REGRESSION.md` (NEW) - Comprehensive documentation (8,681 bytes)
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` (MODIFIED) - Added reference to regression testing

## Validation

### Acceptance Criteria from devantler-tech/ksail#2220

✅ **Baseline benchmarks established** - Main branch benchmarks serve as dynamic baseline  
✅ **CI job runs benchmarks on PRs** - `benchmark-regression.yaml` workflow executes automatically  
✅ **Performance comparison posted to PRs** - Via github-script action with smart comment management  
✅ **Documentation for interpreting results** - Comprehensive guide in `docs/BENCHMARK-REGRESSION.md`

**Note:** Configurable threshold-based failure is documented as a future enhancement. This keeps the initial implementation simple and allows teams to establish baseline expectations before enforcing ...

+# Benchmark Regression Testing
+
+KSail includes automated benchmark regression testing to detect performance changes in pull requests that modify Go code.
+
+## How It Works
+
+The [benchmark-regression](../.github/workflows/benchmark-regression.yaml) workflow runs automatically on PRs that change `**/*.go`, `go.mod`, or `go.sum` files. It:
+
+1. Runs all Go benchmarks on the PR branch (5 iterations, 3 s per benchmark)
+2. Runs the same benchmarks on `main` to establish a baseline
+3. Compares results with [`benchstat`](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/perf/cmd/benchstat) for statistical analysis
+4. Posts (or updates) a comparison comment on the PR
+
+## Interpreting Results
+
+`benchstat` output contains three key columns per benchmark:
+
+| Column        | Meaning                        | Goal            |
+|---------------|--------------------------------|-----------------|
+| **sec/op**    | Time per operation             | Lower is better |
+| **B/op**      | Bytes allocated per operation  | Lower is better |
+| **allocs/op** | Heap allocations per operation | Lower is better |
+
+Each row shows `old` (main) vs `new` (PR) with a delta percentage and a p-value:
+
+- **p < 0.05** — statistically significant change (highlighted by `benchstat`)
+- **~ (p ≥ 0.05)** — no significant change; difference is within measurement noise
+
+A positive delta in sec/op or B/op indicates a regression; a negative delta indicates an improvement.
+
+## Running Benchmarks Locally
+
+```bash
+# Run all benchmarks
+go test -bench=. -benchmem -run=^$ ./...
+
+# Run a specific package
+go test -bench=. -benchmem -run=^$ ./pkg/k8s/readiness/...
+
+# Compare before/after with benchstat
+go test -bench=. -benchmem -count=5 -run=^$ ./... > before.txt
+# (make changes)
+go test -bench=. -benchmem -count=5 -run=^$ ./... > after.txt
+benchstat before.txt after.txt
+```
+
+Install `benchstat` if needed:
+
+```bash
+go install golang.org/x/perf/cmd/benchstat@latest
+```

+# Benchmark Regression Testing
+
+KSail includes automated benchmark regression testing to detect performance changes in pull requests that modify Go code.
+
+## How It Works
+
+The [benchmark-regression](../.github/workflows/benchmark-regression.yaml) workflow runs automatically on PRs that change `**/*.go`, `go.mod`, or `go.sum` files. It:
+
+1. Runs all Go benchmarks on the PR branch (5 iterations, 3 s per benchmark)
+2. Runs the same benchmarks on `main` to establish a baseline
+3. Compares results with [`benchstat`](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/perf/cmd/benchstat) for statistical analysis
+4. Posts (or updates) a comparison comment on the PR
+
+## Interpreting Results
+
+`benchstat` output contains three key columns per benchmark:
+
+| Column        | Meaning                        | Goal            |
+|---------------|--------------------------------|-----------------|
+| **sec/op**    | Time per operation             | Lower is better |
+| **B/op**      | Bytes allocated per operation  | Lower is better |
+| **allocs/op** | Heap allocations per operation | Lower is better |
+
+Each row shows `old` (main) vs `new` (PR) with a delta percentage and a p-value:
+
+- **p < 0.05** — statistically significant change (highlighted by `benchstat`)
+- **~ (p ≥ 0.05)** — no significant change; difference is within measurement noise
+
+A positive delta in sec/op or B/op indicates a regression; a negative delta indicates an improvement.
+
+## Running Benchmarks Locally
+
+```bash
+# Run all benchmarks
+go test -bench=. -benchmem -run=^$ ./...
+
+# Run a specific package
+go test -bench=. -benchmem -run=^$ ./pkg/k8s/readiness/...
+
+# Compare before/after with benchstat
+go test -bench=. -benchmem -count=5 -run=^$ ./... > before.txt
+# (make changes)
+go test -bench=. -benchmem -count=5 -run=^$ ./... > after.txt
+benchstat before.txt after.txt
+```
+
+Install `benchstat` if needed:
+
+```bash
+go install golang.org/x/perf/cmd/benchstat@latest
+```
+

title: [docs] Add copilot instructions for repository onboarding
body:
Adds `.github/copilot-instructions.md` to reduce agent exploration time and build failures through comprehensive onboarding documentation.

## Content Structure

- **Repository Overview**: Monorepo layout (graphql backend, React frontend, Python client, worker), tech stack (Node ≥20, Python 3.9-3.12, Yarn 4.12.0)
- **Critical Build Requirements**: 
  - Corepack enablement requirement (Yarn 4.12.0 vs global 1.22)
  - `.yarnrc.yml` copy procedure (security policies: disabled scripts, 3-day NPM age gate)
  - Component-specific build sequences with timing estimates
- **CI/CD Workflows**: 5-workflow pipeline (Docker build, API tests, frontend tests, Python matrix tests, license check)
- **Project Structure**: Directory tree with key files (configs, test suites, linting files)
- **Code Review & Security**: Comprehensive review guidelines including:
  - Security critical issues (hardcoded secrets, SQL injection, XSS, input validation, authentication logic)
  - Performance red flags (N+1 queries, inefficient loops, memory leaks, caching opportunities)
  - Code quality essentials (focused functions, clear naming, error handling)
  - Review style guidelines (specific feedback, explain rationale, acknowledge patterns)
  - Readability improvement examples with code samples
  - Pre-commit checks (linting, type checking, testing)
  - CodeQL security scanning information
- **Common Pitfalls**: 6 documented failure modes with workarounds (missing Python deps, build OOM, ElasticSearch setup, unsigned commits)

## Key Discoveries

Testing revealed two critical blockers:
1. `corepack enable` required before any yarn command (package.json specifies 4.12.0, system has 1.22)
2. `.yarnrc.yml` must be copied from parent to working directory (enforces security policies that break default behavior)

## Constraints

File optimized to 1.70 pages (850 words, 189 lines) per 2-page requirement.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Your task is to "onboard" this repository to Copilot coding agent by adding a .github/copilot-instructions.md file in the repository that contains information describing how a coding agent seeing it for the first time can work most efficiently.

You will do this task only one time per repository and doing a good job can SIGNIFICANTLY improve the quality of the agent's work, so take your time, think carefully, and search thoroughly before writing the instructions.

<Goals>
- Reduce the likelihood of a coding agent pull request getting rejected by the user due to
generating code that fails the continuous integration build, fails a validation pipeline, or
having misbehavior.
- Minimize bash command and build failures.
- Allow the agent to complete its task more quickly by minimizing the need for exploration using grep, find, str_replace_editor, and code search tools.
</Goals>

<Limitations>
- Instructions must be no longer than 2 pages.
- Instructions must not be task specific.
</Limitations>

<WhatToAdd>

Add the following high level details about the codebase to reduce the amount of searching the agent has to do to understand the codebase each time:
<HighLevelDetails>

- A summary of what the repository does.
- High level repository information, such as the size of the repo, the type of the project, the languages, frameworks, or target runtimes in use.
</HighLevelDetails>

Add information about how to build and validate changes so the agent does not need to search and find it each time.
<BuildInstructions>

- For each of bootstrap, build, test, run, lint, and any other scripted step, document the sequence of steps to take to run it successfully as well as the versions of any runtime or build tools used.
- Each command should be validated by running it to ensure that it works correctly as well as any preconditions and postconditions.
- Try cleaning the repo and environment and running commands in different orders and document errors and misbehavior observed as well as any steps used to mitigate the problem.
- Run the tests and document the order of steps required to run the tests.
- Make a change to the codebase. Document any unexpected build issues as well as the workarounds.
- Document environment setup steps that seem optional but that you have validated are actually required.
- Document the time required for commands that failed due to timing out.
- When you find a sequence of commands that work for a particular purpose, document them in detail.
- Use language to indicate when something should always be done. For example: "always run npm install before building".
- Record any validation steps from documentation.
</BuildInstructions>

List key facts about the layout and architecture of the codebase to help the agent find where to make changes with minimal searching.
<ProjectLayout>

- A description of the major architectural elements of the project, including the relative paths to the main project files, the location
of configuration files for linting, compilation, testing, and preferences.
- A description of the checks run prior to check in, including any GitHub workflows, continuous integration builds, or other validation pipelines.
- Document the steps so that the agent can replicate these itself.
- Any explicit validation steps that the agent can consider to have further confidence in its changes.
- Dependencies that aren't obvious from the layout or file structure.
- Finally, fill in any remaining space with detailed lists of the following, in order of priority: the list of files in the repo root, the
contents of the README, the contents of any key source files, the list of files in the next level down of directories, giving priority to the more structurally important and snippets of code from key source files, such as the one containing the main method.
</ProjectLayout>
</WhatToAdd>

<StepsToFollow>
- Perform a comprehensive inventory of the codebase. Search for and view:
- README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and all other documentation files.
- Search the codebase for build steps and indications of workarounds like 'HACK', 'TODO', etc.
- All scripts, particularly those pertaining to build and repo or environment setup.
- All build and actions pipelines.
- All project files.
- All configuration and linting files.
- For each file:
- think: are the contents or the existence of the file information that the coding agent will need to implement, build, test, validate, or demo a code change?
- If yes:
   - Document the command or information in detail.
   - Explicitly indicate which commands work and which do not and the order in which commands should be run.
   - Document any errors encountered as well as the steps taken to workaround them.
- Document any other steps or information that the agent can use to reduce time spent exploring or trying and failing to run bash commands.
- Finally, explicitly instruct the agent to trust the instructions and only perform a search if the information in the instructions is...

</details>



<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT TIPS -->
---

💡 You can make Copilot smarter by setting up custom instructions, customizing its development environment and configuring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Learn more [Copilot coding agent tips](https://gh.io/copilot-coding-agent-tips) in the docs.

title: Consolidate duplicate SonarCloud analysis into a single CI step
body:
The `sonarcloud.yml` workflow was uploading two separate Sonar analyses per run: one in "Build and analyze" and a second in "Code Coverage" (`mvn sonar:sonar -Pcoverage`), causing duplicate SonarCloud uploads and unnecessary CI time.

## Changes

- **Merged both steps** into a single "Build, collect coverage and analyze" step
- **Simplified Maven command**: `mvn clean verify org.sonarsource.scanner.maven:sonar-maven-plugin:sonar`
  - Dropped redundant `install` phase (not needed for SonarCloud)
  - Dropped `-Pcoverage` (no such profile exists in `pom.xml`; JaCoCo is configured globally in `<build><plugins>` and generates XML reports during `verify`)
- **Moved `/etc/hosts` setup** before the Maven step so `host.testcontainers.internal` resolves during the `verify` phase

```yaml
# Before: two separate steps
- name: Build and analyze
  env:
    SONAR_TOKEN: de1b5cc660cd210dde840f492c371da6cc801763
  run: mvn clean install verify org.sonarsource.scanner.maven:sonar-maven-plugin:sonar
- name: Code Coverage
  env:
    SONAR_TOKEN: de1b5cc660cd210dde840f492c371da6cc801763
  run: mvn sonar:sonar -Pcoverage

# After: single step
- name: Build, collect coverage and analyze
  env:
    SONAR_TOKEN: de1b5cc660cd210dde840f492c371da6cc801763
    GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  run: mvn clean verify org.sonarsource.scanner.maven:sonar-maven-plugin:sonar
```

title: feat: set minimum timeout when `detectPromptInjection` rule present
body:
Extracts the inline timeout computation from `createClient.decide` into a standalone `decideTimeout` function and enforces a 1s minimum timeout when a `PROMPT_INJECTION_DETECTION` rule is configured.

- **`protocol/client.ts`**: New `decideTimeout(timeout, rules)` function replaces inline logic. Scans rules via boolean flags, doubles timeout for `EMAIL` (unchanged), enforces `Math.max(result, 1_000)` for `PROMPT_INJECTION_DETECTION`. Marked `@internal`.
- **`protocol/test/client.test.ts`**: 7 unit tests covering no rules, unrelated rules, email-only, prompt injection below/above 1s, and both rules combined.

```ts
decideTimeout(500, []);                                    // 500
decideTimeout(500, [emailRule]);                            // 1000 (doubled)
decideTimeout(500, [promptInjectionRule]);                  // 1000 (minimum enforced)
decideTimeout(2000, [promptInjectionRule]);                 // 2000 (already above minimum)
decideTimeout(750, [emailRule, promptInjectionRule]);        // 1500 (doubled > minimum)
```

title: [coro] Wire ExceptionHandler return value through coroutine throw paths
body:
This PR continues the ExceptionHandler integration by making generated coroutine code consume the value returned by `startException`, instead of discarding it.  
It also removes an eval/threaded edge where reading unset TLS could crash during exception processing.

- **Problem scope**
  - `BaseContinuation.startException` returns `Exception`, but generated throw paths were not using that return value.
  - On threaded targets (including eval’s threaded runtime), reading an unset TLS slot could throw instead of behaving like `null`.

- **Codegen: propagate transformed exceptions**
  - Updated coroutine codegen so both exception entry points assign `startException(...)` back into `etmp_error`.
  - This makes custom `ExceptionHandler` implementations able to replace/wrap exception instances in a way that is actually respected by state-machine flow.

  ```ocaml
  (* before: start_exception ecaught; assign old value *)
  b#assign etmp_error (start_exception ecaught)
  ```

- **Type correctness for generated call**
  - `start_exception` call expression now uses `basic.texception` (instead of `tvoid`) to match assignment semantics in generated code.

- **TLS robustness**
  - `haxe.coro.Tls<T>.get_value()` now returns `null` when TLS has no value set, rather than surfacing runtime TLS-not-set exceptions.
  - This aligns TLS reads with nullable semantics already used by exception-stack state handling.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

>

> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>[coro] ExceptionHandler context element</issue_title>
> <issue_description>An idea that has come up is to add an `ExceptionHandler` context element for coroutines which `BaseContinuation.startException` and `BaseContinuation.buildCallStack` delegate to. This would then replace `StackTraceManager` as a context element.
> 
> There's quite a bit of stuff to design surrounding this and while we're at it, we should also make the entire thing thread-safe. While our continuation API can generally assumed to be single-threaded, elements in the coroutine context may be accessed from various threads at the same time.
> 
> Here's my mockup design:
> 
> ```haxe
> import haxe.Exception;
> import haxe.coro.BaseContinuation;
> import haxe.coro.context.IElement;
> import haxe.coro.context.Key;
> 
> abstract class ExceptionHandler implements IElement<ExceptionHandler> {
> 	public static final key = new Key<ExceptionHandler>('ExceptionHandler');
> 
> 	abstract public function startException(cont:BaseContinuation<Any>, exception:Exception):Exception;
> 
> 	abstract public function buildCallStack(cont:BaseContinuation<Any>):Void;
> 
> 	public function getKey() {
> 		return key;
> 	}
> }
> 
> class DefaultExceptionHandler extends ExceptionHandler {
> 
> 	// From StackTraceManager
> 	public var insertIndex:Null<Int>;
> 
> 	public function startException(cont:BaseContinuation<Any>, exception:Exception):Exception {
> 		// Stuff that's currently in BaseContinuation
> 		return exception;
> 	}
> 
> 	public function buildCallStack(cont:BaseContinuation<Any>) {
> 		// Stuff that's currently in BaseContinuation
> 	}
> }
> ```
> 
> Calls to `startException` and `buildCallStack` are never concurrent with regards to the same `BaseContinuation` instance, but there can be two different threads calling them for two different continuation classes.
> 
> The ultimate goal is to have continuations themselves serve as the observable stack via their `getStackItem` and `callerFrame` methods, independent of which threads resumed them. They already manage their own call position through the `setClassFuncStackItem` and `setLocalFuncStackItem` methods. The general stack layout is then:
> 
> 1. Exception location
> 2. Synchronous stack, starting at the last `setClassFuncStackItem` or `setLocalFuncStackItem` location (the top stack).
> 3. Continuation stack, starting at the initial synchronous invocation (the coro stack).
> 4. Synchronous stack to how we got to that initial coroutine invocation.
> 
> We have a test case for this in hxcoro which currently isn't working quite right anymore due to threading problems and inaccuracies when it comes to modifying actual exception stacks: https://github.com/HaxeFoundation/hxcoro/blob/master/tests/src/TestCallStack.hx
> 
> The threaded aspect of this cannot be properly tested in this repository, so that's something we'll have to do over at hxcoro with its structured concurrency. 
> 
> This is a tough one!</issue_description>

title: Cache list_models across all SDK languages to prevent rate limiting under concurrency
body:
Concurrent `send_and_wait` calls trigger redundant `list_models` API requests, causing 429 errors at ~100 concurrent sessions. This fix implements caching across **all SDK languages** (Python, Node.js, .NET, and Go) to ensure consistent behavior.

## Changes

- **Cache models list per client connection**: `list_models()` now caches results after first successful call across all SDKs
- **Prevent race conditions**: Language-appropriate locking mechanisms ensure only one request fetches when cache is empty; subsequent concurrent calls wait and receive cached result
- **Cache invalidation**: Clear on `stop()` and `force_stop()`/`forceStop()`/`ForceStop()` to ensure fresh data after reconnect
- **Return defensive copies**: Prevent callers from mutating cached data

## Implementation by Language

### Python
```python
async def list_models(self) -> list["ModelInfo"]:
    async with self._models_cache_lock:
        if self._models_cache is not None:
            return list(self._models_cache)  # Return copy
        
        # Fetch while holding lock - other coroutines wait here
        response = await self._client.request("models.list", {})
        models = [ModelInfo.from_dict(m) for m in response.get("models", [])]
        self._models_cache = models
        
        return list(models)
```

### Node.js
- Uses Promise-based locking
- Returns array copies via spread operator

### .NET
- Uses `SemaphoreSlim` for async locking
- Returns new `List<ModelInfo>` copies

### Go
- Uses `sync.Mutex` for thread-safe access
- Returns copies via Go's `copy()` function

Models are now fetched once per client connection regardless of concurrent session count across all SDK implementations.

title: Make WriteCodeFragment task locale-independent for reproducible builds
body:
Work item (Internal use): 

### Summary

`WriteCodeFragment` task embeds localized resource strings as comments in generated source files, breaking reproducible builds. Generated code varies by system locale.

**Changes:**
- Added `AssemblyResources.GetInvariantString()` method that retrieves resources using `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`
- Updated `WriteCodeFragment.cs` line 171 to call `GetInvariantString()` instead of `ResourceUtilities.GetResourceString()`
- Added `CommentIsInvariantCulture` Theory test with parameterized cultures (en-US, fr-FR, ja-JP, de-DE) that verifies comment invariance across different locales

The generated comment `"// Generated by the MSBuild WriteCodeFragment class."` now remains English regardless of system locale.

### Customer Impact

Builds using `WriteCodeFragment` (e.g., auto-generated assembly attributes) produce identical output regardless of build machine locale. Fixes build cache misses and enables proper reproducible builds for compliance scenarios.

### Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

No behavior change except comment text is now always English. Generated code functionality unchanged.

### Testing

- All 48 existing `WriteCodeFragment_Tests` pass
- New `CommentIsInvariantCulture` Theory test runs 4 times (once per culture parameter) verifying comment is identical across en-US, fr-FR, ja-JP, and de-DE cultures
- Manual verification: French locale produces English comments while MSBuild messages remain localized

### Risk

**Low.** Single-line change to comment generation. Resource lookup mechanism unchanged, only culture parameter differs. No API surface changes.

> Here `WriteCodeFragment` task use localized resource string as comment in generated source file. This behavior is at odds with reproducible build. I think that resource string should be replaced with language neutral non-localizible string constant.</issue_description>
> 
> <agent_instructions>Make the WriteCodeFragment Task look up the invariant culture resource string for this comment. DO NOT set the thread-or-process-level static properties controlling culture/ui culture to do this, look the resource up directly.</agent_instructions>
>

> That's one solution - another might be to allow providing the locale to use to look up the embedded resource string.
> 
> I tend to agree that generated code should be invariant by default, though.  @rainersigwald Do we have any guidelines for generated code that we use/reference?</body></comment_new>
> <comment_new><author>@rainersigwald</author><body>
> I'm not aware of any but I agree that it seems like it should be invariant by default.</body></comment_new>

title: [OCRVS-10453] Remove FHIR/Hearth test suites, fix docker-compose regression, and fix compiler errors
body:
Cleans up test suites broken by FHIR/Hearth removal, fixes a truncated env var, removes FHIR-dependent source code, and resolves compiler errors across affected packages.

## Changes

- **`docker-compose.yml`**: Fix truncated `USER_MANAGEMENT_URL=http://user-` → `http://user-mgnt:3030/` in the `config` service
- **`packages/commons`**: Delete `assignment.test.ts` — imported from `./fhir` and `./assignment` which no longer exist
- **`packages/workflow/package.json`**: Remove `setupFilesAfterEnv` reference to deleted `./test/setupTest.ts` (caused a Jest validation error blocking all tests)
- **Deleted all test suites** in legacy FHIR-based packages:
  - `packages/notification` (5 files)
  - `packages/search` (1 file)
  - `packages/user-mgnt` (20 files)
  - `packages/webhooks` (3 files)
  - `packages/workflow` (4 files)
- **Test scripts**: Changed `test` script to `yarn test:compilation` for `workflow`, `webhooks`, `search`, `notification`, and `metrics` (removes jest invocations that fail when no test files exist)
- **`packages/metrics/src/api.ts`**: Fixed `IAuthHeader` import — changed from non-existent `@metrics/features/registration` to `@opencrvs/commons`
- **`packages/client`**: Fixed `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` lint warning in `Sidebar.tsx` by removing redundant conditional check
- **`packages/user-mgnt`**: Fixed compiler errors by removing all remaining FHIR operations:
  - `createUser/handler.ts` + `system/handler.ts`: replaced FHIR practitioner/role creation with `uuid()` for `practitionerId`
  - `createUser/service.ts`: removed FHIR type imports (`Extension`, `findExtension`, `OPENCRVS_SPECIFICATION_URL`) and `getSignatureExtension`
  - `getUser/service.ts` + `handler.ts`: removed FHIR-dependent signature fetching; user is returned directly from the DB
  - `updateUser/handler.ts`: removed all FHIR operations; updates MongoDB directly and handles signature upload to minio
  - `utils/location.ts`: replaced removed `SavedLocation` type with `{ id: string }`
- **`packages/gateway`**: Fixed all compiler errors and removed dead code:
  - Removed `searchFieldAgents` resolver from `root-resolvers.ts` (references removed schema type `GQLSearchFieldAgentResponse`, `dataSources.countryConfigAPI`, `postMetrics`)
  - Fixed `primaryOffice` → `primaryOfficeId` in `createOrUpdateUserPayload()`
  - Replaced `dataSources.usersAPI` calls with direct `getUser()` function calls
  - Defined local `IUserPayload` and `IUserSearchPayload` interfaces in `root-resolvers.ts`
  - Fixed `utils/index.ts`: replaced `IUserModelData`/`ISystemModelData` with `User` from commons plus `UserMgntResponse` type (includes `practitionerId`)
  - Fixed `utils/validators.ts`: removed unused `GQLAttachmentInput`/`GQL*RegistrationInput` imports and dead validation functions
  - Deleted dead files: `records/index.ts`, `utils/testUtils.ts`, `features/metrics/service.ts`, `features/user/usersAPI.ts`
  - Deleted outdated tests: `systems/root-resolvers.test.ts`, `user/root-resolvers.test.ts`, `user/type-resolvers.test.ts`
  - Deleted dead code: `metrics/type-resolvers.ts`, `role/root-resolvers.ts`, `systems/root-resolvers.ts`

title: Remove duplicate AZC0012 analyzer
body:
AZC0012 (single-word type name detection) is now implemented in the new analyzer package. This removes the duplicate implementation from Azure.ClientSdk.Analyzers only.

## Changes

**Removed from Azure.ClientSdk.Analyzers:**
- `TypeNameAnalyzer.cs` - AZC0012 implementation
- AZC0012 descriptor from `Descriptors.cs`
- `AZC0012Tests.cs` - all test cases

**No changes to other files:**
- ErrorAnalyzers package remains unchanged (prompts, tests, samples all retain AZC0012 support)
- Documentation references to AZC0012 remain unchanged
- test-proxy NoWarn list remains unchanged (still includes AZC0012)

**Preserved:**
- `NamingSuggestionHelper.cs` - used by multiple analyzers (AZC0034, AZC0030, AZC0031, AZC0032, AZC0033, AZC0036)
- All AZC0012 references outside of Azure.ClientSdk.Analyzers - error code continues to exist from new package

### What changes are proposed in this pull request? The PR size labeling workflow (`pr-size.yml`) failed when attempting to add `size/*` labels that don't exist in the repository. This PR fixes the workflow to auto-create missing labels using the `gh` CLI. **Changes:** - **Updated `.github/workflows/pr-size.yml`**: - Added `issues: write` permission (required for label creation) - Added label existence check using `gh label list --search` before adding labels - Auto-creates missing labels with `gh label create --color ededed` if they don't exist - Wrapped `gh pr edit --remove-label` with `|| true` to gracefully handle missing labels without failing The workflow maintains the original inline `node -e` + `gh` CLI approach without requiring `actions/checkout` or `actions/github-script`. All existing functionality is preserved (generated file filtering, size thresholds). ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Manual tests Validated workflow syntax and pre-commit hooks. ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. You can skip the rest of this section. ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. You can skip the rest of this section. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [x] No. You can skip the rest of this section. #### How should the PR be classified in the release notes? Choose one: - [x] `rn/none` - No description will be included. The PR will be mentioned only by the PR number in the "Small Bugfixes and Documentation Updates" section #### Should this PR be included in the next patch release? - [ ] Yes (this PR will be cherry-picked and included in the next patch release) - [x] No (this PR will be included in the next minor release)

Fix `pr-size.js` to auto-create missing labels before applying them. > > Reference: https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/actions/runs/22018853511/job/63624663902?pr=20816 > > ## Instructions > > 1. **Discard all existing changes** on this branch (the `create-size-labels.yml` file is not needed) > 2. **Modify `.github/workflows/pr-size.js`** to ensure labels are created if they don't exist before adding them to a PR > > ### Implementation > > In `pr-size.js`, before calling `github.rest.issues.addLabels`, add a try/catch that: > 1. First tries `github.rest.issues.getLabel` to check if the label exists > 2. If it gets a 404, creates the label with `github.rest.issues.createLabel` using color `ededed` > 3. title: Trigger APIView CI on PRs when Azure.ClientSdk.Analyzers changes
body:
APIView depends on Azure.ClientSdk.Analyzers via ProjectReference but changes to the analyzers aren't verified against APIView before merge.

## Changes

- Added `src/dotnet/Azure.ClientSdk.Analyzers` to the pr path filters in `src/dotnet/APIView/apiview.yml`

When PRs are created that modify Azure.ClientSdk.Analyzers, the APIView CI will automatically trigger. The APIView CI already builds the APIView project, which has a ProjectReference dependency on Azure.ClientSdk.Analyzers, so any breaking changes to the analyzers will be caught during the APIView build process before the PR is merged.

Note: The path is only added to PR triggers, not to regular triggers, to prevent unnecessary CI runs on direct commits to main while still providing verification during the PR review process.

title: fix: treat `format: int64` as `bigint` across plugin-oas, plugin-ts, plugin-zod, and plugin-faker
body:
`format: int64` was mapped identically to `format: int32` — both emitted the `integer` keyword, producing `number`/`z.int()`. Zod v4 rejects integers outside `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, making valid int64 values fail validation. The `wrapOutput` workaround shown in the issue screenshot was the only escape hatch. ## 🎯 Changes ### `plugin-oas` - Added `bigint` to `SchemaKeywordMapper` type and `schemaKeywords` constant - `SchemaGenerator`: `format: int64` now emits `bigint` keyword; `format: int32` retains `integer` keyword ### `plugin-ts` - Added `BigIntKeyword` entry to `keywordTypeNodes` in `factory.ts` - `bigint` keyword → TypeScript `bigint` primitive type ### `plugin-zod` - `bigint` keyword → `z.bigint()`, or `z.coerce.bigint()` when coercion is enabled ### `plugin-faker` - `bigint` keyword → `faker.number.bigInt()` (native Faker.js v8 API for generating random `bigint` values) ### Result ```yaml # OpenAPI spec id: type: integer format: int64 ``` ```ts // plugin-ts: was `number`, now: id: bigint // plugin-zod: was `z.number().int()` / `z.int()`, now: id: z.bigint() // plugin-zod with coercion enabled: was `z.coerce.number().int()`, now: id: z.coerce.bigint() // plugin-faker: was `faker.number.int()`, now: id: faker.number.bigInt() ``` `format: int32` is unaffected and continues to emit `number`/`z.int()`. ## ✅ Checklist - [x] I have followed the steps in the [Contributing guide](https://github.com/kubb-labs/kubb/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have tested this code locally with `pnpm run test`. ## 🚀 Release Impact - [x] This change affects published code, and I have generated a [changeset](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/docs/adding-a-changeset.md). - [ ] This change is for the docs (no release).
Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > Int64 is treated as Number, causing validation to fail for big numbers > ### What version of `kubb` is running? > > 4.24.0 > > ### What kind of platform do you use? > > MacOS > > ### Your `kubb.config.ts` config file? > > ```typescript > import { defineConfig } from "@kubb/core"; > import { pluginTs } from "@kubb/plugin-ts"; > import { pluginZod } from "@kubb/plugin-zod"; > > export default defineConfig({ > root: ".", > input: { path: "./openapi.yaml" }, > output: { path: "./generated", clean: true }, > plugins: [ > pluginTs({ > output: { path: "./types", barrelType: false }, > }), > pluginZod({ > output: { path: "./zod", barrelType: false }, > typed: true, > version: "4", > }), > ], > }); > ``` > > ### Swagger/OpenAPI file? > > ```bash > openapi: 3.0.3 > info: > title: Int64 demo API > version: 0.0.1 > > paths: > /items: > post: > operationId: createItem > requestBody: > content: > application/json: > schema: > $ref: '#/components/schemas/Item' > responses: > '201': > description: Created > > components: > schemas: > Item: > type: object > required: [id, name] > properties: > id: > type: integer > format: int64 > description: Unique identifier (int64, use bigint in JS) > name: > type: string > count: > type: integer > format: int32 > description: Small integer (int32) > ``` > > ### What version of external packages are you using(`@tanstack-query`, `MSW`, `React`, `Vue`, ...) > > ```JSON > { > "name": "kubb-demo", > "private": true, > "type": "module", > "scripts": { > "generate": "kubb generate -c kubb.config.ts", > "validate": "tsx validate.mjs", > "validate:unsafe": "node validate-unsafe-number.mjs" > }, > "devDependencies": { > "@kubb/cli": "^4.19.2", > "@kubb/core": "^4.19.2", > "@kubb/plugin-oas": "^4.19.2", > "@kubb/plugin-ts": "^4.19.2", > "@kubb/plugin-zod": "^4.19.2", > "typescript": "^5.7.2", > "zod": "^4.3.6", > "tsx": "^4.19.2" > } > } > ``` > > ### What steps can reproduce the bug? > > 1. In your openapi spec, define a field with `type: integer` and `format: int64` (see example) > 2. Generate zod v4 schemas and typescript types > 3. Validate a big number like 9007199254741993 > 4. Validation fails even though it's a valid int64 number > > ### How often does this bug happen? > > Every time > > ### What is the expected behavior? > > zod v4 is validating that a number being parsed is actually within the safe range (less than `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`), which is not always the case for Int64 numbers. This means that `type: integer` with `format: int64` will sometimes fail. > > I think it should be an option to treat Int64 numbers as bigints instead, both in the `@kubb/plugin-zod` and `@kubb/plugin-ts` (and possibly other plugins as well?). There might be cases where this is unwanted behavior due to backwards compatibility or such, open to hear your thoughts. > > ### Additional information > > I've managed to come up with a workaround for plugin-zod using wrapOutput, but I can't find a similar approach for plugin-ts. > > > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > >

title: feat(iceberg): enforce merge-on-read for append-only tables
body:
I hereby agree to the terms of the [RisingWave Labs, Inc. Contributor License Agreement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/risingwavelabs/risingwave/17af8a747593ebdbfa826691daf75bdab7d14fa0/.github/contributor-license-agreement.txt). ## What's changed and what's your intention? Append-only Iceberg tables now enforce merge-on-read write mode. Copy-on-write provides no benefit for append-only workloads (no updates/deletes to eagerly compact) and has worse write performance. **Changes:** - Added `validate_append_only_write_mode` helper that rejects copy-on-write for append-only sinks - Validation runs during config parsing (`from_btreemap`) and at sink creation (`validate`) - Upsert sinks can still use copy-on-write **Example:** ```rust // This now fails at config parsing CREATE SINK s AS SELECT * FROM t WITH ( connector = 'iceberg', type = 'append-only', write_mode = 'copy-on-write', // ERROR: not supported ... ); // Defaults to merge-on-read if unspecified CREATE SINK s AS SELECT * FROM t WITH ( connector = 'iceberg', type = 'append-only', ... ); ``` ## Checklist - [ ] I have written necessary rustdoc comments. - [x] I have added necessary unit tests and integration tests. - [ ] I have added test labels as necessary. - [ ] I have added fuzzing tests or opened an issue to track them. - [ ] My PR contains breaking changes. - [ ] My PR changes performance-critical code, so I will run (micro) benchmarks and present the results. - [ ] I have checked the [Release Timeline](https://github.com/risingwavelabs/rw-commits-history/blob/main/release_timeline.md) and [Currently Supported Versions](https://docs.risingwave.com/changelog/release-support-policy#support-end-dates-for-recent-releases) to determine which release branches I need to cherry-pick this PR into. ## Documentation - [x] My PR needs documentation updates.
Release note **Breaking change for append-only Iceberg sinks:** Copy-on-write mode is no longer supported. Explicitly setting `write_mode = 'copy-on-write'` for append-only sinks will now fail with a clear error message. Merge-on-read remains the default and is strictly better for append-only workloads. Upsert sinks are unaffected and can continue using either mode.
Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > iceberg: enforce merge on read write-mode for append only iceberg table by defaut. > Since the merge on read is strictly better than copy on write for append only iceberg table, we should enforce it instead of confusing users. > > enforce merge on read write-mode for append only iceberg table by defaut. > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > >
- Fixes risingwavelabs/risingwave#24486 --- 💬 We'd love your input! Share your thoughts on Copilot coding agent in our [2 minute survey](https://gh.io/copilot-coding-agent-survey).
