title: Add sketch trim tool with hover preview and constraint-preserving split
body:
Implements a sketch trim tool that clips segments of entities between their intersections with other entities, with real-time hover preview of the segment to be removed.

## Core Infrastructure

- **`Entity.Split()` now preserves constraints and style automatically**: after splitting, `ReplaceEntityInConstraints(this.end, part.end)` transfers endpoint constraints to the new entity, and the original entity's `style` is copied to the split part
- **`Entity.FindParameter(Vector3 pos)`**: new virtual method (ternary-search numerical base) returning normalized `t ∈ [0,1]` for the closest point on an entity; optimized overrides in `LineEntity` (dot-product projection), `ArcEntity`/`EllipticArcEntity` (angle-based), `SplineEntity` and `FunctionEntity` (subdivision-aware ternary search)
- **`Entity.GetAllIntersections(Entity e, bool refine = false)`**: returns all crossing points with another entity by testing every segment pair; when `refine: true`, each rough intersection is Newton-refined via `EquationSystem` (same pattern as `PointOn`/`Tangent` constraints) for sub-pixel precision
- **`FunctionEntity.GetTrimPreviewStep()`**: method on `FunctionEntity` returning `1 / max(64, subdivision × ⌈range⌉)` so oscillating function curves are previewed at their natural density

## Entity Split Implementations

- **`FunctionEntity.OnSplit()`** (was commented-out stub): clones the entity with the t-range split at `FindParameter(pos)`, preserving expressions, basis, and subdivision; sets `tEndFixed`/`tBeginFixed` on both halves
- **`SplineEntity.OnSplit()`** (was commented-out stub): geometrically correct split via de Casteljau's algorithm

## Trim Tool

`TrimTool` hover logic:
1. Collects all intersections of hovered entity with sketch entities via `GetAllIntersections(other, refine: true)` — Newton-refined through `EquationSystem` for precision; also includes positions of `PointOn` constraints where the entity is the `on` entity, so adjacent endpoint-on-curve connections act as trim boundaries
2. Finds the segment `[t_before_mouse, t_after_mouse]` between neighboring intersections (endpoint touches at `t=0`/`t=1` are included, enabling adjacent/T-intersection trimming)
3. Draws that segment using the named `"trimPreview"` style (defined in `StrokeStyles.prefab`, queue=3007 above hover's 3006, no depth test) via the `DetailEditor.toolPreviewDraw` delegate; preview step is read from the entity as `FunctionEntity.GetTrimPreviewStep()` when applicable

On click, trims by splitting at the stored intersection positions and destroying the segment under the cursor. Handles all cases:

```
// "trim middle" case
var part1 = entity.Split(posBegin);  // entity → [A…I1], part1 → [I1…B]
var part2 = part1.Split(posEnd);     // part1 → [I1…I2], part2 → [I2…B]
part1.Destroy();                     // removes [I1…I2]; constraints and style transferred by Split()

// "no intersections" case
entity.Destroy();                    // entire entity removed

// "loop entity" case (circle/ellipse)
var arc = new ArcEntity(sketch);     // keeps the non-trimmed arc; original circle destroyed; style inherited
```

Supported entity types: lines, arcs, elliptic arcs, splines, arbitrary function curves, circles, and ellipses.

## Supporting Changes

- `SplitTool`: removed now-redundant manual `ReplaceEntityInConstraints` call; added null guard for entities without `OnSplit`
- `DetailEditor`: added `public Action<ICanvas> toolPreviewDraw` delegate; clears `"trimPreview"` style bucket and invokes it each frame
- `StrokeStyles.prefab`: added `"trimPreview"` named style (red, queue=3007, depthTest=false) so the trim preview always renders above the hover highlight

> **Unity integration note**: `TrimTool` needs to be added as a MonoBehaviour component under the ToolBar GameObject in the scene to appear in the toolbar.

title: Refresh README visuals with real obfuscation terminal GIF and Medium preset output excerpt
body:
Improves the main README’s presentation while preserving existing content and structure. Adds a clearer visual entry point for new users by showing a real obfuscation run and a real output excerpt.

- **README visual refresh**
  - Added a new `## Preview` section to the main README.
  - Embedded an animated asset: `assets/readme/obfuscation-preview.gif`.
  - Kept existing sections/content intact and in the same general order.

- **Preview GIF updated to real CLI output**
  - Regenerated `assets/readme/obfuscation-preview.gif` from an actual `cli.lua` obfuscation run.
  - The GIF now shows real terminal output during obfuscation, including colorized log styling.

- **Obfuscation output preview**
  - Replaced the handcrafted/simplified output sample with an excerpt from a real obfuscated file generated using the Medium preset.
  - Clarified in the README that the shown block is an excerpt and intentionally truncated.

```lua
-- input.lua
local secret = "Prometheus"
local answer = 42
print(secret .. " -> " .. answer)

-- generated with: lua ./cli.lua --preset Medium ./simple.lua
-- excerpt from ./simple.obfuscated.lua
return(function(...)local L={"afT6mf1V","/7mJXsuvmE1c/fT3"; ...}
... (remaining obfuscated output omitted)
```

- **Copy polish**
  - Minor wording/capitalization cleanup in existing README text (no semantic/content expansion).

- **Assets**
  - Updated `assets/readme/obfuscation-preview.gif` for in-README rendering.

## Progress: Addressed Code Review Feedback

### Completed Tasks

- [x] Removed SUMMARY.md helper file from repository
- [x] Added SUMMARY.md to .gitignore
- [x] Refined code review instruction to avoid circular dependency

### Changes Made

**1. Removed SUMMARY.md**
- This was a temporary helper file for PR creation
- Should not be committed to the repository
- Now added to .gitignore alongside other PR helper files

**2. Updated .gitignore**
- Added `SUMMARY.md` to the PR helper files section
- Prevents accidental commits of temporary documentation

**3. Refined Code Review Instruction** (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`)
- Changed from "always run" to "run the pr-finalize skill" for functional code PRs
- Removed "always" to avoid circular dependency issues
- Clarified this applies specifically to "PRs that change functional code"
- Avoids triggering on documentation-only or configuration-only PRs like this one

### Before
```
When performing a code review, always run the pr-finalize skill...
```

### After
```
When performing a code review on PRs that change functional code, run the pr-finalize skill...
```

### Impact

- SUMMARY.md no longer clutters the repository
- Code review instruction is more appropriate and avoids circular dependency
- pr-finalize skill will be used for functional code reviews where it adds the most value

+# Learn From PR
+
+Extracts lessons learned from a completed PR to improve repository documentation and agent capabilities.
+
+## Inputs
+
+| Input | Required | Source |
+|-------|----------|--------|
+| PR number or Issue number | Yes | User provides (e.g., "PR #33352" or "issue 33352") |
+| Session markdown | Optional | `.github/agent-pr-session/issue-XXXXX.md` or `pr-XXXXX.md` |
+
+## Outputs
+
+1. **Learning Analysis** - Structured markdown with:
+   - What happened (problem, attempts, solution)
+   - Fix location analysis (attempted vs actual)
+   - Failure modes identified
+   - Prioritized recommendations
+
+2. **Actionable Recommendations** - Each with:
+   - Category, Priority, Location, Specific Change, Why It Helps
+
+## Completion Criteria
+
+The skill is complete when you have:
+- [ ] Gathered PR diff and metadata
+- [ ] Analyzed fix location (attempted vs actual)
+- [ ] Identified failure modes
+- [ ] Generated at least one concrete recommendation
+- [ ] Presented findings to user
+
+## When to Use
+
+- After agent failed to find the right fix
+- After agent succeeded but took many attempts
+- After agent succeeded quickly (to understand what worked)
+- When asked "what can we learn from PR #XXXXX?"
+
+## When NOT to Use
+
+- Before PR is finalized (use `pr-finalize` first)
+- For trivial PRs (typo fixes, simple changes)
+- When no agent was involved (nothing to analyze)
+
+---
+
+## Workflow
+
+### Step 1: Gather Data
+
+```bash
+# Required: Get PR info
+gh pr view XXXXX --json title,body,files
+gh pr diff XXXXX
+
+# Check for session markdown
+ls .github/agent-pr-session/issue-XXXXX.md .github/agent-pr-session/pr-XXXXX.md 2>/dev/null
+```
+
+**If session markdown exists, extract:**
+- Fix Candidates table (what was tried)
+- Files each attempt targeted
+- Why attempts failed
+
+**Analyzing without session markdown:**
+
+When no session file exists, you can still learn from:
+1. **PR discussion** - Comments reveal what was tried
+2. **Commit history** - Multiple commits may show iteration
+3. **Code complexity** - Non-obvious fixes suggest learning opportunities
+4. **Similar past issues** - Search for related bugs
+
+Focus on: "What would have helped an agent find this fix faster?"
+
+### Step 2: Fix Location Analysis
+
+**Critical question:** Did agent attempts target the same files as the final fix?
+
+```bash
+# Where did final fix go?
+gh pr view XXXXX --json files --jq '.files[].path' | grep -v test
+
+# If session markdown exists, compare to attempted files
+```
+
+| Scenario | Implication |
+|----------|-------------|
+| Same files | Agent found right location |
+| Different files | **Major learning opportunity** - document why |
+
+**If different files:** Answer these questions:
+- Why did agent think that was the right file?
+- What search would have found the correct file?
+
+### Step 3: Analyze Outcome
+
+Determine which scenario applies and look for the relevant patterns:
+
+#### Scenario A: Agent Failed
+
+| Pattern | Indicator |
+|---------|-----------|
+| **Wrong file entirely** | All attempts in File A, fix in File B |
+| **Tunnel vision** | Only looked at file mentioned in error |
+| **Trusted issue title** | Issue said "crash in X" so only looked at X |
+| **Pattern not generalized** | Fixed one instance, missed others |
+| **Didn't search codebase** | Never found similar code patterns |
+| **Missing platform knowledge** | Didn't know iOS/Android/Windows specifics |
+| **Wrong abstraction layer** | Fixed handler when problem was in core |
+| **Misread error message** | Error pointed to symptom, not cause |
+| **Incomplete context** | Didn't read enough surrounding code |
+| **Over-engineered** | Complex fix when simple one existed |
+
+#### Scenario B: Agent Succeeded Slowly (many attempts)
+
+| Pattern | Indicator |
+|---------|-----------|
+| **Correct file, wrong approach** | Found right file but tried wrong fixes first |
+| **Needed multiple iterations** | Each attempt got closer but wasn't quite right |
+| **Discovery was slow** | Eventually found it but search was inefficient |
+| **Missing domain knowledge** | Had to learn something that could be documented |
+
+**Key question:** What would have gotten agent to the solution faster?
+
+#### Scenario C: Agent Succeeded Quickly
+
+| Pattern | Indicator |
+|---------|-----------|
+| **Good search strategy** | Found right file immediately |
+| **Understood the pattern** | Recognized similar issues from past |
+| **Documentation helped** | Existing docs pointed to solution |
+| **Simple, minimal fix** | Didn't over-engineer |
+
+**Key question:** What made this work? Should we reinforce this pattern?
+
+### Step 4: Find Improvement Locations
+
+```bash
+# Discover where agent guidance lives
+find .github/instructions -name "*.instructions.md" 2>/dev/null
+find .github/skills -name "SKILL.md" 2>/dev/null
+ls .github/architecture/ 2>/dev/null
+```
+
+| Location | When to Add Here |
+|----------|------------------|
+| `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` | Domain-specific guidance |
+| `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md` | Skill needs new step or checklist |
+| `.github/architecture/*.md` | Architectural knowledge |
+| Code comments | Non-obvious code behavior |
+
+### Step 5: Generate Recommendations
+
+For each recommendation, provide:
+
+1. **Category:** Instruction file / Skill / Architecture doc / Inline comment / Linting issue
+2. **Priority:** High (prevents class of bugs) / Medium (helps discovery) / Low (nice to have)
+3. **Location:** Exact file path
+4. **Specific Change:** Exact text to add
+5. **Why It Helps:** Which failure mode it prevents
+
+**Prioritization factors:**
+- How common is this pattern?
+- Would future agents definitely hit this again?
+- How hard is it to implement?
+
+**Pattern-to-Improvement Mapping (Failures/Slow Success):**
+
+| Pattern | Likely Improvement |
+|---------|-------------------|
+| Wrong file entirely | Architecture doc explaining component relationships |
+| Tunnel vision | Instruction file: "Always search for pattern across codebase" |
+| Missing platform knowledge | Platform-specific instruction file |
+| Wrong abstraction layer | Architecture doc explaining layers |
+| Misread error message | Code comment explaining the real cause |
+| Over-engineered | Skill enhancement: "Try simplest fix first" |
+
+**Pattern-to-Improvement Mapping (Quick Success - reinforce):**
+
+| Pattern | Improvement |
+|---------|-------------|
+| Good search strategy | Document the search pattern that worked in skills |
+| Documentation helped | Note which docs were valuable, ensure they stay updated |
+| Recognized pattern | Add to instruction files as known pattern |
+
+### Step 6: Present Findings
+
+Present your analysis covering:
+- What happened and what made it hard
+- Where agent looked vs actual fix location
+- Which patterns applied and evidence
+- Prioritized recommendations with full details (category, priority, location, exact change, why it helps)
+
+---
+
+## Error Handling
+
+| Situation | Action |
+|-----------|--------|
+| PR not found | Ask user to verify PR number |
+| No session markdown | Analyze PR diff only, note limited context |
+| No agent involvement evident | Ask user if they still want analysis |
+| Can't determine failure mode | State "insufficient data" and what's missing |
+
+## Constraints
+
+- **Analysis only** - Don't apply changes (use learn-from-pr agent for that)
+- **Actionable recommendations** - Every recommendation must have specific file path and text
+- **Don't duplicate** - Check existing docs before recommending new ones
+- **Focus on high-value learning** - Skip trivial observations
+- **Respect PR scope** - Don't recommend improvements unrelated to the PR's learnings
+
+---
+
+## Examples
+
+### Example: Wrong File Entirely
+
+**PR #33352** - TraitCollectionDidChange crash on MacCatalyst
+
+**What happened:**
+- Issue title: "ObjectDisposedException in ShellSectionRootRenderer"
+- Agent made 11 attempts, ALL in `ShellSectionRootRenderer.cs`
+- Actual fix was in `PageViewController.cs`
+
+**Failure Mode:** Trusted issue title instead of searching for pattern.
+
+**Recommendation:**
+- **Category:** Instruction File
+- **Location:** `.github/instructions/ios-debugging.instructions.md`
+- **Change:** "When fixing iOS crashes, search for the PATTERN across all files, not just the file named in the error"
+- **Why:** Prevents tunnel vision on named file
+
+### Example: Slow Success
+
+**PR #34567** - CollectionView scroll position not preserved
+
+**What happened:**
+- Agent took 5 attempts to find fix
+- First 3 attempts were in wrong layer (handler vs core)
+- Eventually found it after reading more context
+- Final fix was simple once the right layer was identified
+
+**Pattern:** Wrong abstraction layer - fixed handler when problem was in core.
+
+**Recommendation:**
+- **Category:** Architecture Doc
+- **Location:** `.github/architecture/handler-vs-core.md`
+- **Change:** Document layer responsibilities - handlers map properties, core handles behavior
+- **Why:** Helps agent identify correct layer faster
+
+### Example: Quick Success
+
+**PR #35678** - Button disabled state not updating
+
+**What happened:**
+- Agent found fix in 1 attempt
+- Searched for "IsEnabled" pattern across codebase immediately
+- Found similar past fix in another control and applied same approach
+- Simple, minimal change
+
+**Pattern:** Good search strategy - recognized pattern from similar code.
+
+**Recommendation:**
+- **Category:** Skill Enhancement
+- **Location:** `.github/skills/try-fix/SKILL.md`
+- **Change:** Add to search strategy: "Search for same property pattern in other controls"
+- **Why:** Reinforces successful discovery technique
+

- [x] Modify `event/iowatcher.h` - Add `EVENT_IO_URING` to backend selection logic
- [x] Modify `event/hloop.c` - Add `EVENT_IO_URING` case to `hio_engine()` function
- [x] Modify `event/hloop.h` - Add `EVENT_IO_URING` to the engine name comment

- [x] Add `io_uring_get_sqe_safe()` helper to handle SQE exhaustion (submit + retry)
- [x] Handle `iowatcher_init()` failure in `iowatcher_add_event()` (return error)

## Implementation: Exclude `metadata: read` from Generated Permissions

**Background:** The `metadata: read` permission is a built-in GitHub Actions permission that is always available and should not be explicitly declared in workflow YAML files.

**Changes Made:**

- [x] Add `PermissionMetadata` constant to permission scopes in `pkg/workflow/permissions.go`
- [x] Update `GetAllPermissionScopes()` to include the new metadata scope
- [x] Update `convertStringToPermissionScope()` to handle "metadata" string
- [x] Modify `RenderToYAML()` in `permissions_operations.go` to skip metadata (similar to organization-projects)
- [x] Add comprehensive tests to verify metadata permission is excluded from YAML output
- [x] Update existing merge tests to account for new metadata permission scope
- [x] Exclude metadata from dangerous permissions validation
- [x] Run linter and formatter (make fmt && make lint) - all checks passed
- [x] Recompile workflow files (make recompile) - 145/145 workflows compiled successfully
- [x] Run all permission tests - all tests passing

**Technical Details:**

The implementation adds `metadata` as a valid permission scope but ensures it's never rendered in the final YAML output. This is achieved by:

1. Adding `PermissionMetadata` to the list of permission scopes (similar to existing scopes like `PermissionContents`, `PermissionIssues`, etc.)
2. Skipping the metadata scope during YAML rendering in `RenderToYAML()` method
3. Including metadata in permission merging operations (so it can be set/merged like other permissions internally)
4. Filtering it out during final YAML generation (since it's a built-in permission)
5. Excluding metadata from dangerous permissions validation (since it's read-only)

**Test Coverage:**

Added `TestPermissions_MetadataExcluded` with 4 test cases:
- metadata permission excluded from explicit permission maps
- metadata excluded from all:read expansion
- metadata:write also excluded
- only-metadata case renders empty permissions

All existing tests updated and passing, including dangerous permissions tests.

title: Fix Uri.TryUnescapeDataString throwing instead of returning false with small destination buffers
body:
`Uri.TryUnescapeDataString` threw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` instead of returning `false` when the destination span was shorter than the index of the first `%` in the input:

```csharp
Uri.TryUnescapeDataString("aa%", [], out _); // threw ArgumentOutOfRangeException
```

## Description

**Root cause:** When the input contains `%`, the method uses `destination.Slice(indexOfFirstToUnescape)` as the initial buffer for `ValueStringBuilder`. If `destination.Length < indexOfFirstToUnescape`, this `Slice` call throws instead of returning `false` gracefully.

**Fix:** Added an early-out guard — when `destination.Length < indexOfFirstToUnescape`, the destination cannot hold even the literal prefix before the first `%`, so `false` is returned immediately with `charsWritten = 0`. This check is placed before the overlapped-buffer detection, so it fires unconditionally in both overlapped and non-overlapped cases.

**Tests:** Added `[Theory]` cases covering the reported scenario and similar variants (`"aa%"` and `"aaa%41"` with destination sizes smaller than the prefix length).

title: feat(sdl): add support for additional private container registries
body:
SDL Builder only exposed Docker Hub and GHCR in the private registry dropdown, but Akash supports GCR, AWS ECR, Azure ACR, GitLab, and custom registries.

### Changes

- **Extended registry options** in `ImageCredentialsHost.tsx`:
  - Google Container Registry (`gcr.io`)
  - AWS Elastic Container Registry (`ecr`)
  - Azure Container Registry (`azurecr.io`)
  - GitLab Container Registry (`registry.gitlab.com`)
  - Custom registry with URL input field

- **Schema updates** in `sdlBuilder.ts`:
  - Added new host enum values and `customRegistryUrl` field
  - Validation requiring custom URL when "custom" is selected
  - Hostname format validation via regex

- **SDL generation/import** in `sdlGenerator.ts` and `sdlImport.ts`:
  - Custom registry URL becomes the actual `host` in generated SDL
  - Import detects unknown hosts and maps to "custom" with `customRegistryUrl`

- **ImageRegistryLogo** now returns `null` for registries without logos instead of failing

### Example SDL output

When user selects "Custom Registry" and enters `myregistry.example.com`:

```yaml
services:
  web:
    image: myregistry.example.com/myimage:v1
    credentials:
      host: myregistry.example.com
      username: user
      password: pass
```

title: Add detailed GitOps resource status to CI debug output
body:
CI debug step lacked visibility into GitOps resource states, making Flux and ArgoCD deployment failures difficult to diagnose.

## Changes

- **Enhanced `.github/actions/debug-kubernetes-failure/action.yaml`**
  - Added FluxInstance status (`flux-system` namespace)
  - Added OCIRepository status (`flux-system` namespace)
  - Added ArgoCD Application status (all namespaces)
  - Shows both summary table (`kubectl get -o wide`) and detailed status (`kubectl describe`)
  - Detailed status includes conditions, reconciliation state, artifact information, sync status, and health status
  - Gracefully handles missing CRDs when GitOps tools not installed

- **Updated `.github/actions/debug-kubernetes-failure/README.md`**
  - Added example output for GitOps resources including detailed status sections
  - Enhanced common failure patterns with specific condition-based debugging guidance
  - Documented patterns like `ArtifactFailed`, operation state failures, and sync errors

## Output Format

```bash
=== FluxInstance Status ===
NAMESPACE     NAME   AGE   READY   STATUS
flux-system   flux   10m   False   OCIRepository not synced

=== FluxInstance Details ===
Status:
  Conditions:
    Last Transition Time:  2024-01-22T07:20:00Z
    Message:               Reconciliation finished, next run in 1h0m0s
    Reason:                ReconciliationSucceeded
    Status:                True
    Type:                  Ready

=== OCIRepository Status ===
NAMESPACE     NAME          URL                                   AGE   READY   STATUS
flux-system   flux-system   oci://ghcr.io/org/repo/manifests     10m   False   authentication required

title: Fix user-level tasks.json causing infinite spinner
body:
### This changes visible behavior

User-level tasks defined in `~/.config/Code/User/tasks.json` now execute correctly instead of hanging with an infinite spinner.

The following changes are proposed:

- Add type guard in `resolveTask()` and `resolveInternalTask()` to distinguish `WorkspaceFolder` objects from `TaskScope` enum values
- Use `TaskScope.Workspace` as fallback when scope is not a `WorkspaceFolder`
- Add null safety check since `typeof null === 'object'` in JavaScript

## The purpose of this change

Both methods unconditionally cast `task.scope` to `WorkspaceFolder`:

```typescript
// Before
const workspaceFolder: vscode.WorkspaceFolder = task.scope as vscode.WorkspaceFolder;
```

VSCode's Task API defines `task.scope` as `WorkspaceFolder | TaskScope.Global | TaskScope.Workspace`. User-level tasks have `scope = TaskScope.Global` (numeric value 1), causing the cast to produce invalid state.

```typescript
// After
const workspaceFolder: vscode.WorkspaceFolder | undefined = 
    (task.scope && typeof task.scope === 'object') ? task.scope as vscode.WorkspaceFolder : undefined;
const resolvedTask = new vscode.Task(definition, workspaceFolder ?? vscode.TaskScope.Workspace, ...);
```

`CustomBuildTaskTerminal` already handles `undefined` workspaceFolder by falling back to the active project.

body:
## Summary

Adds a confirmation dialog before resetting gesture settings to prevent accidental data loss.

**Changes:**
- Added `showResetConfirmation` state to manage dialog visibility
- Modified reset button to trigger confirmation instead of immediate reset
- Added `confirmationDialog` modifier applied directly to the button with Yes/No action buttons
- Added localization strings: `gestures.reset.confirmation.title` and `gestures.reset.confirmation.message`

Implementation follows existing patterns from `WatchConfigurationView` and `CarPlayConfigurationView`.

title: Fix syntax errors in check-for-new-contributor workflow and optimize template fetching
body:
The `check-for-new-contributor.yml` workflow fails with syntax errors because the `env` context is not available in job-level `if` conditions in GitHub Actions.

## Changes

- **Removed `env.CONTRIBUTOR_WHITELIST` checks from job-level `if` conditions** in all three jobs (`greet-first-time-pr`, `greet-first-time-issue`, `greet-first-time-comment`)
- **Moved whitelist validation into GitHub script steps** where `process.env` is accessible
- **Removed unnecessary repository checkouts** from all three jobs
- **Replaced filesystem-based template reading with GitHub API** - templates are now fetched using `github.rest.repos.getContent()` instead of `fs.readFileSync()`

## Example

Before (job-level - causes syntax error):
```yaml
if: |
  github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && 
  !contains(env.CONTRIBUTOR_WHITELIST, github.event.pull_request.user.login)
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v6
  - uses: actions/github-script@v8
    with:
      script: |
        const fs = require('fs');
        let prMessage = fs.readFileSync(
          path.join(process.env.GITHUB_WORKSPACE, '.github/templates/pr_welcome.md'),
          'utf8'
        );
```

After (script-level - works correctly and more efficient):
```yaml
if: |
  github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'
steps:
  - uses: actions/github-script@v8
    with:
      script: |
        const whitelist = process.env.CONTRIBUTOR_WHITELIST || '';
        if (whitelist.includes(author)) {
          console.log(`${author} is in the contributor whitelist. Skipping greeting.`);
          return;
        }
        
        const { data } = await github.rest.repos.getContent({
          owner,
          repo,
          path: '.github/templates/pr_welcome.md'
        });
        let prMessage = Buffer.from(data.content, 'base64').toString('utf8');
```

## Benefits

- Fixes syntax errors and allows workflow to run correctly
- Faster execution without repository checkout
- More efficient use of GitHub API for template content
- Cleaner code with fewer dependencies

Functionality unchanged - whitelisted contributors are still skipped, but the check now occurs where the `env` context is available.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem
> 
> The `.github/workflows/check-for-new-contributor.yml` workflow file has syntax errors that prevent it from running correctly. The workflow fails with the following errors:
> 
> 1. **Line 27, Col 9**: Unrecognized named-value: 'env'. Located at position 164 within expression in `greet-first-time-pr` job
> 2. **Line 90, Col 9**: Unrecognized named-value: 'env'. Located at position 80 within expression in `greet-first-time-issue` job  
> 3. **Line 144, Col 9**: Unrecognized named-value: 'env'. Located at position 88 within expression in `greet-first-time-comment` job
> 
> The root cause is that the `env` context is not available in job-level `if` conditions in GitHub Actions. The `env` context can only be accessed within step-level contexts or within the scripts themselves.
> 
> ## Solution
> 
> Update the `.github/workflows/check-for-new-contributor.yml` file to:
> 
> 1. **Remove `env.CONTRIBUTOR_WHITELIST` checks from job-level `if` conditions**
> 2. **Move whitelist validation into the GitHub script steps** where `process.env` is accessible
> 3. **Simplify job-level conditions** to only check event type and action
> 
> ### Specific Changes
> 
> For all three jobs (`greet-first-time-pr`, `greet-first-time-issue`, `greet-first-time-comment`):
> 
> - Remove the line `!contains(env.CONTRIBUTOR_WHITELIST, github.event.pull_request.user.login)` from the job-level `if` condition
> - Add whitelist check at the beginning of each script:
>   ```javascript
>   // Check if author is in the whitelist
>   const whitelist = process.env.CONTRIBUTOR_WHITELIST || '';
>   if (whitelist.includes(author)) {
>     console.log(`${author} is in the contributor whitelist. Skipping greeting.`);
>     return;
>   }
>   ```
> 
> This approach maintains the same functionality while being compatible with GitHub Actions' context availability rules.
> 
> ## File to Update
> 
> - `.github/workflows/check-for-new-contributor.yml`
> 
> The file is currently at commit `38e8a3c8802a7b0353433475cdf544b68d877220`.


</details>

> @copilot rename the field to "manifest-files" and support an enum string:
> 
> - blocked (default). no writes allowed....

Done in ae482bf. The field is now `manifest-files` with a pure string enum:

- `blocked` (default) — hard-block; safe output fails with an error
- `allowed` — all manifest/config file changes permitted
- `fallback-to-issue` — push branch / skip push, create a review issue instead

The old `allow-manifest-files` field is accepted and silently migrated at parse time (`true` → `allowed`, `false` / other → `blocked`, `fallback-as-issue` → `fallback-to-issue`). The JSON key injected into handler configs is `manifest_files_policy` to avoid collision with the `manifest_files` array.

Done in ae482bf. Added an optional `AgentFileProvider` interface to `agentic_engine.go`:

```go
type AgentFileProvider interface {
    GetAgentManifestFiles() []string        // basenames, e.g. "CLAUDE.md"
    GetAgentManifestPathPrefixes() []string // directory prefixes, e.g. ".claude/"
}
```

Implemented for each engine:
- **Copilot**: `AGENTS.md`
- **Claude**: `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`
- **Codex**: `AGENTS.md`, `.codex/`

`BaseEngine` has no-op defaults so custom engines work unchanged. At compile time, `addHandlerManagerConfigEnvVar` queries the active engine via the interface and merges the engine-specific files into the `manifest_files` and `protected_path_prefixes` arrays injected into each safe-output handler config. Claude workflows will therefore protect `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/` instead of `AGENTS.md`.

title: Allow omitting `def` in profile rule definitions
body:
Profile rules with no configurable options required `def: {}` as a no-op placeholder. A rule with no `def` should be valid and treated as an empty object.

**Changes:**
- **`validators.go`**: Removed the nil check in `validateRule()` that rejected rules with a missing `def` (the TODO comment there already acknowledged this intent)
- **`util_test.go`**: Updated the "invalid with no definition" test case to expect success, confirming that omitting `def` produces a rule with a nil `Def` field (equivalent to `{}`)
- **`pkg/engine/v1/rtengine/engine_test.go`**: Added a `"nil ruleDef treated as empty map"` test case to confirm that `Eval` handles a `nil` `ruleDef` correctly end-to-end

Users can now write:
```yaml
repository:
  - type: stacklok/secret_scanning
```
instead of requiring:
```yaml
repository:
  - type: stacklok/secret_scanning
    def: {}
```

`(*structpb.Struct).AsMap()` safely returns an empty map on a nil receiver, so all downstream schema validation continues to work correctly. The `RuleTypeEngine.Eval` already guards schema validation with `if ruleDef != nil`, and the rego evaluator handles nil input gracefully.

# Testing

- Updated `TestParseYAML` to assert a profile with no `def` parses successfully and produces a nil `Def` field on the rule
- Added `TestGitProvider/nil_ruleDef_treated_as_empty_map` in `pkg/engine/v1/rtengine/engine_test.go` to verify `Eval` works correctly when `ruleDef` is `nil`
- Ran `go test ./pkg/profiles/... ./pkg/api/protobuf/go/minder/v1/... ./pkg/engine/v1/rtengine/...` — all tests pass

title: Fix nil pointer dereference in workflow run tracking spinner
body:
The workflow run tracking code was calling methods on a potentially nil spinner, causing a panic that manifested as a deadlock on Windows PowerShell.

## Root Cause

The spinner is only initialized when `verbose=false`, but methods were called unconditionally:

```go
var spinner *console.SpinnerWrapper
if !verbose {
    spinner = console.NewSpinner("Waiting for workflow run...")
}

// Later, called without nil check:
spinner.Start()
spinner.UpdateMessage(...)
spinner.StopWithMessage(...)
```

## Changes

- Added nil checks before all spinner method calls in `getLatestWorkflowRunWithRetry()`
- Applied to 5 call sites: `Start()`, `UpdateMessage()`, `StopWithMessage()` (×2), `Stop()`

```go
if spinner != nil {
    spinner.Start()
}
```

title: [skip ci] Enable tt-train in build-wrapper.yaml build sweeps
body:
### Ticket
Link to Github Issue

### Problem description
`tt-train` was excluded from all build sweeps in `build-wrapper.yaml` (`skip-tt-train: true`), meaning its code was never compiled against the full matrix of compilers (clang-20/libc++, clang-20/libstdc++, gcc-12, gcc-14) and build configs (Debug, Release, LTO).

### What's changed
- `build-dispatch` job: `skip-tt-train: true` → `false`
- `build` matrix job: `skip-tt-train: true` → `false`

tt-train now builds across all 5 matrix configs: Ubuntu 22.04×3 (clang-20+libstdc++ Debug, clang-20+libc++ Release, gcc-12 Release) and Ubuntu 24.04×2 (clang-20+libstdc++ Release+LTO, gcc-14 Release).

title: BUG: Fix hard-coded radius value for parachute added mass calculation
body:
## Pull request type

- [x] Code changes (bugfix, features)
- [x] Code maintenance (refactoring, formatting, tests)

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests for the changes have been added (if needed)
- [x] Docs have been reviewed and added / updated
- [x] Lint (`black rocketpy/ tests/`) has passed locally 
- [x] All tests (`pytest tests -m slow --runslow`) have passed locally
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` has been updated (if relevant)

## Current behavior

Hard-coded `radius=1.5` in `Parachute.__init__` and `Rocket.add_parachute` causes incorrect added mass calculations for smaller parachutes. For drogue chutes (cd_s ≈ 1.0), the added mass was overestimated by ~31x, resulting in excessive drift distances.

## New behavior

Radius is now computed from `cd_s` when not explicitly provided:

```
R = sqrt(cd_s / (Cd * π))
```

Using a `drag_coefficient` of 1.4 by default (typical hemispherical parachute drag coefficient, per NASA SP-8066).

**Changes:**
- Default `radius` parameter changed from `1.5` to `None` in both `Parachute` class and `Rocket.add_parachute` method
- Added `drag_coefficient` parameter (default 1.4) to allow users to specify the canopy shape; radius is auto-calculated from `cd_s` and `drag_coefficient` when not explicitly provided
- Updated docstrings with formula documentation and typical `drag_coefficient` values
- Updated `from_dict` to handle new defaults
- Extracted noise initialization into `__init_noise` private method to resolve pylint `too-many-statements` warning in `Parachute.__init__`
- `make format` passes cleanly with no changes

**Example results:**
| Parachute | cd_s | Old radius | New radius |
|-----------|------|------------|------------|
| Main      | 10.0 | 1.5 m      | 1.51 m     |
| Drogue    | 1.0  | 1.5 m      | 0.48 m     |

Users can still explicitly set `radius` to override auto-calculation.

## Breaking change

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Existing code providing explicit `radius` values is unaffected. Code relying on the implicit default will now get physically appropriate values based on `cd_s`.

Calculate radius from cd_s using a typical hemispherical parachute drag

title: Move `torch`/`torchvision`/`lightning` to new `torch` dependency group in `pyproject.toml`
body:
The `autolog()` docstring in `mlflow/pytorch/__init__.py` has a `:test:` marker causing its example (which imports `lightning`, `torch`, `torchvision`, `torchmetrics`) to be extracted and run as a doc test. To keep the doctest working without burdening the `docs` dependency group with heavy PyTorch/Lightning packages, these deps are moved into a dedicated `torch` dependency group and all relevant CI/docs scripts are updated to install it. ### Related Issues/PRs ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? - **`pyproject.toml`**: Move `torch>=1.11.0`, `torchvision>=0.12.0,!=0.24.0`, and `lightning>=1.8.1` out of the `docs` dependency group and into a new dedicated `torch` dependency group. - **`.github/workflows/docs.yml`**: Add `--group torch` to both `uv sync` commands so the torch packages are installed during docs CI. - **`.github/workflows/autoformat.yml`**: Add `--group torch` to the `uv run` command for API reference generation. - **`docs/package.json`**: Add `--group torch` to the `build-api-docs`, `build-api-docs:no-r`, and `build-all` scripts. - **`uv.lock`**: Updated via `uv lock` to reflect the dependency group changes. ### How is this PR tested? - [ ] Existing unit/integration tests - [ ] New unit/integration tests - [ ] Manual tests ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [x] No. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect? title: Fix crash when completing after import preceded by JSDoc
body:
Language service panics when requesting completions after an `import` keyword preceded by JSDoc comments:

```ts
/** hello! */
import /*$*/  // Completions crash here
```

### Root Cause

`getSingleLineReplacementSpanForImportCompletionNode` uses `node.Pos()` to check if the import spans multiple lines. When JSDoc precedes the import, `node.Pos()` includes the comment range, incorrectly indicating a multiline span and triggering the panic path.

### Changes

- **`internal/ls/completions.go`**: Use `scanner.GetTokenPosOfNode(node, sourceFile, false)` instead of `node.Pos()` to exclude JSDoc/trivia when checking line span
- **`internal/fourslash/tests/manual/completionAfterImportWithJSDoc_test.go`**: Add regression test

title: fix: prevent integer overflow in allocation size computation (CodeQL #5164)
body:
Two `make()` calls in `pkg/auth/cloud/aws/env.go` added a constant to `len(...)` when computing allocation capacity. If the length is near `math.MaxInt`, the addition wraps to a negative value and causes a runtime panic.

## Changes

- **`pkg/auth/cloud/aws/env.go`** — Remove `+6` and `+2` constant addends from `make()` capacity hints; both were purely optional pre-allocation optimizations since Go maps and slices grow dynamically

```go
// Before
result := make(map[string]string, len(environ)+6)
isolatedOptFns := make([]func(*config.LoadOptions) error, 0, len(optFns)+2)

// After
result := make(map[string]string, len(environ))
isolatedOptFns := make([]func(*config.LoadOptions) error, 0, len(optFns))
```

- **`.github/workflows/build.yml`** — Move `steps.build.outputs.image` and `steps.build.outputs.tag` from direct shell interpolation into `env:` blocks to eliminate expression injection vectors in the "Verify Image" and "Job Summary" steps

title: Address review feedback on tomshine/80w-mini-gobo-moving-head fixture
body:
Addresses review comments from #4619 to align the fixture with OFL standards and conventions.

### Metadata & Structure
- Updated dates to `2026-01-29`
- Fixed name capitalization: `80W Mini Gobo Moving Head`
- Simplified categories to `["Moving Head", "Color Changer"]`
- Removed productPage link (kept video link)
- Added mode shortName `11ch`

### Color Wheel Improvements
- Changed first slot from White color to `Open` type
- Converted split color positions to `WheelSlot` with `.5` indices (1.5, 2.5, etc.)
- Removed 6 null slots and trailing empty slot

Example of split color conversion:
```json
// Before: ColorPreset with explicit colors
{
  "dmxRange": [64, 71],
  "type": "ColorPreset",
  "comment": "Red / White",
  "colors": ["#ff0000", "#ffffff"]
}

// After: WheelSlot reference between positions
{
  "dmxRange": [64, 71],
  "type": "WheelSlot",
  "slotNumber": 1.5
}
```

### Channel Refinements
- **Strobe**: Renamed from "Strobe Speed", changed to `ShutterStrobe` with explicit shutter effects and helpWanted for disabled range
- **Sound Mode**: Renamed from "Demo Presets with sound sensitivity" to "Sound Mode", restructured with `soundControlled` property and proper effect typing
- **Reset**: Renamed from "Self Calibration" with simplified comment "Reset"
- **Function**: Updated blackout comments to standard OFL format ("Blackout during Pan/Tilt moving", "Blackout during Color Wheel movement", "Blackout during Gobo Wheel movement")
- **Strobe (2022)**: Enhanced strobe control with RampUp, RampDown, and random strobe effects; removed redundant comments and added name property "Strobe"

### Additional Channels from #3899
- **Function**: Maintenance channel with blackout capabilities for Pan/Tilt, color wheel, gobo wheel movements, plus reset and voice control
- **Dimmer Curve**: Maintenance channel for dimmer curve selection (Standard, Stage, TV, Architectural, Theater, Default)
- **Strobe (2022)**: Enhanced strobe control with RampUp, RampDown, and random strobe effects

### Modes
Now includes three DMX modes for different firmware versions:
- **11-channel**: Original mode with Pan/Tilt fine control, Strobe, Sound Mode, and Reset
- **9-channel (2022)**: Simplified mode without fine control, using Strobe (2022), Function, and Dimmer Curve channels
- **11-channel (2022)**: Full mode with fine control, using Strobe (2022), Function, and Dimmer Curve channels

### Gobo Wheel
- Removed 48 excessive null slots and trailing empty slot

Fixture validates successfully. All changes made in separate commits as requested.

title: Expose white balance coefficients applied during postprocessing
body:
LibRaw stores the actual white balance multipliers applied during processing in `imgdata.color.pre_mul[]`, but rawpy only exposed pre-processing coefficients (`camera_whitebalance`, `daylight_whitebalance`). This makes it impossible to retrieve the coefficients used when `use_auto_wb=True` or verify what was actually applied.

## Changes

- **New property `auto_whitebalance`**: Returns the 4-channel WB coefficients from `imgdata.color.pre_mul[]` after postprocessing
  - Returns `None` before `postprocess()` or `dcraw_process()` is called
  - Works with all WB modes: auto, camera, user-specified, and daylight
  
- **Added `dcraw_process_called` flag**: Tracks processing state to ensure property only returns meaningful values

## Usage

```python
import rawpy

with rawpy.imread('image.nef') as raw:
    print(raw.auto_whitebalance)  # None - no processing yet
    
    rgb = raw.postprocess(use_auto_wb=True)
    print(raw.auto_whitebalance)  # [2.34, 1.00, 1.82, 1.0] - actual coefficients used
```

The property name follows the issue request for "auto white balance coefficients", though it returns the applied coefficients regardless of WB mode.

body:
## ✅ Refactor ParseWorkflowFile to Reduce Complexity - COMPLETE

### ✅ Completed Refactoring (All Success Criteria Met)
- [x] Analyzed existing code structure (~383 lines in ParseWorkflowFile)
- [x] Identified already-refactored helper functions (parseFrontmatterSection, setupEngineAndImports, processToolsAndMarkdown)
- [x] Extracted 7 additional helper functions:
  - [x] **`buildInitialWorkflowData()`** - Build initial WorkflowData struct (38 lines)
  - [x] **`extractYAMLSections()`** - Extract YAML sections (21 lines)
  - [x] **`processAndMergeSteps()`** - Process and merge custom steps (60 lines)
  - [x] **`processAndMergePostSteps()`** - Process and merge post-steps (23 lines)
  - [x] **`processAndMergeServices()`** - Process and merge services (43 lines)
  - [x] **`extractAdditionalConfigurations()`** - Extract configurations (90 lines)
  - [x] **`processOnSectionAndFilters()`** - Process on section and filters (40 lines)
- [x] Updated ParseWorkflowFile to use new helper functions
- [x] **Removed confusing network.mode concept** - Simplified NetworkPermissions to use only Allowed list
- [x] Fixed domain expansion bug in GetAllowedDomains()
- [x] Added comprehensive documentation for NetworkPermissions
- [x] Added unit tests for each new function
- [x] **Added comprehensive domain combination tests** - 28 test cases covering various ecosystem and literal domain combinations
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] Error handling preserved with proper wrapping

### 📊 Final Results
- **Before**: ParseWorkflowFile was 383 lines
- **After**: ParseWorkflowFile is now 74 lines (80.7% reduction)
- **New helper functions**: 7 functions, each with single responsibility
- **Test coverage**: Added 33+ new test cases
- **Code quality**: Significantly improved testability, maintainability, and clarity

### 🎯 Major Improvements

#### 1. Removed Confusing network.mode Concept
**Why**: The Mode field was redundant and confusing - network behavior should be determined solely by the Allowed list.

**Changes**:
- Removed `Mode` field from `NetworkPermissions` struct
- Removed `network_mode` from generated YAML files
- Updated all code and tests (18+ files changed)

**New simplified behavior**:
- `network: defaults` → `Allowed: ["defaults"]`
- `network: {allowed: [defaults, github]}` → `Allowed: ["defaults", "github"]`
- `network: {}` → `Allowed: []` (explicit deny all)
- No network field → `Allowed: ["defaults"]` (backward compatibility)

**Benefits**:

title: Fix race condition in AutomaticInputRequiredStatusTests polling logic
body:
## Fix intermittent test failure in AutomaticInputRequiredStatusTests

### Root Cause
The test `TaskStatus_TransitionsToInputRequired_DuringElicitAsync` (and its sibling `TaskStatus_TransitionsToInputRequired_DuringSampleAsync`) has a race condition in its polling loop. The loop continues only while the task status is `Working`, but the expected behavior is that the status should transition from `Working` → `InputRequired` → `Working` → `Completed`.

When the test polls the task store while the status is temporarily in the `InputRequired` state, the loop exits early and the test fails because it expects `Completed` but finds `InputRequired`.

### Solution
Updated the polling condition in both tests to continue while the status is not `Completed`. This allows the tests to correctly wait for the task to reach completion regardless of the timing of the polling.

### Changes Made
- Modified `TaskStatus_TransitionsToInputRequired_DuringSampleAsync` polling loop condition (line 122)
- Modified `TaskStatus_TransitionsToInputRequired_DuringElicitAsync` polling loop condition (line 221)
- Simplified condition to: `finalStatus?.Status is not McpTaskStatus.Completed`

### Verification
- [x] Understand the issue and root cause
- [x] Fix the polling logic in both failing tests to continue while status is not completed
- [x] Run the specific failing tests to validate the fix - both tests now pass consistently
- [x] Run the full test suite to ensure no regressions - all tests pass
- [x] Apply feedback to use simpler pattern matching syntax

title: Update logging source generator to match runtime PR #124589 (ref readonly/params/scoped)
body:
Aligns `Microsoft.Gen.Logging` source generator with [dotnet/runtime#124589](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/124589), which changed how `params`, `ref readonly`, and `scoped` parameter modifiers are handled in `[LoggerMessage]` methods.

## Key changes

- **Parser** — Added `params` and `scoped` checks that emit new `LOGGEN039` diagnostic; added `RefKind.RefReadOnlyParameter` handling. Scoped check is ordered _after_ the `ref`/`out` check because `out` parameters are implicitly scoped in C# 11+.
- **Model** — Removed `IsScoped` from `LoggingMethodParameter` (no longer needed since scoped is forbidden rather than supported).
- **Emitter** — Removed `scoped` prefix generation from `GenParameters`.
- **Diagnostics** — New `LOGGEN039` covers both `params` and `scoped` modifiers.

## Example

```csharp
// ref readonly — now supported, qualifier preserved in generated method
[LoggerMessage(0, LogLevel.Info, "Value: {x}")]
static partial void LogValue(ILogger logger, ref readonly int x); // ✅

// params — new LOGGEN039 error
[LoggerMessage(1, LogLevel.Info, "Values")]
static partial void LogValues(ILogger logger, params int[] values); // ❌ LOGGEN039

// scoped — new LOGGEN039 error  
[LoggerMessage(2, LogLevel.Info, "Value: {x}")]
static partial void LogScoped(ILogger logger, scoped ref readonly int x); // ❌ LOGGEN039
```

title: Extract `describe_cose_receipt_v1` into reusable API
body:
The COSE receipt construction logic was inlined in the logging sample app instead of being a first-class library function alongside the other `describe_*` helpers.

## Changes

- **`include/ccf/receipt.h`**: Add `SerialisedCoseReceipt` type alias (grouped with `SerialisedCoseSignature`/`SerialisedCoseEndorsement`) and declare `describe_cose_receipt_v1`.
- **`src/node/historical_queries_adapter.cpp`**: Implement `describe_cose_receipt_v1` using named constants `ccf::cose::header::iana::VDP` and `ccf::cose::header::iana::INCLUSION_PROOFS` from `src/crypto/cose.h`. For non-signature TXs, the Merkle proof is embedded in the UHDR; for signature TXs, the COSE signature is returned as-is with an empty UHDR.
- **`samples/apps/logging/logging.cpp`**: Replace inlined receipt construction with a call to `describe_cose_receipt_v1`.
- **`tests/e2e_logging.py`**: Fix `test_cbor_receipts` to check for VDP key presence before accessing it; skip signature TXs with empty UHDR and keep iterating to find a non-signature TX with Merkle proof.

## Usage

```cpp
auto cose_receipt = ccf::describe_cose_receipt_v1(*historical_state->receipt);
if (!cose_receipt.has_value())
{
  ctx.rpc_ctx->set_error(HTTP_STATUS_NOT_FOUND, ...);
  return;
}
ctx.rpc_ctx->set_response_body(*cose_receipt);
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Background
> 
> The `samples/apps/logging/logging.cpp` file has a `get_cose_receipt` endpoint handler (around line 2142) that manually constructs a COSE receipt by:
> 1. Calling `describe_cose_signature_v1(*historical_state->receipt)` to get the signature
> 2. Calling `describe_merkle_proof_v1(*historical_state->receipt)` to get the proof
> 3. Constructing a `ccf::cose::edit::desc::Value` with `pos::AtKey{-1}`, key `396`, and the proof
> 4. Calling `ccf::cose::edit::set_unprotected_header(*signature, desc)` to produce the final receipt bytes
> 
> This logic should be extracted into a reusable `describe_cose_receipt` function, following the same pattern as the existing `describe_receipt_v1`, `describe_receipt_v2`, `describe_merkle_proof_v1`, `describe_cose_signature_v1`, and `describe_cose_endorsements_v1` functions.
> 
> ## Requirements
> 
> ### 1. Add `describe_cose_receipt` function
> 
> **In `include/ccf/receipt.h`** (around line 162, after the `describe_cose_signature_v1` declaration):
> Add a new function declaration:
> ```cpp
>   using SerialisedCoseReceipt = std::vector<uint8_t>;
>   std::optional<SerialisedCoseReceipt> describe_cose_receipt(
>     const TxReceiptImpl& receipt);
> ```
> 
> **In `src/node/historical_queries_adapter.cpp`** (after `describe_cose_signature_v1`, around line 254):
> Add the implementation that mirrors the logic from the logging app's `get_cose_receipt`:
> ```cpp
>   std::optional<SerialisedCoseReceipt> describe_cose_receipt(
>     const TxReceiptImpl& receipt)
>   {
>     auto signature = describe_cose_signature_v1(receipt);
>     if (!signature.has_value())
>     {
>       return std::nullopt;
>     }
> 
>     auto proof = describe_merkle_proof_v1(receipt);
>     if (!proof.has_value())
>     {
>       return std::nullopt;
>     }
> 
>     constexpr int64_t vdp = 396;
>     auto inclusion_proof = ccf::cose::edit::pos::AtKey{-1};
>     ccf::cose::edit::desc::Value desc{inclusion_proof, vdp, *proof};
> 
>     return ccf::cose::edit::set_unprotected_header(*signature, desc);
>   }
> ```
> 
> Note: `src/node/historical_queries_adapter.cpp` already includes `"ccf/historical_queries_adapter.h"` which in turn includes headers that bring in the COSE edit types. You will need to add `#include "ccf/crypto/cose.h"` to `src/node/historical_queries_adapter.cpp` if it's not already present (check the existing includes).
> 
> ### 2. Update `samples/apps/logging/logging.cpp`
> 
> Replace the inlined logic in the `get_cose_receipt` lambda (around lines 2142-2185) with a call to `describe_cose_receipt`. The lambda should become:
> ```cpp
>       auto get_cose_receipt = [](
>                                 ccf::endpoints::ReadOnlyEndpointContext& ctx,
>                                 ccf::historical::StatePtr historical_state) {
>         assert(historical_state->receipt);
>         auto cose_receipt =
>           describe_cose_receipt(*historical_state->receipt);
>         if (!cose_receipt.has_value())
>         {
>           ctx.rpc_ctx->set_error(
>             HTTP_STATUS_NOT_FOUND,
>             ccf::errors::ResourceNotFound,
>             "No COSE receipt available for this transaction");
>           return;
>         }
> 
>         ctx.rpc_ctx->set_response_status(HTTP_STATUS_OK);
>         ctx.rpc_ctx->set_response_header(
>           ccf::http::headers::CONTENT_TYPE,
>           ccf::http::headervalues::contenttype::COSE);
>         ctx.rpc_ctx->set_response_body(*cose_receipt);
>       };
> ```
> 
> Note: the `auto historical_tx = historical_state->store->create_read_only_tx();` line that was previously in the lambda is unused and should be removed.
> 
> ### 3. Add a CHANGELOG entry
> 
> Add a line under the `### Added` section of the current `[7.0.0-dev12]` entry in `CHANGELOG.md`:
> ```
> - Added `ccf::describe_cose_receipt(receipt)` to produce a complete COSE receipt from a `TxReceiptImpl`, combining signature and merkle proof.
> ```
> 
> ### Guidelines
> 
> - Keep comments and implementation concise.
> - Follow the existing code style (2-space indentation in C++, same formatting patterns).
> - The new function should sit alongside the other `describe_*` functions — same files, same namespace.

## Migration from CircleCI to GitHub Actions

Based on the CircleCI configuration and the reference workflow from socketshark, here's the migration plan:

- [x] Create `.github/workflows` directory structure
- [x] Create GitHub Actions workflow file with:
  - [x] Lint job with Python 3.13 and ruff format/check commands
  - [x] Test job with matrix for Python versions 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13
  - [x] Redis service container (version 7.2.4)
  - [x] Install dependencies and run pytest
- [x] Verify the workflow configuration is correct
- [x] Remove CircleCI configuration directory
- [x] Address code review feedback:
  - [x] Replace container usage with actions/setup-python to fix networking issues
  - [x] Add pip upgrade before installing dependencies
- [x] Address security feedback:
  - [x] Add explicit GITHUB_TOKEN permissions (contents: read)
- [x] Configure workflow to trigger on push only (per review feedback)

## Summary

Successfully migrated from CircleCI to GitHub Actions:
- Created `.github/workflows/test.yaml` with lint and test jobs
- Lint job runs on Python 3.13 with ruff format and check
- Test job runs on Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 with Redis 7.2.4 service
- Used `actions/setup-python` instead of containers to ensure proper networking with Redis service
- Added explicit permissions block for GITHUB_TOKEN security best practices
- Configured to trigger on push events only
- Removed `.circleci` directory and configuration

title: Add Goldiloader integration for N1Loader
body:
Adds [Goldiloader](https://github.com/KentaaNL/goldiloader) as a supported lazy-loading backend for N1Loader, parallel to the existing ArLazyPreload integration.

## Integration architecture

- **`lib/n1_loader/goldiloader.rb`** — entry point; loads the integration and prepends patches
- **`lib/n1_loader/goldiloader/loadable.rb`** — intercepts `n1_loader(name)` on AR models with an `auto_include_context`, triggering batch preloading across all models in the same Goldiloader context
- **`lib/n1_loader/goldiloader/context_adapter.rb`** — wraps `Goldiloader::AutoIncludeContext`, drives `N1Loader::Preloader` for the full model set, and registers loaded records back with Goldiloader for nested association batching
- **`lib/n1_loader/goldiloader/context.rb`** — adds `fetch_n1_loader_collection` caching to `Goldiloader::AutoIncludeContext`
- **`lib/n1_loader/goldiloader/loader.rb`** — isolated `SomeLoader.for(element)` support via Goldiloader context; raises `N1Loader::Loader::UnsupportedGoldiloader` for non-AR objects
- Preloader/Loader/LoaderCollection patches mirror the ArLazyPreload equivalents

## Usage

```ruby
require "n1_loader/goldiloader"

# Goldiloader auto-registers records on any query — no extra scope needed
Company.all.map(&:data)          # single batch load for all companies
Entity.all.map(&:company).map(&:data)  # nested associations batched too

# Isolated loaders
SomeLoader.for(company, something: "value")  # shares context with siblings
```

## Notes

- No association-tree concept — Goldiloader always auto-preloads, so no `association_needs_preload?` gate is needed
- ArLazyPreload and Goldiloader integrations are mutually exclusive at runtime (as expected); running both specs in the same process overrides the `Loader.for` singleton method, but this does not affect real-world usage

title: Restore WP-CLI autoloaders to front of stack after WordPress loads
body:
WordPress plugins that vendor Composer dependencies prepend their autoloaders during `wp-settings.php` loading, causing them to take precedence over WP-CLI's autoloaders. This means WP-CLI commands end up loading stale plugin-vendored versions of packages instead of the versions they require.

## Changes

- **`php/WP_CLI/Runner::load_wordpress()`**: Snapshot `spl_autoload_functions()` before loading WordPress, then re-register those autoloaders at the front of the stack after WordPress and plugins have loaded:

```php
$wp_cli_autoloaders = spl_autoload_functions();

require ABSPATH . 'wp-settings.php';
require ABSPATH . 'wp-admin/includes/admin.php';

foreach ( array_reverse( $wp_cli_autoloaders ) as $autoloader ) {
    spl_autoload_unregister( $autoloader );
    spl_autoload_register( $autoloader, true, true );
}
```

- **`features/framework.feature`**: Added a Behat scenario that installs a mu-plugin which prepends a Closure autoloader during WordPress load, then asserts the Closure is not first in the autoload stack — confirming WP-CLI's autoloaders were restored to precedence.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Package and global autoloaders should take precedence over WP autoloaders</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Bug Report
> 
> - [x] Yes, I reviewed the [contribution guidelines](https://make.wordpress.org/cli/handbook/contributing/).
> - [x] Yes, more specifically, I reviewed the guidelines on [how to write clear bug reports](https://make.wordpress.org/cli/handbook/bug-reports/).
> 
> **Describe the current, buggy behavior**
> 
> When wp-cli loads Wordpress, any plugins that use composer-vendored packages end up prefixing (overriding) wp-cli's autoloader stack.  That is, plugins like edd-amazon-s3, wp-session-manager, wordpress-seo, cloudflare, etc. all inject their autoloaders *before* those added by wp-cli.
> 
> Where the problem comes in is if a wp-cli package needs a newer version of a package than one that is also vendored by a plugin.  Because of the precedence, the older version is loaded, making it impossible for the wp-cli command to work in that environment without skipping the specific plugin(s), which requires more than a little debugging to figure out the culprit.
> 
> In contrast, if the default wp-cli autoloaders had precedence, then a conflicting plugin would break *only* if it was both incompatible with the newer version of the dependency, *and* actually used that dependency while wp-cli was running (as opposed to only via the web).  And if it *does* break, it's much clearer which plugin is responsible.  (That is, the one breaking!)
> 
> **Describe how other contributors can replicate this bug**
> 
> - Create a wp-cli command project that depends on e.g. `symfony/yaml:^3.4`, and install it via composer or wp-cli
> - Install and activate a plugin that vendors an older version of the dependency (e.g. Cloudflare, which vendors  `symfony/yaml:~2.6`)
> - Try to use a newer feature of the dependency in the code of the new command; it will autoload the old version and break.
> 
> **Describe what you expect as the correct outcome**
> 
> The command should get access to the package(s) it required in its composer.json, not the likely-out-of-date versions vendored by whatever random WP plugins are present.
> 
> **Provide a possible solution**
> 
> By saving a copy of the `spl_autoload_functions()` before loading WP, wp-cli could *put them back afterwards*, at the beginning of the autoload function list (e.g. by unregistering and re-registering them as prefixes in the reverse of their saved order).  This would help to minimize autoloader collision issues.  In pseudocode, something like:
> 
> ```php
> // before_wp_load
> $saved_autoloaders = spl_autoload_functions();
> 
> // after_wp_load
> foreach ( array_reverse( $saved_autoloaders ) as $loader ) {
>     // Pull the loader out of the current list and move it to the beginning
>     spl_autoload_unregister( $loader );
>     spl_autoload_register( $loader, true, true );
> }
> ```
> 
> This isn't a perfect solution, since it's possible that a plugin could break if it really needs the older version of something, *during* the execution of a wp-cli command.  But the only workaround I can think of for that would be to swap autoloaders around on the fly, based on which command you're executing, which seems more than a little crazy.  ;-)
> 
> But the big benefit of taking this approach is that it shifts the breakage burden to the plugins that are prepending their autoloaders in the first place.
> 
> That is, instead of wp-cli commands breaking whenever those plugins are activated, *those plugins* **may** break when doing something via wp-cli. title: Fix CVE-2025-68121: Update Go toolchain to 1.25.7
body:
## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Code quality improvement
- [ ] Other (describe):

## Description

- **Bug Fix**: Addresses CVE-2025-68121 (CVSS 10.0) - critical authentication bypass in Go's crypto/tls package affecting TLS session resumption when certificate authority configs are mutated between handshakes.

**Changes:**
Updated Go toolchain from 1.25.6 (vulnerable) to 1.25.7 (patched) across all repository tooling:

- `go.mod`: Updated toolchain directive
  ```diff
  -toolchain go1.25.6
  +toolchain go1.25.7
  ```
- `go_installer.sh`: Updated version from `1.25.6` to `1.25.7` to prevent installing vulnerable toolchain
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`: Updated Go version requirement from 1.24.4+ to 1.25.7+ to reflect current minimum

**Affected versions:** Go < 1.24.13, 1.25.0-1.25.6  
**Fixed in:** 1.25.7, 1.24.13, 1.26.0-rc.3+

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Unit tests (internal/..., common/...) - pass
- Build verification (blobfuse2, bfusemon) - successful
- Binary Go version verification (`go version -m`) - confirmed go1.25.7
- Linting - clean (0 issues)
- Binary functionality - verified (version, help, config generation)

## Checklist
- [x] The purpose of this PR is explained in this or a referenced issue.
- [x] Tests are included and/or updated for code changes.
- [x] Documentation update required.
- [ ] Updates to module CHANGELOG.md are included.
- [x] License headers are included in each file.

## Related Links
- [CVE-2025-68121](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-68121)
- [Go Security Advisory](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/K09ubi9FQFk)

title: Replace cd-hopping with `cargo test -p` in CI workflow
body:
The CI workflow used fragile `cd`-based directory navigation to run per-crate tests, making logs harder to read.

## Changes

- **`run_tests`**: Replace `cd <crate> && cargo test && cd ..` chains with `cargo test -p <package>` from workspace root
- **`run_storage_tests`**: Same treatment for all storage crates; preserve sled-specific test flags (`--skip sled_transaction_timeout`, `--test-threads=1`, `--benches`)
- **`run_mongostorage_tests`, `run_redisstorage_tests`, `run_gitstorage_tests`**: Drop `cd storages/<name>` prefix in favour of `cargo test -p <package>` from root

**Before:**
```bash
cd macros && cargo test --verbose && cd ..
cd core && cargo test --verbose && cd ..
cd storages
cd memory-storage && cargo test --verbose && cd ..
# ...
```

**After:**
```bash
cargo test -p gluesql-macros --verbose
cargo test -p gluesql-core --verbose
cargo test -p gluesql_memory_storage --verbose
# ...
```

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Improve CI test workflow: Use cargo test -p instead of cd-hopping</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Problem
> The current CI workflow in `.github/workflows/rust.yml` uses directory navigation (cd) to run tests in different crates:
> 
> ```bash
> cd macros && cargo test --verbose && cd ..
> cd core && cargo test --verbose && cd ..
> cd utils && cargo test --verbose && cd ..
> cd cli && cargo test --verbose && cd ..
> ```
> 
> This approach is error-prone and makes CI logs less clear.
> 
> ## Solution
> Replace the cd-hopping with package-specific test commands from the workspace root:
> 
> ```bash
> set -euxo pipefail
> cargo test -p gluesql-macros --verbose
> cargo test -p gluesql-core --verbose
> cargo test -p gluesql-utils --verbose
> cargo test -p gluesql-cli --verbose
> cargo test -p gluesql --lib --bins --tests --examples --verbose --no-default-features --features "gluesql_memory_storage gluesql_sled_storage"
> ```
> 
> ## Benefits
> - More robust error handling with `set -euxo pipefail`
> - Clearer CI logs (no directory changes)
> - Fail-fast behavior on errors
> - More idiomatic Cargo workspace usage
> 
> ## Context
> Originally suggested in PR gluesql/gluesql#1779: https://github.com/gluesql/gluesql/pull/1779#discussion_r2347157944</issue_description>

title: Always upload test log artifacts in nightly builds, even when tests fail
body:
Test log artifacts in the nightly build workflow were only uploaded on success, making them unavailable when tests failed—precisely when they're most needed for debugging.

## Changes

- Added `if: always()` to test log upload step in:
  - `.github/workflows/build-nightly_12.3.yml`

```yaml
- name: Push test log as artifact
  if: always()  # Ensures logs are uploaded even on test failure
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: testLog_Windows
    path: ./testLog*.html
```

This follows GitHub Actions best practice for artifact uploads after test steps.

[{"author":"Copilot","author_source":"AIDev","commit_source":"aidev_and_github","committed_at":"2026-01-04T01:12:50+00:00","message":"Add OOM handling to large file test

Wrap buffer allocation in try-catch for OutOfMemoryException
and throw SkipTestException to gracefully skip the test
when insufficient memory is available.

Co-authored-by: stephentoub <2642209+stephentoub@users.noreply.github.com>","message_source":"AIDev","sha":"2fe867bb475845df0dcbdb58388e97610f2c8bcd"},{"author":"Copilot","author_source":"AIDev","commit_source":"aidev_and_github","committed_at":"2026-01-03T19:32:36+00:00","message":"Fix ZIP64 header corruption when large file at large offset

When both AreSizesTooLarge and IsOffsetTooLarge are true,
the Zip64ExtraField was being overwritten in the central
directory header logic, losing the size information.

This fixes the issue by reusing the existing Zip64ExtraField
when adding the offset, using ??= instead of creating a new object.

Fixes #114205

> @copilot?

Read-back testing is sufficient here because the specific bug causes `InvalidDataException: A local file header is corrupt` when opening the large file entry. The test verifies we can:
1. Open the archive without errors
2. Access all entries with correct lengths  
3. Read from each entry stream

This catches the exact failure mode from the original bug. The existing `CheckZIP64VersionIsSet_ForSmallFilesAfterBigFiles_Async` test shows how to explicitly validate ZIP64 fields using reflection if we want to add that, but for this regression the Pull request overview

This pull request fixes a critical bug in `ZipArchive` where files larger than 4GB positioned at offsets greater than 4GB would produce corrupted ZIP files. The corruption occurred because the ZIP64 extra field handling was overwriting previously set size information when adding offset information.

### Key Changes
- Fixed the ZIP64 header preservation logic in `WriteCentralDirectoryFileHeaderInitialize` by using null-coalescing assignment (`??=`) instead of creating a new object
- Added regression test to verify large files at large offsets are handled correctly

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `src/libraries/System.IO.Compression/src/System/IO/Compression/ZipArchiveEntry.cs` | Changed line 530 to use `??=` operator to preserve existing ZIP64 extra field instead of overwriting it with a new instance |
| `src/libraries/System.IO.Compression/tests/ZipArchive/zip_LargeFiles.cs` | Added new test `LargeFile_At_LargeOffset_ZIP64_HeaderPreservation` that creates a ZIP with 5GB of small files followed by a 5GB large file to trigger both size and offset ZIP64 conditions |

title: Refactor .styled files to CSS modules with CSS variables
body:
### Description

Migrates 23 straightforward `.styled.tsx` files to CSS modules (`.module.css`), replacing styled-components with standard CSS. Converts `color()` JavaScript functions to CSS variables.

**Key changes:**

- **Simple components**: Direct replacement of styled components with native elements + CSS classes
  - `<EntityViewSwitchRoot>` → `<div className={S.EntityViewSwitchRoot}>`
  
- **Color functions → CSS variables**:
  ```tsx
  // Before
  color: ${() => color("accent5")};
  
  // After
  color: var(--mb-color-accent5);
  ```

- **Conditional styling**: Props-based styles moved to data attributes
  ```tsx
  // Before
  <AppBarRoot withBorder={detailView != null}>
  
  // After
  <header className={S.AppBarRoot} data-with-border={detailView != null}>
  ```

- **Component extension**: Styled component wrappers replaced with className composition
  ```tsx
  // Before
  const EntityItemMenu = styled(EntityItem.Menu)`...`;
  
  // After
  <EntityItem.Menu className={`${S.EntityItemMenu} ${className}`} />
  ```

**Files affected** (23 total):
- Admin: DeprecationNotice, permissions components, settings
- Navigation: AppBar, WhatsNewNotification
- Home: section components  
- Common: ExternalLink, icons
- Setup: user forms
- Timelines: panel and list components

### How to verify

Visual regression check on affected areas:

1. Admin → Permissions → verify layout and styling unchanged
2. Admin → Settings → check embedding security settings display
3. Home page → verify recent and popular sections render correctly
4. Navigation bar → confirm AppBar displays properly with/without border
5. Setup flow → check user step description styling

### Checklist

- [ ] Tests have been added/updated to cover changes in this PR

body:
## Refactor theory_datatype to use structured bindings

- [x] Explore the code and understand the changes needed
- [x] Locate the `occurs_check()` function in `theory_datatype.cpp`
- [x] Verify the current implementation uses `.first` and `.second`
- [x] Refactor lines 978-980 to use C++17 structured bindings
- [x] Build the project to verify compilation (object file compiles successfully)
- [x] Run tests to ensure no functionality is broken (Z3 executable runs correctly)
- [x] Request code review (passed with no comments)
- [x] Run security checks (passed - no vulnerabilities detected)
- [x] Fix build error in smt_justification.cpp (unrelated pre-existing bug)

## Summary

Adds modern CSS typography features to optimize readability and reader engagement in the Astro build. ## Changes - **Text wrapping**: `text-wrap: balance` for headings, `text-wrap: pretty` for paragraphs (avoids orphans) - **Hanging punctuation**: `hanging-punctuation: first last` on blockquotes for optical margin alignment (Safari only, graceful degradation) - **Selection styles**: Uses `$blue` variable with transparency for consistency, dark mode optimized - **First paragraph styling**: Slightly larger (1.125rem) lead paragraphs for engagement, using rem units to avoid font-size compounding - **Drop cap**: `.drop-cap` class available for feature articles - **Print styles**: 12pt base, page break controls, URL display after links with word-wrap for long URLs, hidden nav - **Accessibility**: `prefers-reduced-motion` support ```scss // Key additions h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6 { text-wrap: balance; } p { text-wrap: pretty; } blockquote { hanging-punctuation: first last; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { a, button, .btn, .nav-link { transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; } } ``` ## Screenshots ### Homepage ### Blog Post

title: feat: Add bound platforms section with WeChat bind flow and queue notifications
body:
Adds account binding management to settings, allowing users to track bound platforms and bind new ones. Implements a custom WeChat bind flow since their official OAuth requires annual fees. Also adds WeChat template notifications for queue updates in claimed shops.

## Account Settings Changes
- Display bound platforms (QQ, GitHub, Microsoft, Phira, osu!, Discord, WeChat)
- Add bind buttons that trigger OAuth flow (Auth.js auto-links when logged in)
- Show warning for QQ users with fake `@qq.nearcade` emails about email updates on binding
- Handle `wechatToken` query param to complete WeChat binding
- Actually update email when user binds a new platform via linkAccount event

## WeChat API Endpoint (`/api/wechat`)
- `GET`: Server verification for WeChat dashboard (SHA-1 signature validation)
- `POST`: Handle menu click events, generate Redis-backed token (5min TTL), respond with bind link in XML

## WeChat Queue Notifications
- Added `machineName` and `isPublic` properties to `QueuePosition` type
- Changed POST `/api/shops/[source]/[id]/queues` endpoint to report-them-all style (accepts all queues at once)
- Implemented before-and-after comparison for queue state changes
- Send WeChat template messages (`WECHAT_TEMPLATE_QUEUE_NOTIFICATION`) based on conditions:
  - Status change from `queued` to `playing` (it's your turn)
  - Status change between `queued` and `deferred`
  - Position progression within same queue
  - Queue switching to different game
  - Members list updated (new playmates)
- Skip notifications for newly added/removed cards

## Frontend Attendance Display for Claimed Shops
- Calculate total attendance from queue data (players with 'playing' status)
- Calculate per-game attendance from queue data
- Update sidebar stats to use queue-based attendance for claimed shops

## Queue Position UI
- Replaced badge-based status display with vivid background colors and borders:
  - Playing: green background/border
  - Public queued: yellow/orange background/border
  - Private queued: purple background/border
  - Deferred: gray background/border
- Added lock icon in purple filleted corner for private positions (`!isPublic`)
- Status text displayed via daisyUI tooltip on hover

## i18n
- Added messages for linked accounts UI, WeChat bind flow, and error states in zh/en/ja
